data.title: Test Results for AMD Zen 5
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AMD处理器的性能、架构设计及其与竞争产品的对比

不同观点：
• **pbsd** 提到，根据AMD Zen 5优化手册，浮点调度器在满载时会有慢速区域，但在特定条件下（如依赖1周期延迟的操作）可能不会受到惩罚。因此，短向量代码在未填满调度器时会有更好的延迟表现。这与通常认为的向量ALU指令延迟为2及更高有所不同。

• **monster_truck** 支持pbsd的观点，认为在充分利用各种优化后，AMD Zen各代处理器仍有剩余的计算能力。他建议使用较少核心以平衡热负载，从而获得更快的性能。

• **kvemkon** 比较了AMD和Apple的处理器，指出即使在缓存大小相似的情况下，AMD在单线程性能上仍有差距。他还提到，与Qualcomm和ARM的处理器相比，AMD需要到Zen 6才能有较大提升。

• **eigenform** 对Zen 3缺少内存重命名但在Zen 4和Zen 5中恢复的现象表示好奇，提出了技术演进的问题。

• **qwertox** 提供了一份关于Intel、AMD和VIA CPU微架构的优化指南链接，供大家参考。

• **kklisura** 询问如何获取所有这些处理器信息，表现出对学习资源的兴趣。

• **ashvardanian** 批评了AMD在AI方面宣传的误导性，指出Zen5与Intel Xeon处理器的实际对比，并怀疑AVX-512支持和核心数量是否足以竞争。

补充讨论：
• **Sesse__, varispeed, alberth, londons_explore** 提供了其他角度的评论，如对测试结果的期待、M4处理器的比较、文章标题的准确性，以及对整数向量指令使用场景的幽默看法。

争议焦点：
• AMD Zen处理器在实际应用中的延迟表现与其文档说明是否一致，以及AMD在市场宣传中是否存在误导。

data.title: Low cost mmWave 60GHz radar sensor for advanced sensing
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了BGT60TR13C雷达传感器的主要特性及其应用。该传感器工作在60GHz频段，内置天线，采用Finite-State Machine（FSM）管理频率调制和数据采集，通过SPI接口进行配置和控制。其特点包括高信噪比、高带宽、低功耗以及小尺寸（6.5 x 5.0 x 0.9 mm³）。应用场景广泛，涵盖消费电子、无人机、智能家居、安防系统和智能温控等领域。此外，文中还提供了技术支持和设计资源的获取途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：毫米波雷达传感器的技术特性、应用场景及其局限性

不同观点：
• Animats认为该设备为爱好者提供了丰富的功能，如蓝牙、WiFi连接和Android应用，且兼容一些Adafruit产品，这在IC数据表中不常见。然而，其角度分辨率为20度，距离分辨率为1米，且只能检测固定物体，范围仅10米。对于只需简单动作检测的场景（如开灯），有更便宜的微波探测器可选。

• Catbert59提到中国Hi-Link提供的50GHz到60GHz的雷达模块，价格在10-30€，易于在固件和PCB层面进行逆向工程。其中一些是连续波雷达，少数是FMCW雷达，使用Infineon 60GHz雷达芯片，且无需签署NDA即可获取工具和数据表。此外，提到ICLink的ICL1122/ICL1112雷达IC，价格约10€，但数据表难找。

• Scoreandmore分享了使用KIT-CSK-BGT60TR13C制作汽车检测器的经验，认为该设备配置简单且有趣，但发现类似创意早已存在。

• Liftyee对传感器技术的进步感到惊讶，特别是使用新后向散射检测机制的空气尘埃传感器，且价格合理。

• Transpute提供了与毫米波雷达相关的多篇文章链接，供进一步阅读。

• Tamimio认为该设备的探测范围有限，不适合其项目需求。

• Yehat考虑使用毫米波传感器检测雨雪雾，但发现许多传感器专为特定应用设计，难以广泛应用。

• Actinium226提到多家公司尝试在智能手机中应用毫米波雷达，但尚未找到合适的用途。

• Progbits尝试使用60GHz模块构建睡眠追踪器，但数据不准确，考虑是否因技术发展后值得再试。

• Chasd00建议将雷达用于RC飞机的障碍物回避，结合自动驾驶仪。

• Reflexe提到将芯片与波束成形器结合，可实现相控阵雷达，且认为15美元的价格对于此类芯片不算便宜。

• Amelius好奇该芯片能否用于穿墙监控或地震后生命探测。

• Rebelgecko期待该设备能与Home Assistant即插即用。

• Therein指出该设备的谐波频率为氧气的谐振频率，虽然功率水平低，但值得注意。

• Transcriptase幽默地提到如何利用该技术收集数据用于广告 targeting。

补充讨论：
- 毫米波雷达在消费电子和物联网中的应用潜力及技术限制。
- 不同用户对价格、功能和应用场景的看法存在差异。
- 数据表和工具的获取难度及对项目开发的影响。

data.title: Fast and cheap bulk storage: using LVM to cache HDDs on SSDs
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何利用Linux的逻辑卷管理器（LVM）构建一个缓存的RAID阵列，结合SSD和HDD以实现高性价比的存储方案。SSD用于加速频繁访问数据的读取，而大容量的HDD用于存储不常访问的数据。作者选择LVM缓存而不是ZFS或其他工具，因为LVM配置简单且兼容性好。HDD部分采用RAID 1以提高数据可靠性，防止磁盘故障导致数据丢失。文章详细介绍了硬件设置、RAID 1配置、缓存分区创建及逻辑卷管理的具体步骤，并讨论了该方案的优势和注意事项。通过这种方式，用户可以在享受SSD高速性能的同时，利用HDD的大容量存储。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LVM及其相关技术（RAID、缓存、精简配置等）的使用经验和优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持LVM的灵活性与功能**：
  - dale_glass认为LVM非常灵活，具备RAID、迁移、完整性检查、缓存、快照、精简配置等多种功能，推荐将所有设备放入同一个卷组（VG）以充分利用LVM的灵活性。
  - iam-TJ也支持LVM的RAID功能，指出LVM可以按逻辑卷（LV）进行定制，包括缓存、镜像等，且支持实时扩展，非常灵活。
  
• **对精简配置（thin provisioning）的警告**：
  - dale_glass警告不要轻易使用精简配置，因为其性能影响显著，且在数据故障时可能会导致问题。
  
• **对缓存功能的讨论**：
  - gopalv指出缓存的性能提升取决于访问模式，并分享了使用ext4外部日志和将SSD用于缓存的成功经验，但也提到SSD故障可能导致数据丢失的风险。
  - jpecar对LVM缓存持负面态度，认为其早期版本像一个黑盒，无法根据工作负载调整，最终选择了全闪存方案。

• **RAID和数据损坏问题**：
  - Szpadel提醒RAID1仅在磁盘完全损坏时提供保护，但在数据损坏时可能会导致双磁盘数据损坏，而像ZFS或Btrfs这样的文件系统具备校验功能，能更好地处理这种问题。

• **对LVM和MDADM的批评**：
  - KaiserPro对LVM和MDADM持负面态度，认为早期文档不足，且LVM快照曾经不实用，推荐ZFS或GPFS。

• **对其他技术的提及**：
  - riedel询问QNAP NAS的分层技术，认为灵活的分层比缓存更适合普通用户。
  - rsync提到ZFS的元数据缓存设备可以大幅提升IOPS，但警告如果丢失元数据设备会导致数据池丢失。
  
• **其他实现细节和建议**：
  - oakwhiz分享了设置LVM RAID5的经验，指出设置过程复杂，但运行良好。
  - Padriac强调RAID需要监控和告警，以避免潜在问题。
  - whazor建议使用写回缓存以提高写入速度。
  - hinkley提到将数据库的WAL文件放在最快存储上以加速数据库。
  - bjt12345怀念Optane驱动器。
  - thebeardisred指出需要定量测试方法（如fio、rsync）来评估性能改进。

补充讨论：
- LVM的设置和使用涉及复杂的配置和调优，早期文档不足导致一些用户（如KaiserPro）对其持负面态度。
- 不同用户根据自己的需求和经验对缓存、精简配置、RAID等功能有不同的看法，特别是对数据损坏和缓存故障的担忧。
- 对ZFS和Btrfs等其他技术的提及表明，用户在选择文件系统和存储技术时会根据性能、可靠性和功能进行权衡。

44698754.article_content:
Since the inception of
solid-state drives
(SSDs), there has been a choice
to make—either use SSDs for vastly superior speeds, especially with
non-sequential read and writes (“random I/O”), or use legacy spinning
rust
hard disk drives
(HDDs) for cheaper storage that’s a bit slow for
sequential I/O
1
and
painfully
slow for random I/O.
The idea of caching frequently used data on SSDs and storing the rest on HDDs is
nothing new—
solid-state hybrid drives
(SSHDs) embodied this idea in
hardware form, while filesystems like
ZFS
support using SSDs
as
L2ARC
. However, with
the falling price of SSDs, this no longer makes sense outside of niche scenarios
with very large amounts of storage. For example, I have not needed to use HDDs
in my PC for many years at this point, since all my data easily fits on an SSD.
One of the scenarios in which this makes sense is for
the mirrors
I host
at home. Oftentimes, a project will require hundreds of gigabytes of data to be
mirrored just in case anyone needs it, but only a few files are frequently
accessed and could be cached on SSDs for fast access
2
. Similarly, I have
many LLMs locally with
Ollama
, but there are only a few I use very
frequently. The frequently used ones can be cached while the rest can be loaded
slowly from HDD when needed.
While ZFS may seem like the obvious option here, due to Linux compatibility
issues with ZFS
mentioned previously
, I decided to use
Linux’s
Logical Volume Manager (LVM)
instead for this task to save myself
some headache. To ensure reliable storage in the event of HDD failures, I am
running the HDDs in
RAID 1
with Linux’s
mdadm
software RAID.
This post documents how to build such a cached RAID array and explores some
considerations when building reliable and fast storage.
Table of contents
Why use LVM cache?
A quick introduction to LVM
The hardware setup
Why use RAID 1 on HDDs?
Setting up RAID 1 with
mdadm
Creating the SSD cache partition
Creating a new volume group
Creating the cached LV
Creating a filesystem
Mounting the new filesystem
Monitoring
Conclusion
Why use LVM cache?
There are several alternative block device caching solutions on Linux, such as:
bcache
: a built-in Linux kernel module that does similar caching
as LVM. I don’t like the way it’s set up by owning the entire block device and
non-persistent sysfs configurations, compared to LVM remembering all the
configuration options, nor do I enjoy hearing about all the reports of bcache
corrupting data; and
EnhanceIO
: an old kernel module that does something similar to
bcache and LVM cache, but hasn’t been maintained for over a decade.
Since I am very familiar with LVM and have already used it for other reasons, I
opted to use LVM for this exercise as well.
A quick introduction to LVM
If you aren’t familiar with LVM, we’ll need to first introduce some concepts, or
none of the LVM portions of this post will make any sense.
First, we’ll need to introduce block devices, which are just devices with a
fixed number of blocks that can be read at any offset. HDDs and SSDs show up as
block devices, such
/dev/sda
. They can be partitioned into multiple pieces,
showing up as smaller block devices such as
/dev/sda1
, the first partition on
/dev/sda
. Filesystems can be created directly on block devices, but these
block devices can also be used with more advanced things like RAID and LVM.
LVM is a volume manager that allows you to create logical volumes that can be
expanded much more easily than regular partitions. In LVM, there are three major
entity types:
Physical volumes (PVs)
: block devices that are used as the underlying
storage for LVM;
Logical volumes (LVs)
: block devices that are presented by LVM, stored on
one or more PVs; and
Volume groups (VGs)
: a group of PVs on which LVs can be created.
LVs can be used just like partitions to store files, with the flexibility of
being able to expand them at will while they are
actively being accessed
,
without having to be contiguous like real partitions.
There are more advanced LV types, such as thin pools, which doesn’t allocate
space for LVs until they are actually used to store data, and cached volumes,
which this post is about.
The hardware
For the purposes of this post, we will assume that there are two SATA HDDs (
4 TB each in my case), available as block devices
/dev/sda
and
/dev/sdb
:
$
lsblk
NAME               MAJ:MIN RM   SIZE RO TYPE  MOUNTPOINTS
sda                  8:0    0   3.6T  0 disk
sdb                  8:16   0   3.6T  0 disk
...
Warning
: before copying any commands, ensure that you are operating on the
correct device. There is no undo button for most of the commands in this post,
so be very careful lest you destroy your precious data! When in doubt, run
lsblk
to double check!
We’ll also assume that the SSD is
/dev/nvme0n1

(2 TB in my case),
and we will allocate 100 GiB of it as the cache by creating a partition.

44698754.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何利用Linux的逻辑卷管理器（LVM）构建一个缓存的RAID阵列，结合SSD和HDD以实现高性价比的存储方案。SSD用于加速频繁访问数据的读取，而大容量的HDD用于存储不常访问的数据。作者选择LVM缓存而不是ZFS或其他工具，因为LVM配置简单且兼容性好。HDD部分采用RAID 1以提高数据可靠性，防止磁盘故障导致数据丢失。文章详细介绍了硬件设置、RAID 1配置、缓存分区创建及逻辑卷管理的具体步骤，并讨论了该方案的优势和注意事项。通过这种方式，用户可以在享受SSD高速性能的同时，利用HDD的大容量存储。
44698754.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LVM及其相关技术（RAID、缓存、精简配置等）的使用经验和优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持LVM的灵活性与功能**：
  - dale_glass认为LVM非常灵活，具备RAID、迁移、完整性检查、缓存、快照、精简配置等多种功能，推荐将所有设备放入同一个卷组（VG）以充分利用LVM的灵活性。
  - iam-TJ也支持LVM的RAID功能，指出LVM可以按逻辑卷（LV）进行定制，包括缓存、镜像等，且支持实时扩展，非常灵活。
  
• **对精简配置（thin provisioning）的警告**：
  - dale_glass警告不要轻易使用精简配置，因为其性能影响显著，且在数据故障时可能会导致问题。
  
• **对缓存功能的讨论**：
  - gopalv指出缓存的性能提升取决于访问模式，并分享了使用ext4外部日志和将SSD用于缓存的成功经验，但也提到SSD故障可能导致数据丢失的风险。
  - jpecar对LVM缓存持负面态度，认为其早期版本像一个黑盒，无法根据工作负载调整，最终选择了全闪存方案。

  - rsync提到ZFS的元数据缓存设备可以大幅提升IOPS，但警告如果丢失元数据设备会导致数据池丢失。

  - oakwhiz分享了设置LVM RAID5的经验，指出设置过程复杂，但运行良好。

- 对ZFS和Btrfs等其他技术的提及表明，用户在选择文件系统和存储技术时会根据性能、可靠性和功能进行权衡。

data.title: A low power 1U Raspberry Pi cluster server for inexpensive colocation (2021)
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个基于Raspberry Pi的低功耗1U集群服务器项目，旨在以低成本实现服务器托管。项目设计目标是在1A @ 120V的功率限制内，最大化计算能力、存储和性价比。服务器使用Supermicro 1U机箱，内含5个Raspberry Pi 4b作为单板计算机，每个配备Geekworm外壳和Kingston A400 M.2 SSD用于存储。网络部分使用NETGEAR 8口千兆交换机，并通过继电器模块实现远程电源管理。项目总成本约800美元，功耗在空闲时为36-48W，负载时为43.2-50.4W，符合托管服务商的功率限制。文章还详细列出了硬件组装、软件设置及功耗测量方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Raspberry Pi服务器集群项目的实用性、技术细节及替代方案

不同观点：
• 项目作者[postpawl]认为，项目已有4年历史，目前可能使用Mac minis或mini PC更为合适。他也提到廉价托管服务存在安全隐患，例如IP冲突问题。此外，托管公司破产后硬件被归还，表明技术故障风险高。
• [mvip]推荐参考Mythic Beasts的做法，他们将大量Raspberry Pi装入机架，并托管Raspberry Pi官网，提供了实际案例和图片链接。
• [Catbert59]建议使用Intel n100/n150/n305系列设备，特别是n100，因其无活动部件更稳定，但对于n150及以上需要注意主动散热问题。
• [nateb2022]认为该项目的性价比不高，相比之下Hetzner等提供商的服务器配置更高、费用更低，且可以通过eBay淘零件组装更好的服务器。
• [procaryote]提出可以通过直接从继电器供电到Pi的电源引脚来节省USB适配器，并建议添加串行控制台和电源按钮功能，还提到可以使用Pi5和M2板来优化设计。
• [rbanffy]提到许多集群板允许插入计算模块板，并自带开关，可以提供更密集的系统，但制作新板需要大量工作，且涉及复杂的网络设计。
• [bullen]分享了自己构建的集群，使用自托管和家庭光纤，节省空间并实现静音散热，同时提到Raspberry 5和3588发热较高。
• [omarqureshi]描述了自己的类似设置，使用Pi 5和PoE Hats，效果良好且无需额外电源，但遇到PoE Hats风扇问题。

补充讨论：
• [hawk_]询问任意供应商的托管意义，表明对托管应用场景的困惑。
• [dnemmers]担心项目硬件在运输中难以保持完整，但认为在家中使用可能没问题。
• [asteroidburger]指出项目中16GB DDR4内存和1.2TB存储在多个节点间分配，性能不足。
• [arnon]对项目创意表示认可，但认为其难以持久运行。
• [crinkly]提到托管公司对硬件要求严格，且微型集群的IPv4成本问题是个挑战，但认为该项目可能适合IPv6集群。

争议焦点：
• 项目的实用性和性价比受到质疑，尤其是与传统托管服务和硬件方案对比时。
• 硬件的稳定性和运输安全性存在争议，部分评论者认为在家中使用更实际。
• IPv4成本问题在微型集群中被认为是主要挑战之一。

Raspberry Pi 1U Server
There are server colocation providers that allow hosting a 1U server for as low as $30/month, but there's a catch: There are restrictions on power usage (1A @ 120v max, for example) because they're expecting small and power-efficient network equipment like firewalls.
This repo is about designing a server that fits within the 1U space and 1A @ 120v power constraint while maximizing computing power, storage, and value.

data.title: Janet: Lightweight, Expressive, Modern Lisp
data.author: veqq
data.article_summary: Janet是一个功能性和命令式编程语言，核心部分不到1MB，可运行于Windows、Linux、macOS、BSD等系统，易于移植。它既可作为系统脚本语言，也可嵌入其他程序中使用，适用于快速原型设计和动态系统开发。Janet使用标准C99编写，支持线程、网络、事件循环、C语言直接互操作等功能，并附带REPL和调试器。其核心库包含500多个函数和宏，支持将项目导出为独立可执行文件。Janet还提供诸如PEG等高级特性，并可通过jpm工具安装包，如HTTP服务器、Web开发框架、JSON解析器等库。社区和文档资源丰富，支持多种编辑器和平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp语言及其变种（如Janet）的开发体验、生态系统、性能和工具支持

不同观点：
• **uvas_pasas_per**：认为Lisp的语法风格`(fun a b c)`在IDE自动补全方面不如面向对象语言的`.fun(b, c)`直观。开发者需要频繁考虑函数签名，这增加了认知负担。他希望找到一种方法，让编辑和自动补全更顺畅。
• **zelphirkalt**：关注Janet等Lisp变种的生态系统，尤其是库的支持。他提到GNU Guile和Racket有丰富的库，但对Janet的库（如web服务器、JSON解析器、数据结构等）表示担忧。此外，他还强调了可重现性和学习资源的匮乏。
• **dusted**：对Lisp的简洁语法表示欣赏，但尚未实现完整的函数功能，且项目较为混乱，仅为解释型。
• **dmpk2k**：询问Janet是否有原生编译器和类型系统，能否达到SBCL的性能水平，同时希望有更小的镜像尺寸。
• **bjoli**：质疑Janet的独特性，认为它只是Scheme的变种，没有足够的理由从Guile切换到Janet。
• **rich_sasha**：希望有一个决策树来帮助选择合适的Lisp变种（如CL, Scheme, Racket, Clojure, Janet）。

Janet Language
Janet is a functional and imperative programming language. It runs on Windows, Linux,
macOS, BSDs, and should run on other systems with some porting. The entire language (core library,
interpreter, compiler, assembler, PEG) is less than 1MB. You can also add Janet scripting
to an application by embedding a single C source file and a single header.
Download
Source
Documentation
Core API
Forum
Use Cases
Janet makes a good system scripting language, or a language to embed in other programs.  Janet also can be used for rapid prototyping, dynamic systems, and other domains
where dynamic languages shine. Implemented mostly in standard C99, Janet runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.
The few features that are not standard C (dynamic library loading, compiler specific optimizations),
are fairly straightforward. Janet can be easily ported to new platforms. While Janet is embeddable, it comes with a bit more out of the box than many other such easily embeddable languages
such as threading, networking, an event loop, subprocess handling, regex-like library called PEG, and more.
Features
Minimal setup - one binary and you are good to go!
Builtin support for threads, networking, and an event loop
First class closures
Garbage collection
First class green threads (continuations)
Mutable and immutable arrays (array/tuple)
Mutable and immutable hashtables (table/struct)
Mutable and immutable strings (buffer/string)
Macros
Tail call optimization
Direct interop with C via abstract types and C functions
Dynamically load C libraries
Lexical scoping
REPL and interactive debugger

data.author: hansmayer
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种分层推理模型（Hierarchical Reasoning Model, HRM），旨在解决当前大型语言模型在处理复杂目标导向任务时的不足。HRM受人脑分层和多时间尺度处理的启发，通过两个相互依赖的递归模块实现深度计算：负责缓慢抽象规划的高层模块和处理快速详细计算的低层模块。HRM在仅有2700万参数的情况下，使用1000个训练样本即可在复杂推理任务中取得优异表现，无需预训练或链式思考（CoT）数据。该模型在抽象与推理数据集（ARC）上超越了更大的模型，展示了其在通用计算和推理系统中的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HRM模型的性能、原理及其潜在应用和争议

不同观点：
• **积极评价**：
   - [cs702] 认为HRM模型在多个复杂任务（如Sudoku和迷宫问题）上表现出色，尤其在不使用预训练和大量数据的情况下，超过了当前最先进的CoT方法。
   - [topspin] 强调HRM模型的层次推理机制类似于人脑的认知模式，特别是通过自适应停止策略实现“快慢思考”的机制，并认为这种多模块合作是实现AGI的潜在途径。
   - [advael] 对HRM模型使用递归模块增强注意力模型的方法表示赞赏，认为这是未来研究的一个有前景的方向。

• **与认知科学理论的关联**：
   - [SubiculumCode] 从认知心理学角度出发，认为HRM模型与“模糊痕迹理论”相吻合，该理论主张记忆和认知在不同层次上运作，这与HRM的多层次推理机制相似。

• **怀疑与批评**：
   - [JonathanRaines] 对HRM模型的结果表示怀疑，指出该研究尚未经过同行评审，且结果部分缺乏评估细节，实际性能可能不如文中声称的那样优越。
   - [malcontented] 虽然不否认HRM模型的创新性，但对其与CoT模型的比较提出质疑，认为HRM模型更像是一个特定问题的解题器，而非通用的任务解决者。

• **潜在应用与扩展**：
   - [lispitillo] 提出HRM模型与MoE（专家混合模型）结合的可能性，并预测这种结合可能在短时间内实现，但指出HRM模型当前的应用场景有限，缺乏对未来应用的讨论。
   - [OgsyedIE] 认为HRM模型的嵌套结构可以与MoE系统结合，创造出在效率和质量上都有新突破的模型。
   - [camphy] 关注HRM模型在模糊推理场景中的应用潜力，认为目前模型在定义明确的问题空间（如Sudoku）上表现优异，但对其在更复杂环境中的表现存疑。

• **幽默与调侃**：
   - [0x000xca0xfe] 开玩笑地提到HRM模型可能终结CAPTCHA验证码。
   - [belter] 质疑HRM模型是否只是ReAct、Chain-of-Thought和结构化规划的变种。
   - [electroglyph] 简单直接地问“但它能扩展吗？”

补充讨论：
• **实验验证需求**：
   - [nowittyusername] 表示虽然HRM模型的概念听起来合理，但需要第三方验证其实际效果。
   - [smokel] 计划通过GitHub仓库亲自验证HRM模型的效果，并对其无需预训练即可解决规则学习问题表示惊讶。

争议焦点：HRM模型的实际性能、与CoT模型的比较以及其在不同场景中的通用性和扩展性。

Abstract:
Reasoning, the process of devising and executing complex goal-oriented action sequences, remains a critical challenge in AI. Current large language models (LLMs) primarily employ Chain-of-Thought (CoT) techniques, which suffer from brittle task decomposition, extensive data requirements, and high latency. Inspired by the hierarchical and multi-timescale processing in the human brain, we propose the Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM), a novel recurrent architecture that attains significant computational depth while maintaining both training stability and efficiency. HRM executes sequential reasoning tasks in a single forward pass without explicit supervision of the intermediate process, through two interdependent recurrent modules: a high-level module responsible for slow, abstract planning, and a low-level module handling rapid, detailed computations. With only 27 million parameters, HRM achieves exceptional performance on complex reasoning tasks using only 1000 training samples. The model operates without pre-training or CoT data, yet achieves nearly perfect performance on challenging tasks including complex Sudoku puzzles and optimal path finding in large mazes. Furthermore, HRM outperforms much larger models with significantly longer context windows on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC), a key benchmark for measuring artificial general intelligence capabilities. These results underscore HRM's potential as a transformative advancement toward universal computation and general-purpose reasoning systems.

data.title: StackSafe: Taming recursion in Rust without stack overflow
data.author: andylokandy
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了在Rust中处理递归算法导致的栈溢出问题的解决方案——StackSafe。递归算法虽然直观，但在处理深层数据结构时容易引发栈溢出，导致程序崩溃。传统解决方案包括手动将递归转换为迭代代码，但这种方法在处理复杂数据转换和多重递归时非常复杂。低层库如`stacker`和`recursive`提供了一些栈增长机制，但仍需手动处理许多细节。

StackSafe通过简单的注解`#[stacksafe]`自动扩展栈，使递归函数和递归数据结构都能安全运行，无需担心栈溢出。它同时解决了递归函数和递归数据结构的栈溢出问题，已在生产环境中被用于处理大规模数据工作负载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust 中如何解决栈溢出问题以及不同方案的优劣

不同观点：
• [AdieuToLogic] 认为可以使用 Free Monad 模式来解决栈溢出问题，这种方法通过将栈空间转移到堆空间来避免栈溢出。虽然速度较慢，但可以有效防止栈溢出。同时提到 Rust 中有一个叫 higher_free_macro 的库可能适合此用途。

• [hotpotat] 指出，必须小心确保所有递归函数都使用 #[recursive] 注解，类似于在某些 Haskell 模式中选择严格性来避免类似问题。虽然对有这个库感到欣慰，但同时也对 Rust 编译器本身对递归的支持不足表示遗憾。

• [lionkor] 反对使用 Free Monad 模式，认为这是一种内存使用效率低下的“创可贴”式解决方案，并建议使用支持尾递归的库（如 tailcall）来解决问题。

• [CyberDildonics] 提出使用显式的堆栈数据结构来替代调用栈，认为这样可以更有效地控制栈帧的大小和使用情况，避免栈溢出问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于解决栈溢出的最佳方式：一方支持使用 Free Monad 模式和现有库，另一方则倾向于使用尾递归或显式堆栈数据结构。
• 对 Rust 编译器本身对递归支持的不足提出了批评，希望编译器能提供更好的递归支持。
• 不同方案的内存使用效率和性能成为讨论的重要论据，特别是 Free Monad 模式的内存消耗和速度问题被多次提及。

data.title: BlueOS Kernel – Written in Rust, compatible with POSIX
data.author: dacapoday
data.article_summary: BlueOS内核是一个用Rust编写的操作系统内核，注重安全性、轻量化和通用性，兼容POSIX接口并支持Rust标准库。目前支持ARM32、ARM64、RISCV32和RISCV64架构，QEMU平台也受支持，硬件板支持正在开发中。内核包含CPU架构支持、系统调度器、内存管理、文件系统、网络和设备子系统等核心组件。相关技术文档和教程可在BlueOS官网的内核页面找到。项目还包括基于Rust的libc实现和各种示例应用。该项目使用Apache-2.0许可证，已有507个星标和30个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统和设备驱动标准的可行性、中国操作系统开发情况对比以及特定操作系统的技术特点和进展。

不同观点：
• [notepad0x90] 认为如果有一个像POSIX那样的标准设备驱动接口，可以让不同内核如Redox、BlueOS等利用现有的Linux驱动模块。但他指出，由于Linux内核中的数据结构和驱动程序与内核紧密耦合，实现这一目标可能会很复杂。

• [StopDisinfo910] 提出关于中国（如华为和Vivo）的操作系统开发资源在英文世界中的稀缺性，并询问这些操作系统（主要用于手机的RTOS）与QNX、Linux相比如何，以及是否像Fuchsia那样具有野心。他同时提到目前中西方在技术开发上似乎存在一定的隔阂。

• [mrbluecoat] 分享了Blue River Operating System 2的信息，指出它是首个用Rust语言编写的操作系统，强调了Rust在编译阶段就能检测内存安全问题的安全性优势。

• [AuthAuth] 关心Blue River Operating System与Asterinas操作系统在进展上的比较，但没有提供具体细节。

• [notfed] 关心如何在不编译的情况下查看相关书籍内容，暗示对技术文档的获取方式存在疑问。

补充讨论：
• 关于中国操作系统开发的现状和进展，尤其是与西方技术世界的沟通障碍，成为一个隐含的讨论点。
• 不同操作系统（Blue River OS、Asterinas、Fuchsia等）的技术特点，特别是使用Rust语言带来的安全性提升，成为技术细节上的一个焦点。
• 技术文档和资源的可获得性问题也被提及，反映了社区对信息透明度的需求。

data.title: Show HN: Windows 7 GUI for the web
data.author: khangnd
data.article_summary:
7.css是一个CSS框架，用于构建类似Windows 7界面的组件。它基于XP.css，而XP.css则是98.css的扩展。该框架强调语义HTML，如使用`<button>`标签创建按钮，并注重无障碍设计。7.css不包含JavaScript，仅通过CSS样式化HTML，兼容各种前端框架。

使用方法包括通过unpkg直接引入或通过npm安装。若需与其它CSS框架共存，可使用7.scoped.css，将样式限定在`.win7`类内。此外，支持按需引入单独组件样式。

框架提供多种组件，如按钮和气泡（工具提示）。按钮有默认、按下、禁用和聚焦等状态样式。气泡可通过`role="tooltip"`创建，并能定位在不同方向。

7.css
A design system for building faithful recreations of old UIs.
Intro
7.css is a CSS framework for building interface components that look like Windows 7.
It is built on top of the GUI backbone of
XP.css
,
which is an extension of
98.css
.
My First Program
Hello, world!
OK
Cancel
This framework relies on the usage of
semantic HTML
. To make a button, you'll need
to use a
<button>
. Input elements require labels. Tabs rely on the
role="tab"
attribute.
This page will guide you through that process, but accessibility is a primary goal of this project.
You can override many of the styles of your elements while maintaining the appearance provided by
this framework. Need more padding on your buttons? Go for it. Need to add some color to your input labels?
Be our guest.
This framework does not contain any JavaScript
, it merely styles your HTML with some CSS.
This means 7.css is compatible with your frontend framework of choice.
Installation / Usage
The fastest way to use 7.css is to import it from unpkg.
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/7.css">
You can also install 7.css
from npm
.
Installation
npm install 7.css
Usage
import "7.css/dist/7.css";

7.scoped.css
stylesheet instead to scope the styling within a
win7
class.
unpkg:
https://unpkg.com/7.css/dist/7.scoped.css

import "7.css/dist/7.scoped.css"

Tree-shaking

https://unpkg.com/7.css/dist/gui/tabs.css

44702894.article_summary:
7.css是一个CSS框架，用于构建类似Windows 7界面的组件。它基于XP.css，而XP.css则是98.css的扩展。该框架强调语义HTML，如使用`<button>`标签创建按钮，并注重无障碍设计。7.css不包含JavaScript，仅通过CSS样式化HTML，兼容各种前端框架。

使用方法包括通过unpkg直接引入或通过npm安装。若需与其它CSS框架共存，可使用7.scoped.css，将样式限定在`.win7`类内。此外，支持按需引入单独组件样式。

框架提供多种组件，如按钮和气泡（工具提示）。按钮有默认、按下、禁用和聚焦等状态样式。气泡可通过`role="tooltip"`创建，并能定位在不同方向。

data.title: The many JavaScript runtimes of the last decade
data.author: LinguaBrowse
data.article_summary:
过去十年中，JavaScript运行时和引擎大量涌现，使JavaScript得以在云端、边缘计算、智能电视、移动设备甚至微控制器等多种环境中运行。这种多样性源于不同场景对任务精确度的需求。2002年，Akamai推出首个“边缘计算”解决方案，但直到2009年Node.js出现，JavaScript才开始被用于服务器端。2014年，AWS Lambda使Node.js进入无服务器领域。2016年，AWS推出Lambda@Edge，使JavaScript真正进入边缘计算。然而，Cloudflare Workers在2017年迅速崛起，成为直接产品化的JavaScript运行时，获得巨大成功。随后，Deno于2018年出现，成立Deno Land Inc并推出Deno Deploy，挑战Cloudflare。2022年，WinterCG成立以统一新运行时标准，Bun和Wasmer也相继推出新边缘计算解决方案。

不同运行时使用不同引擎，如Deno用V8，Bun用JavaScriptCore，WinterJS用SpiderMonkey，LLRT用QuickJS，Cloudflare Workers用workerd。在微控制器领域，轻量级引擎如Duktape、Espruino、JerryScript、Moddable和elk应运而生，支持低资源设备。最后，一些JavaScript引擎基于已有虚拟机，实现与其他语言的零成本互操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript 各种运行时和引擎的分析与比较

不同观点：
• LinguaBrowse 认为文章覆盖全面，读者能学到新知识，强调文章的广度和深度。
• Laurencerowe 指出 Cloudflare 的 workerd 运行时使用的是 V8 引擎，而非自定义引擎，纠正原文中的不准确之处。
• Weiliddat 补充提到 Bellard 的 QuickJS 仍然活跃，并提供了相关链接，认为需要在讨论中提到这一点。
• Willquack 分享了自己参与的其他未被提及的 JavaScript 运行时项目，如 PythonMonkey 和 DCP，并描述了这些项目的特点和用途。
• Ksherlock 提到微软的 JScript 也应该被提及，尽管其历史久远，但其服务器端应用（如ASP）仍有历史价值。
• Asn0 补充了90年代的 Nombas ScriptEase 运行时，并给出了相关链接。
• Sytten 纠正了 LLRT 运行时的贡献者情况，强调其社区贡献的特性，并指出其在 Rust 环境中的优势。

补充讨论：
• Ottod 和 Podgorniy 对文章质量表示赞赏，认为其具有很高的参考价值。
• Dfee 提出了对不同 JavaScript 运行时未来生存能力的担忧，特别是面对竞争和生态系统整合时，如何确保代码的互操作性。
• NeutralForest 关心如何保持文章中链接的有效性，担心未来可能无法访问原始页面。
• Dehrmann 回忆了 Rhino 作为 Java 内置 JS 解释器的历史，并提到当时没有内置 JSON 解析器的问题。
• Cat-whisperer 对新运行时如何处理异步上下文跟踪提出了疑问，关心它们是使用 Async Hooks 还是自定义解决方案。
• Tom1380 对在微控制器上使用 JavaScript 表示不解，提出了其实际应用场景的问题。

争议焦点：
• 关于 Cloudflare workerd 运行时使用的引擎存在争议，laurencerowe 认为其使用的是 V8 引擎，而非原文所述的自定义引擎。
• 不同历史时期的 JavaScript 引擎和运行时（如 JScript、Nombas ScriptEase）是否应被纳入讨论，ksherlock 和 asn0 提出了补充意见。

44701574.article_content:
July 27, 2025
The many, many, many JavaScript runtimes of the last decade
This last decade has seen an inundation of new JavaScript runtimes (and engines in equal measure), enabling us to run JavaScript in all manner of contexts with precise fitness for task. Through these, we've seen the language spread to the Cloud, the edge, Smart TVs, mobile devices, and even microcontrollers.
In this article, we'll explore what's driving this diversity, and why no one runtime or engine suffices for all purposes.
Edge computing
The first consumer "edge computing" solution was introduced in 2002 by Akamai, who enabled building on the edge using
Java and .NET
. But it would be a long time before JavaScript would join those languages – for one thing, JavaScript wouldn't be useful as a server-side language until Node.js emerged in 2009, and for another, Node.js wouldn't be employed in a serverless context until AWS Lambda in
2014
. It was only with the announcement of Lambda@Edge (in preview from
December 2016
; released
March 2017
) that JavaScript would finally be seen on the edge, again running on Node.js.
But Amazon's monopoly was to be short-lived. For just six months later came the
release
of Cloudflare Workers, a purpose-built minimal runtime revolving around the
Service Worker
API. It was devised to open an "
entirely new market
" to Cloudflare: compute and storage. And this was notably different to Amazon's venture – for the first time in the over twenty years since JavaScript's inception, a company had managed to directly productise a JavaScript runtime.
Cloudflare Workers was a phenomenal success, with
billions of tasks
run in the half year following its beta release. This scent of opportunity triggered a gold rush. Deno
appeared
shortly after in 2018 as a challenger to Node.js, and within three years,
Deno Land Inc
had formed, launching
Deno Deploy
, an edge network intended to
chase after
Cloudflare. With an initial treasure chest of
$4.9 million
and raising a
$21 million
Series A funding round the year after that, it is clear that Cloudflare weren't the only ones who believed in the value of the niche.
The rush continued in 2022. No sooner had
WinterCG
been
formed
to start defining a common ground for all these new JavaScript runtimes popping up than
Bun
appeared, quickly raising
$7 million
[archive]
to
provide
serverless hosting, continuous integration, and… edge computing. Wasmer followed suit in 2023, stepping into the Service Workers arena with
WinterJS
and
Wasmer Edge
. And not to be outdone, the very next year AWS responded with
LLRT
, another low-latency runtime just right for the edge (though not yet having an edge worker offering).
For all the overlap in strategy, notable is the variety in engines underpinning all these runtimes. While Deno continues Node.js's tradition of using
V8
, we see Bun employing
JavaScriptCore
, WinterJS using
SpiderMonkey
, LLRT on
QuickJS
, and Cloudflare Workers on the tailor-made
workerd
. No longer is the backend solely a stage for Node.js and V8 – it's now fashionable to pick a runtime and engine optimised for the task.
Microcontrollers
Many of the above runtimes would have a hard time running on a microcontroller, though. For the unfamiliar, AWS defines them
as follows
:
… a microcontroller is the basic computing unit inside smart electronic devices like washing machines and thermostats. It's a very tiny computer with its own RAM, ROM, and I/O systems, all embedded on a single chip. It can process digital signals and respond to user input, but its computing capacity is limited.
At the low end, microcontrollers may cost as little as
3 cents
, have mere bytes of RAM, run in under a milliamp of current, have an 8-bit architecture, and/or have under a kilobyte of storage.
Given these specs, full-blown Node.js would be well out of the question, so many took to producing slim-as-possible engines –
Duktape
,
Espruino
, and
mjs
in 2013,
JerryScript
in 2014,
Moddable
in 2018, and
elk
in 2021. These projects pride themselves in running on under 64 kB of RAM (in fact apparently little more than 100 bytes, in the case of Elk!), though do make tradeoffs in other areas like
performance
to do so.
These engines then spawned new runtimes, though not necessarily serving the very lowest end of microcontrollers. JerryScript underlies
IoT.js
(2015) and
Microlattice.js
(2016), both Internet of Things runtimes;
XS
(2018?) underlies Moddable; and DukTape underlies
low.js
(2018), a low-resource reimplementation of Node.js.
It goes to show that venture capital needn't be a lure to develop a JavaScript runtime; sometimes people just want to run JavaScript on a device no matter what. Sometimes, they want to call JavaScript even when working in a different language – which brings us onto our next topic.
Polyglot engines
Although most JavaScript engines are based on a bespoke virtual machine (VM) used only by the engines themselves, some are based on established VMs, enabling zero-cost interop with

data.author: thm
data.article_summary: Allianz Life证实，在2025年7月中旬的一次数据泄露事件中，黑客通过社交工程技术入侵了其第三方云CRM系统，窃取了大多数客户、金融专业人士及部分员工的个人信息。该公司已通知FBI，并表示没有证据显示其他系统被入侵。尽管未透露具体受影响人数，Allianz Life拥有140万客户。此次攻击被认为与黑客组织Scattered Spider有关，该组织近期针对保险行业发起多次攻击。Allianz计划从8月1日开始通知受影响个人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据泄露、系统安全责任以及如何改善安全现状

不同观点：
• Buttons840认为，安全研究人员（包括白帽和灰帽黑客）应享有法律保护，只要他们报告发现的漏洞。当前系统让公司可以隐藏安全漏洞，同时避免外部对其系统进行安全测试，这实际上牺牲了国家安全以保护公司利益。
• slashdev主张通过改变激励机制来减少数据泄露的影响，例如不再假设个人信息是完全私密的，而是将责任归于公司，如果公司未验证用户身份，则应承担责任。
• giantfrog认为，只有让高管因疏忽而破产或入狱，数据泄露的频率和严重性才会降低。
• time4tea建议对每条丢失的记录处以高额罚款，以迫使公司更加重视数据安全，而不是仅仅发送道歉邮件了事。
• amai提到，Allianz提供针对网络攻击的保险，这可能是应对网络安全问题的一种解决方案。
• ofjcihen指出，某些平台（如Salesforce）在安全配置和监控方面存在严重缺陷，这增加了数据泄露的风险。
• jmkni和pwarner关注具体数据泄露事件中的第三方责任以及相关的技术细节。
• bee_rider和nothercastle质疑公司使用易被黑客获取的凭证进行身份验证的责任问题。
• Havoc认为，公司通常只是简单道歉，而没有实质性改进。
• rr808抱怨个人财务信息在租赁和贷款过程中容易被泄露，建议建立临时安全上传系统。
• urquhartfe指出，公司对工程和IT的投资不足是数据安全问题的根本原因。
• SilverElfin提到，一些公司甚至不愿透露被泄露的具体信息，仅提供信用监控服务，这令人愤怒。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于公司是否应为其系统安全负全责，以及如何通过法律和经济手段促使公司改进安全措施。
• 讨论还涉及具体技术问题，如Salesforce的安全配置缺陷，以及对身份验证过程的改进建议。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，有些人认为需要通过更严厉的惩罚和责任追究来促使公司认真对待数据安全。

44703079.article_content:
U.S. insurance giant Allianz Life has confirmed to TechCrunch that hackers stole the personal information of the “majority” of its customers, financial professionals, and employees during a mid-July data breach.
When reached by TechCrunch, Allianz Life spokesperson Brett Weinberg confirmed the breach.
“On July 16, 2025, a malicious threat actor gained access to a third-party, cloud-based CRM system used by Allianz Life,” referring to a customer relationship management (CRM) database containing information on its customers. “The threat actor was able to obtain personally identifiable data related to the majority of Allianz Life’s customers, financial professionals, and select Allianz Life employees, using a social engineering technique,” the spokesperson said.
The company disclosed the data breach on Saturday in a
legally required filing
with Maine’s attorney general, but did not immediately provide a number of how many Allianz Life customers are affected. According to the spokesperson, Allianz Life has 1.4 million customers. Its parent company, Allianz, has more than 125 million customers worldwide.
Allianz Life said it notified the FBI, and added it had “no evidence” that any other systems on its network were compromised.
The insurance giant would not say if it had received any communication from the hackers, such as a ransom note. The company also would not attribute the breach to a hacking group.
Allianz Life is the latest company in the past month to have been hacked during a wave of data breaches targeting the wider insurance industry,
including Aflac
, a major provider of supplementary health insurance. Security researchers at Google said in June that
they were “aware of multiple intrusions” across the insurance sector
attributed to Scattered Spider, a collective of hackers and techniques that rely on social engineering techniques, such as deceptively calling and tricking helpdesks into granting them access to a company’s network.
Prior to targeting insurance companies, the Scattered Spider hackers were seen
targeting the U.K. retail industry
, as well
as the aviation and transportation sectors
, and are historically known for hacks
targeting Silicon Valley technology giants
.
Per the Maine filing, Allianz plans to begin notifying affected individuals around August 1.
Do you know more about the Allianz Life cyberattack? Are you an affected customer or employee? Securely contact this reporter via encrypted message at zackwhittaker.1337 on Signal.

data.title: Math Is Erotic
data.author: HR01
data.article_summary: Matthew B. Crawford 回顾了 J. Jacob Tawney 的新书《Another Sort of Mathematics》，强调数学不仅关乎经济竞争力或批判性思维，更是一种追求美的体验。作者回忆起在大学物理课上，诺贝尔奖得主 Bob Schrieffer 通过波动方程和磁场现象最终揭示麦克斯韦方程的美妙时刻，展现了数学中蕴含的宇宙统一性。Tawney 主张通过数学证明体验其内在之美，而非仅仅服务于外部目的。在当前教育体系面临人工智能和学术职业化挑战的背景下，Crawford 认为应重新思考教育的本质，回归追求真理的自由教育，让数学成为通向超越人类心智的途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数学的本质及其与人类感知、宇宙秩序的关系

不同观点：
• **数学与性罪感**：pyuser583提到，他记得有资料显示帕斯卡放弃数学是因为他认为数学是一种性罪恶。这一观点将数学与道德、宗教层面的罪恶感联系在一起，尽管没有提供具体来源。
  
• **数学与宇宙之美**：bwfan123认为数学揭示了心智与宇宙之间的共鸣，这种共鸣体现了宇宙的秩序与美。他还引用了希腊语中“cosmos”一词的双重含义，即秩序与美，并提出数学具有“情色”性质，因为它唤起了人们对真理、美和善良的渴望。这一观点强调了数学的美学和哲学维度。

• **数学的超自然性质**：Nasrudith认为数学具有超自然性质，它不仅可以描述宇宙，还可以描述无数可能的宇宙及其内部一致性。数学甚至可以独立于宇宙存在，描述那些不可能存在的事物。这一观点强调了数学的抽象力量及其超越现实的特性。

补充讨论：
• **寻找类似文章**：lnfromx询问是否有人知道与上述观点类似的文章，表明对探索数学与宇宙、人类感知之间关系的文章感兴趣。

• **AI与“半吊子”现象**：bwfan123提到了文章链接，讨论了人工智能带来的“半吊子”现象，这与其他讨论点形成了一种延伸讨论，关注了科技对数学及人类认知的影响。

争议焦点：
• 数学的本质：bwfan123和Nasrudith的观点都强调了数学的美和秩序，但Nasrudith进一步提出了数学的超自然性质，与bwfan123的美学和哲学视角形成了一种对比和补充。

• 帕斯卡与数学的性罪感：pyuser583的观点较为独特，与其他讨论的数学美学和哲学维度形成对比，提出了历史人物对数学的道德和宗教层面的看法。

44700925.article_content:
Math Is Erotic
Matthew B. Crawford
July 24, 2025
Share
Article
Another Sort of Mathematics:
Selected Proofs Necessary to Finally Acquire an Education in Mathematics
by j. jacob tawney
encounter books, 328 pages, $34.99
The most shining moment of my education as a physics major at UC Santa Barbara came in the final lecture of an upper-division course on electricity and magnetism. We had learned the facts early in the semester and could do the problem sets. Then the instructor, Nobel laureate Bob Schrieffer, seemed to take us backward. He spent a few lectures plumbing the depths of “the wave equation” that can be used to describe all phenomena with periodic motions, from water waves to sound waves. It also describes the pattern that appears when you walk past two fences and their visual elements of light and darkness superimpose—called a “moiré pattern.” (My dad, a physics professor at Berkeley, liked to point these out to me as a kid as we walked past fenced tennis courts toward the swimming pool at the Claremont Hotel, where he would do beautiful dives off the high dive.)
The next several lectures seemed totally unrelated. They were about magnetism, with field patterns and lines of force and whatnot. Professor Schrieffer hinted that some big reveal was coming, but I was losing patience. I couldn’t see the coherence of these disparate things. In the final lecture, without announcing where we were headed or giving anything away, he worked the blackboard furiously. Chalk dust floated in the air and found its way onto his clothes in random smears. About one minute before the end of this last class, he turned and grinned triumphantly. There on the blackboard was something that I “knew” and recognized from early in the course, to be accepted and memorized. But it now appeared as a revelation, something of incomparable beauty and wonder: Maxwell’s Equations. They show the fundamental unity of electrical and magnetic phenomena. We had arrived at them beginning from water waves. I was stunned.
The purely mental activity of doing mathematics can be a mode of access to something that transcends the human mind. That this should be the case would seem to indicate that there is a deep resonance between mind and cosmos—almost as if cosmos participates in mind.
J. Jacob Tawney, in his new book
Another Sort of Mathematics
, writes that there are “some things from mathematics that you should experience.” What an odd and arresting way to open a book about math. It is not the sort of exhortation we are used to hearing from the STEM-winders-and-grinders who push math for the sake of economic competitiveness, critical thinking skills, or other ends extrinsic to math itself. For Tawney, there is something beautiful and important to be experienced. He comes to us not as an “educator” in the dreary, institutional sense of that word, but as an evangelist.
His book arrives at a time when it has become necessary to rethink education altogether. David McGrogan at
News from Uncibal
writes about “the coming competence apocalypse.” The likely atrophy of our mental faculties from outsourcing mental tasks to AI will only accelerate the long-running collapse of competence that McGrogan details. Meanwhile, John Carter at
Postcards from Barsoom
likens the state of the university to that of the monasteries in late-medieval England, where, he writes, “religious vows were more theoretical than daily realities for many monks. Does anyone truly think that Harvard professors take
Veritas
at all seriously?”
Scholarly careerism, declining curricular standards, the replication crisis, a demented ideological monoculture, administrative bloat—a steady accumulation of chronic cultural entropy has built up inside the organizational tissue of the academy, rendering universities less effective, less trustworthy, less affordable, and less useful than ever before in history.
The function universities have long played is less one of educating than of credentialing. Carter gives us good reason to think the credentialing function of universities is about to collapse, due to AI. But he finds new possibilities, or rather old possibilities, emerging from the wreckage: liberal education in the original sense, as a leisure activity (“scholar” is from
schole
,
leisure) for its own sake; for the love of truth. Unburdened of its current gatekeeping role in the political economy of managerialism and bullshit jobs, and no longer serving as a legitimation operation for unpopular political projects (producing “the Science” that must be “followed”), the successor to the modern university will be something subterranean rather than publicity-seeking, disconnected from power and money, useless, a place where people with the most searching minds gather to pursue truth for the love of it, as literal amateurs.
Which brings me back to Tawney’s book. In
Another Sort of Mathematics
, mathematical proofs take pride of place. They do so not as a response to that characteristically moder

data.title: The Bootstrap Load
data.author: gone35
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了英特尔4004微处理器设计中的自举负载技术。该技术由设计者Federico Faggin开发，利用硅栅技术实现，能够在输出电压等于全供电电压的情况下构建逻辑门，而传统电阻负载只能达到供电电压的60%。通过深入理解器件物理原理，Faggin成功制造出无需额外掩模层的优质片上电容，解决了此前被认为无法实现的难题。自举负载和隐埋接触对于在有限功耗下实现所需速度至关重要。相比之下，四相设计虽能达到类似效果但更为复杂，如Rockwell的第一款微处理器PPS-4。4004的原始电路图中广泛使用了自举负载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于bootstrap load的细节及其技术背景

不同观点：
• [_ihaque] 认为原文链接中对bootstrap load的描述不够详细，但提到@kens写了一篇更详尽的文章来解释这一技术（提供了具体链接）。这表明[_ihaque]关注的是技术细节的深入了解，并通过引用其他资源来补充原文内容的不足。

• [cushychicken] 则关注的是4004 schematic（可能是指Intel 4004芯片的电路图）的紧凑性，对其能够将整个设计浓缩到三页纸上表示惊讶和赞赏。这表明[cushychicken]的关注点在于技术的精简和工程设计的巧妙。

补充讨论：
- [_ihaque] 引用的文章链接（https://www.righto.com/2020/10/how-bootstrap-load-made-histo...）进一步探讨了bootstrap load的技术实现和历史背景，提供了更深入的技术分析。
- [cushychicken] 的评论反映了对于技术文档简洁性和工程复杂性的感慨，没有涉及具体的技术实现细节。

争议焦点：评论之间并无直接争议，但可以看出对同一技术话题的不同关注点，[_ihaque]注重技术细节和背景，而[cushychicken]则偏重于设计的简洁和精妙。

44704482.article_content:
The Bootstrap Load
Home
Back
The Intel 4004 Microprocessor and the Silicon Gate Technology
A testimonial from Federico Faggin, designer of the 4004 and developer of its enabling technology
Quick Links:
Silicon Gate Technology
The Buried Contact
The Gilbert Hyatt Patent
The Bootstrap Load
At Fairchild, Faggin also built bootstrap load devices in early 1970, using the
silicon gate technology
.
Bootstrap load is a circuit technique that allows building logic gates with
the output voltage equal to the full supply voltage compared with a normal resistive load where the output voltage reaches about 60% of the supply voltage. The bootstrap load devices
required the fabrication of good-quality capacitors on a chip that were thought impossible to manufacture with SGT without using an extra masking layer. Faggin, a physicist, came to the solution thanks to:
"an understanding of the physics of how devices work, because in a bootstrap load what you need to do is to always have a virtual junction, instead of a physical junction."
(Faggin, in a 2007 oral panel interview with David House CHM), and he showed how to make bootstrap load devices without an extra masking layer.
The
buried contact
and particularly the bootstrap load, were indispensable to obtain the required speed within the available power budget. The only other design technique with the
correct speed-power product, available at that time, was the more cumbersome
four-phase design used by Four-Phase Systems, Inc. and by Rockwell. Rockwell
used it in their first microprocessor, the PPS-4, which was completed nine
months after Intels 4004.
Original schematic of the 4004 showing bootstrap loads
Detail in the original diagram of the Arithmetic Unit (ARU) of the 4004 with original pencil notations by F. Faggin. A resistor symbol in the schematic indicates an MOS transistor with its gate connected to its drain and used as a resistive load. When a B is shown next to a resistor symbol, a bootstrap load needs to be used. Bootstrap loads in silicon gate are found throughout the
3-sheets schematics
.
44704482.article_summary: 本文介绍了英特尔4004微处理器设计中的自举负载技术。该技术由设计者Federico Faggin开发，利用硅栅技术实现，能够在输出电压等于全供电电压的情况下构建逻辑门，而传统电阻负载只能达到供电电压的60%。通过深入理解器件物理原理，Faggin成功制造出无需额外掩模层的优质片上电容，解决了此前被认为无法实现的难题。自举负载和隐埋接触对于在有限功耗下实现所需速度至关重要。相比之下，四相设计虽能达到类似效果但更为复杂，如Rockwell的第一款微处理器PPS-4。4004的原始电路图中广泛使用了自举负载。

data.author: JadedBlueEyes
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者和朋友如何破解了他们租住的房子里的智能洗衣机，以实现更有用的功能。洗衣机配有Wi-Fi和手机应用，可以发送洗涤完成通知，但一次只能一个人连接，使用不便。作者利用逆向工程和网络抓包工具（如tcpdump和mitmproxy）分析了洗衣机应用的通信流量，发现它与特定的服务器通信。通过设置OpenWRT路由器，作者成功捕获了洗衣机的网络流量，并计划模仿其通信方式，以便在多个设备上接收通知。此外，作者还提到他们用类似的方法破解了老房子的门铃，通过433MHz接收器在Discord上接收通知。最终，他们成功实现了对洗衣机通知功能的改进。

44704270.article_content:
How I hacked my washing machine
¶
If you've known me for some amount of time you knew this was something that was bound to happen eventually. Yesterday (and technically today), me and a friend went on an endeavor to hack our washing machine, partially for the fun of it, and partially because there's actually a practical use for it.
Some background
¶
For context, I recently moved into a new house for uni, with some friends. This house was pre-furnished, so it came with all the appliances we needed, including a washing machine and whatnot. And, in true typical renting fashion, the washing machine is some cheap "smart" model, that features a Wi-Fi connection, and a mobile app to control it. Now, half of this house is populated by cybersecurity students, so naturally we were scoffing at the idea of putting the washing machine on the network.
And then we did it.
Turns out, this washing machine has the capability to send notifications to the mobile app whenever a load finishes. There's also some other stuff too like "self clean" or whatever, but nothing functional (the app is some cheap crappy HTML job crammed into a WebView). This was kinda funny, however, having notifications for when your "three hour" (usually like 4-5 hours) load finishes is actually really useful, especially when you're like me and forgot to... buy clothes, so have to keep the same set of clothes clean constantly. However,
only one person can be connected to the washing machine at a time
, so if someone else wanted notifications, you'd have to disconnect the washing machine from your app, and then let them do the whole jig. Which involves reconnecting it to the Wi-Fi network, by the way.
The front page of the washing machine app, after logging in. The app is called "
Hoover Wizard
".
Notifications received for when a wash cycle finishes.
The doorbell
¶
Tangentally related, this house is an incredibly old victorian house, meaning the walls, floors, and doors are super thick. There's also only one person living on the ground floor near the door, so having someone knock on the door, or a doorbell that just rings near the door isn't helpful, since nobody will hear it. Luckily, however, this doorbell has a receiver that plugs in elsewhere, and the doorbell broadcasts a signal to it when pressed. This is a 433MHz doorbell, which is a common frequency for these types of devices.
In short, my friend bought a cheap receiver that listens for these signals, and then uses that signal to send a notification in our Discord server, so that we all know when someone rang the doorbell. In future, it'll also probably be used in conjunction with a security camera, so we can see who rang the doorbell. Pretty neat, right?
The doorbell triggering a notification in our Discord server.
This does still, in addition, ring the actual doorbell receiver, so there's still an audible notification, but this is more of a backup.
It was after seeing the success of this project that we had the bright idea - what if we could do the same thing with the washing machine? So we started plotting...
The plan
¶
Going into this, I had some experience with reverse engineering and hacking apps on my phone. I had previously done a bit of work on reverse engineering the attendance app for my university, which was fun, but ultimately didn't go anywhere because it started being more effort than fun. However, this lead me to the initial idea - see what the washing machine app connects to, and work out the API from there. This would've been simple, just install some self-signed TLS certificate on my phone, and then use a tool like
tcpdump
and
mitmproxy
to capture DNS requests and other traffic.
However, we realised that most of the work was done
by the washing machine itself
. This gave me the bright idea to just capture the traffic from the washing machine itself, and then reverse engineer that. And so, I went and grabbed an
OpenWRT
-compatbile router I had laying around, flashed it, and set it up to listen on 2.4GHz (since that's all the washing machine worked with), and connect to WAN via 5GHz, with my laptop in the middle connected over Ethernet.
After setting up the router, I broadcast a temporary SSID, and paired the washing machine to it. Grabbed the IP address of the washing machine, and then started capturing traffic with
tcpdump
. Unfortunately, I don't have any of those captures anymore.
Who is my washing machine talking to
¶
After tracing the traffic for a short while, I noticed four things:
The washing machine REALLY liked talking to... itself? I don't think whoever engineered their networking stack knew what a loopback interface was, because it was sending a lot of traffic from itself to its own IP address. I didn't think this was relevant, so I ignored it.
It really liked sending traffic to
255.255.255.255
every second, for some reason. Again, ignored.
It occasionally contacted
simplyfimgmt.candy-hoover.com
. This is a CNAME to some herokudns domain, which I thought was odd, but

data.title: The JJ VCS workshop: A zero-to-hero speedrun
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为 "jj-workshop" 的项目，旨在帮助用户快速掌握新的版本控制系统 JJ（Jujutsu VCS）。JJ 被设计为比 Git 更易用，但在实际使用中，作者发现从 Git 转换过来仍有学习曲线，尤其是处理合并冲突等操作。为解决这一问题，作者创建了这个工作坊，提供了一系列练习和视频教程，帮助用户在短时间内熟悉 JJ 的主要工作流程。工作坊包括观看简介视频、通过幻灯片进行8个练习（耗时1-2小时），以及在遇到问题时参考视频解决方案。该项目旨在让用户快速上手 JJ，避免作者曾经历的学习困难。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对版本控制工具 **JJ (Jujutsu)** 的理解和使用体验，及其与 **Git** 的关系。

不同观点：
• **Jenk** 认为，JJ 需要用户摆脱 Git 的思维模式，才能真正理解和欣赏 JJ 的设计理念。他之前一直在将 JJ 和 Git 互相翻译对比，但后来意识到 JJ 应该被视为一种新的工作流，而不是简单的 Git 抽象层。
  
• **sn9** 持不同意见，认为 JJ 应该与 Git 兼容，并质疑使用 JJ 是否有助于提高 Git 使用技巧，或者能否用来教别人 Git 工作流。

• **myst** 支持 JJ 比 Git 更简单的观点，认为 JJ 在用户体验上是对 Git 的一大提升。

• **vlovich123** 提到 **graphite.dev** 作为一个在 Git/GitHub 上提供堆叠工作流的工具，认为它能够自动管理分支和 PR，同时保持与 Git 的兼容性。这暗示了另一种工具选择，可能比 JJ 更符合某些用户的需求。

补充讨论：
• **sastraxi** 关注文档方面的改进，建议在 README 文件中添加 Jujutsu 主页的链接，以便用户获取更多信息。

• **notnmeyer** 对 JJ 表示了积极的期待，但没有深入讨论技术细节，只是表达了使用的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• **JJ 是否应该完全摆脱 Git 的思维模式** 是主要争议点。Jenk 认为需要“忘记”Git 才能用好 JJ，而 sn9 和 myst 则认为 JJ 应该与 Git 兼容或至少在用户体验上更简单。

Become a Jujutsu Master in 1 hour
Perhaps you've heard of the JJ VCS, a new VCS replacing git that makes commit discipline and dealing with stacked PRs a breeze. Perhaps you've read the same blog posts I have, about how great jj is and how easy it is to get started.
But it wasn't enough for me, and it might not be enough for you. I felt my productivity grind to a halt as I struggled with things that had become second nature after 15 years of using git. Even though I was told it would be easy, I dreaded for days the prospect of dealing with my first merge conflict.
But then I hit jj heaven, and my productivity reached new heights. If only I'd had first gotten to do deliberate practice of the major workflows, I would have gotten there much faster.
I created this workshop to save the rest of my team — and now the rest of the world — from the same learning pains I went through learning JJ.
This is not yet another blog post about the awesomeness of jj.  It's a series of exercises — done in simulation in this tiny repo — to give you experience with all the major version-control workflows as fast as possible.
Steps
Watch the
intro video
(<6m at 1x speed).
Go through the
slides
,  featuring a series of 8 exercises to take you from "Create a new commit" to "resolve merge conflicts in a stack of PRs." (1-2 hours for someone with no jj experience.)
Watch the
conclusion video
(<6m at 1x speed).
Get stuck at any point?
Watch the video solutions below

• **myst** 支持 JJ 比 Git 更简单的观点，认为 JJ 在用户体验上是对 Git 的一大提升。

• **vlovich123** 提到 **graphite.dev** 作为一个在 Git/GitHub 上提供堆叠工作流的工具，认为它能够自动管理分支和 PR，同时保持与 Git 的兼容性。这暗示了另一种工具选择，可能比 JJ 更符合某些用户的需求。

补充讨论：
• **sastraxi** 关注文档方面的改进，建议在 README 文件中添加 Jujutsu 主页的链接，以便用户获取更多信息。

• **notnmeyer** 对 JJ 表示了积极的期待，但没有深入讨论技术细节，只是表达了使用的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• **JJ 是否应该完全摆脱 Git 的思维模式** 是主要争议点。Jenk 认为需要“忘记”Git 才能用好 JJ，而 sn9 和 myst 则认为 JJ 应该与 Git 兼容或至少在用户体验上更简单。

data.author: bingden
data.article_summary: 伦敦梅fair区的豪华街道上聚集了英国顶级私家侦探公司，其阴暗的业务名称令人联想到詹姆斯·邦德电影中的反派企业，且生意兴隆。这些公司雇佣前英国间谍、警察、记者和军事情报官员，提供从企业背景调查到全面监视的服务，有些甚至涉及非法获取个人敏感信息。政府部长和情报机构警告，外国政府利用这些公司进行“肮脏工作”，包括监视和骚扰逃至英国的异见人士。隐私国际组织的伊利亚·西亚蒂萨指出，该行业几乎不受监管，对隐私、人权和民主构成严重威胁。伦敦凭借靠近法律和金融行业的优势，成为全球私家情报中心，前情报官员利用隐秘的从业经历吸引国际客户。尽管部分业务平凡枯燥，但涉及高额诉讼支持的工作利润丰厚，包括对手研究以抹黑对手。

44687145.article_content:
LONDON — Nestled among the luxury properties of London’s elite on the opulent streets of Mayfair are the headquarters of Britain’s premier private spy firms.
Their ominous names bring to mind the shady corporations of James Bond villains — and business is booming.
Scooping up staff ranging from former British spies and police officers to ex-journalists and military intelligence officials, the U.K.’s private intelligence and investigation firms offer services from basic corporate checks to full-scale surveillance. Some even dabble in the illegal acquisition of highly personal information.
Advertisement
Advertisement
In the last year,
government ministers
and
intelligence agencies
have warned that foreign states are using the industry to “carry out their dirty work” in the U.K. — sometimes through the surveillance and harassment of dissidents that have fled to Britain as a safe haven.
POLITICO has spoken to multiple figures who have worked in — and been targets of — Britain’s private spy companies. Some say that despite tough government rhetoric, the industry’s questionable practices remain unregulated and its companies largely unaccountable.
The industry operates “with virtually no oversight, posing serious threats to privacy, human rights and democracy,” said Privacy International’s Ilia Siatitsa.
She warned: “The industry’s ability to offer powerful surveillance and intelligence-gathering capabilities to anyone with the means to pay, without meaningful scrutiny, is alarming.”
Coming in from the cold
London has become the global capital of the private intelligence industry, in part thanks to a worldwide fascination with fictional British spies in James Bond films and John le Carré novels.
Former spies make up an eye-catching minority of those now plying their trade in the private sector, with senior spooks founding or sitting on the boards of firms.
Advertisement
Advertisement
These include former heads of foreign-focused intelligence agency MI6. Others don’t publicly advertise their former careers, instead touting a vague history of experience in Whitehall and the U.K. Foreign Office.
Some believe these big-name hires are just window dressing to woo international clients.
One figure in private intelligence, granted anonymity like others in this article because of the sensitive nature of their role, said: “You’ve got the great and good on the board, you’ve got a lord here, a lady there, you’ve got a spook, you’ve got the ex-head of this and that — if you’re Mr. Investor from Ukraine or Indonesia, you’re impressed with that.”
London’s emergence as the epicenter of private intelligence is largely down to its proximity to two big pools of clients: Britain’s legal and financial sectors. | Neil Hall/EPA
A second industry figure said there’s an “element of marketing” involved because corporate clients with a hunger for info find it “very impressive that someone has served in a secret intelligence service.”
Some spooks move to the private sector because gathering intelligence — whether for King and country, or the highest bidder — is simply all they know. Some struggle in the private sector without direct access to the contacts and state support they previously enjoyed.
Britain is an outlier when it comes to the freedoms afforded to retired intelligence officers, with most never disclosing their former employment when leaving agencies like MI5 and MI6.
Advertisement
Advertisement
“That is quite unusual,” said a third private intelligence figure, adding that in the U.S. people are “very open” about having worked for the CIA. America has a “semi-retirement model where when you’re moving out of the agency, you’ll probably spend about six or seven years subcontracting back, and then you’ll finally move into the private sector.”
“We don’t do things like that here at all. So, Vauxhall [MI6] will almost never outsource meaningful intelligence work to the private sector,” they said.
Still, trading in knowledge is commonplace. The same person added that there is a “lot of frustration from both sides of the river [Thames] that the old boys’ network was getting a bit too informal, with people telling their clients that they can call their old buddies.”
Lawfare
London’s emergence as the epicenter of private intelligence is largely down to its proximity to two big pools of clients: Britain’s legal and financial sectors. These two powerhouses of the U.K. economy are regularly at the heart of complex cases that run into the billions.
Much of this work is “quite pedestrian,” says the second private intelligence figure. Basic due diligence reports involve routine checks, including whether someone is on a sanctions list or has had negative press. These, the same person said, are usually done by young graduates and the work “isn’t very well paid or exciting.”

data.title: Dual-Brain Challenge Tetris Game
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一款类似《俄罗斯方块》的游戏。玩家需要躲避掉落的方块，通过移动和旋转来完成整行，以求生存。游戏控制包括：使用方向键←/→移动，↑键旋转方块，↓键缓慢下落，空格键快速下落。玩家角色则通过A/D键左右移动，W键跳跃。若在同一位置停留超过10秒，游戏即结束。游戏结束时显示得分、清除行数以及重启选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏机制和规则设计，特别是关于暂停功能和策略优化的问题。

不同观点：
• [magneticnorth] 认为游戏缺乏暂停功能，导致玩家在尚未理解规则时就失败，体验令人沮丧。他建议增加暂停功能，以便有足够时间阅读规则和理解游戏玩法。

• [jsnell] 关注的是游戏策略问题，具体是关于一种他认为过于简单且可能降低游戏趣味的策略。他描述了一种通过创建特定"房间"来保护"红点"并简化游戏的方法，认为这种策略会使游戏失去挑战性。他提出，需要为红点的移动引入一种评分系统，以增加变化性和风险奖励，避免玩家选择单调的最优策略。

补充讨论：
• [jsnell] 提到了一种可能的解决方案，即通过改变红点游戏的得分机制来增加复杂性和趣味性，而不是简单地将其作为二元生死条件。他预见到玩家会自然地选择最优策略，即使这种策略可能很无聊，因此需要游戏设计上的调整来引导玩家进行更多样化的操作。

• 争议的焦点在于如何平衡游戏的难度和趣味性。一方面，[magneticnorth] 希望有更好的学习曲线，另一方面，[jsnell] 则关注游戏策略的深度和变化性，以避免策略单一化。

总结：玩家对游戏的规则学习体验和策略深度存在不同关注点，前者希望增加暂停功能以方便学习，后者则建议通过调整评分系统来增加游戏的复杂性和趣味性。

data.title: Government-Funded Alchemy
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕黄金合成、元素嬗变、政府投资与科技发展的多方面讨论。

不同观点：
• **twic的观点**：twic讨论了通过汞浴合成黄金的过程，特别是金汞合金（amalgam）的物理性质问题，并质疑如何从汞中分离出黄金。他提到当金含量很低时，合金表现得像汞，并引用了视频作为例子。twic进一步质疑分离方法的可行性，认为传统采矿方法可能不适用。

• **PaulHole的观点**：PaulHole引用了科幻小说《The Door into Summer》中的元素嬗变技术，描述了一个黄金廉价且元素嬗变技术普及的未来世界。他通过小说情节探讨了工程师的幸福和自动化技术的影响，并提到在该虚构世界中，机器学习技术早在1950年代就已实现。

• **godelski的观点**：godelski对政府在Marathon Fusion等项目上的小额投资持积极态度，认为即使失败也能带来有价值的知识，并使这些知识公开化，从而对未来的研究有益。他批评了围绕这些项目的炒作和风险规避行为，认为适度的失败是可以接受的，因为它们提供了学习机会。他还建议增加投资，即使失败也能接受。

• **tbrownaw的观点**：tbrownaw对通过汞合成黄金的方法表示赞赏，特别指出这是一种可能有效处理有害物质汞的方法。

• **throwawaymaths的观点**：throwawaymaths讨论了黄金作为货币的历史价值，认为黄金的价值在于其易于验证的特性，不需要复杂的化学方法，这在古代是一种无需信任的货币形式。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：twic对如何从汞中有效分离出黄金表示怀疑，而PaulHole则通过科幻小说的情节描绘了一个黄金廉价且元素嬗变技术普及的未来。这两种观点在现实与虚构之间形成对比。

• **政府投资与风险**：godelski对小额政府投资持积极态度，认为即使失败也有价值，而对围绕这些项目的炒作和风险规避持批评态度。这与其他讨论者对技术可行性的关注形成对比。

• **黄金的物理性质与验证**：讨论中涉及了金汞合金的物理性质问题（twic）以及黄金作为历史货币的易验证性（throwawaymaths），这从科学和历史两个角度丰富了讨论。

• **godelski的观点**：godelski对政府在Marathon Fusion等项目上的小额投资持积极态度，认为即使失败也能带来有价值的知识，并使这些知识公开化，从而对未来的研究有益。他批评了围绕这些项目的炒作和风险规避行为，认为适度的失败是可以接受的，因为它们提供了学习机会。他还建议增加投资，即使失败也能接受。

• **tbrownaw的观点**：tbrownaw对通过汞合成黄金的方法表示赞赏，特别指出这是一种可能有效处理有害物质汞的方法。

• **throwawaymaths的观点**：throwawaymaths讨论了黄金作为货币的历史价值，认为黄金的价值在于其易于验证的特性，不需要复杂的化学方法，这在古代是一种无需信任的货币形式。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：twic对如何从汞中有效分离出黄金表示怀疑，而PaulHole则通过科幻小说的情节描绘了一个黄金廉价且元素嬗变技术普及的未来。这两种观点在现实与虚构之间形成对比。

• **政府投资与风险**：godelski对小额政府投资持积极态度，认为即使失败也有价值，而对围绕这些项目的炒作和风险规避持批评态度。这与其他讨论者对技术可行性的关注形成对比。

• **黄金的物理性质与验证**：讨论中涉及了金汞合金的物理性质问题（twic）以及黄金作为历史货币的易验证性（throwawaymaths），这从科学和历史两个角度丰富了讨论。

主要讨论点：华盛顿邮报的新闻质量、其持有者贝索斯的动机、以及该报在当前媒体环境下的地位和挑战。

不同观点：
• **skybrian**：认为华盛顿邮报的新闻报道依然质量良好，但其意见栏目没有太大价值，不如Substack上的博客。
• **Animats**：指出华盛顿邮报依赖外部投稿的“意见”板块类似于亚马逊的转售模式，新闻报道多基于新闻稿，实地记者数量不足。仅有少数报道为实际记者采写。
• **dotcoma**：提供了一个外部文章链接，似乎暗示华盛顿邮报正在衰落，但未详细阐述观点。
• **kelseyfrog**：认为贝索斯收购华盛顿邮报是一个注定失败的举动，暗示其长期发展不利。
• **dimal**：提出贝索斯为了保护亚马逊，削弱了华盛顿邮报的意见栏目，并通过向特朗普捐款来化解反垄断威胁。
• **rs186**：认为只要订阅数和收入没有大幅下降，华盛顿邮报的问题就不重要，贝索斯乐见其成。
• **PaulHoule**：认为贝索斯因为害怕特朗普而改变华盛顿邮报的方向，指出在独裁社会中，寡头面临的危险促使贝索斯采取这种策略。
• **scoreandmore**：简短回应，表示同意其他人的观点。
• **VivaTechnics**：简短回应，似乎表示支持某些观点，但未具体说明。

补充讨论：
- **新闻质量与来源**：Animats提出的新闻多来自新闻稿的观点，强调了当前新闻报道中实地记者减少的问题。
- **贝索斯的动机**：dimal和PaulHoule都认为贝索斯在收购华盛顿邮报后的行为受到了政治因素的影响，特别是与特朗普的关系。
- **华盛顿邮报的未来**：kelseyfrog和rs186对华盛顿邮报的未来持不同看法，一个认为收购是失败之举，另一个认为只要财务状况良好，问题就不大。

争议焦点：贝索斯是否为了保护亚马逊而有意削弱了华盛顿邮报的新闻独立性和质量，以及这种行为是否源于对特朗普的畏惧。

data.title: Instrumenting Next.js with runtime secret injection
data.author: nimishk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Next.js 14中使用instrumentation功能在运行时注入密钥。Instrumentation文件（instrumentation.ts/js）可以在Next.js项目启动时运行自定义逻辑，常用于初始化日志或遥测服务。通过这种方式，可以在应用运行时安全地注入和管理密钥，避免将密钥硬编码到代码或.env文件中，从而降低密钥泄露的风险。与.env文件相比，使用密钥管理工具（如Phase、AWS Secrets Manager、HashiCorp Vault）能提供更安全的加密、访问控制和审计功能。文章通过一个实例演示了如何创建instrumentation文件，并在Next.js应用启动时从Phase获取密钥注入到应用中。这种方法提高了应用的可移植性和密钥管理的安全性。

44702627.article_content:
blog
Instrumenting Next.js with runtime secret injection
Leveraging the instrumentation feature in Next.js 14 to inject secrets into applications at runtime.
Rohan
Sunday, July 27, 2025
Copy URL
Photo by EJ Strat
What's an Instrumentation File?
Instrumentation
is a new feature introduced in Next.js 14 that allows you to run custom logic when your application starts.
The
instrumentation.ts/js
file lives at the root of your Next.js project and exposes a
register()
API, which will be called once when a new Next.js server instance is initiated.
Instrumentation is most often used to initiate logging or telemetry services. This example from Vercel's docs shows a basic example of how this works:
//instrumentation.ts
import
{
registerOTel
}
from
'@vercel/otel'
export
function
register
(
)
{
registerOTel
(
'next-app'
)
}
In this example, the
register()
function initializes
OpenTelemetry
for the Next.js application.
Instrumenting with Secrets
As we've seen, the
register()
API is meant primarily for running code at startup and initializing services or tools that can be used later during application runtime. This lends itself nicely as a way to inject secrets into our app. We've discussed the benefits of runtime secret injection, specifically in the context of Next.js in a
previous post
, so have a look at that if you want to know more. The TL;DR is that it keeps secrets out of code, version control, and build artifacts. Runtime secret injection also makes your application more portable and easier to distribute, either within your team or for public consumption.
Why not just use a .env file?
Next.js evaluates (server-side) secrets and environment variables at runtime, if provided as a
.env
file. While this works, it comes with a number of drawbacks, security concerns, and clumsy DX. We've covered this topic in-depth in
another post
, but in short,
.env
files are problematic because they often end up in version control or left lying on local disks unencrypted, increasing the risk of a secret leak. They're nearly impossible to manage securely at scale, are difficult to distribute across a team, and offer no access control or security. Secret management tools offer encryption, access controls, easy collaboration, auditing, and rotation, making them a much safer, scalable, and developer friendly solution.
So let's take a look at how we could use the instrumentation file to inject secrets from a secrets management tool into our Next.js application at runtime.
The Setup
We're going to bootstrap a fresh Next.js project, add an instrumentation file to it, and use a secrets management service to inject secrets into our app at runtime.
I've bootstrapped a Next.js application using
npx create-next-app@latest
and the following options:
[email protected]
Ok to proceed?
(
y
)
y
✔ What is your project named? … instrumentation-demo
✔ Would you like to use TypeScript? … Yes
✔ Would you like to use ESLint? … Yes
✔ Would you like to use Tailwind CSS? … Yes
✔ Would you like your code inside a
`
src/
`
directory? … No
✔ Would you like to use App Router?
(
recommended
)
… Yes
✔ Would you like to use Turbopack
for
`
next dev
`
? … Yes
✔ Would you like to customize the
import
alias
(
`
@/*
`
by default
)
? … No
In this example, we'll be using Phase to inject secrets into our app, but this approach can be adapted to work with any secret management service, such as AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, or even a custom solution.
For this demo, I've created an app on Phase called
instrumentation-demo
with some dummy secrets:
Step 1: Create the Instrumentation File
Create a new file called
instrumentation.ts
at the root of your Next.js project. This file will contain the logic to fetch and inject secrets into your application. If your project uses a different folder structure, such as a
src
directory, you can place the file there. Check out the
Next.js instrumentation documentation
for more details.
>
tree
-L
1
├── app
├── eslint.config.mjs
├── instrumentation.ts 👈
├── next.config.ts
├── next-env.d.ts
├── node_modules
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── postcss.config.mjs
├── public
├── README.md
└── tsconfig.json
In our file, we will export a function called
register()
that will be called when the Next.js server starts. We'll leverage this function to fetch secrets from Phase and inject them into the global scope, making them accessible throughout our application. For now, let's just add a
console.log()
to make sure it's being called correctly when our app starts up:
// instrumentation.ts
export
function
register
(
)
{
console
.
log
(
'Hello world!'
)
}
Start Next.js with
npm run dev
and we can verify that our instrumentation file is working:
▲ Next.js
15.4
.2
(
Turbopack
)
- Local:        http://localhost:3000
- Network:      http://192.168.0.197:3000
✓ Starting
..
.
✓ Compiled instrumentation Node.js
in
13ms
✓ Compiled instrumentation Edge
in
41ms
Hello world
!
✓ Ready
in
1069ms
Note: Instrumentation only runs when the Next server start

data.author: handfuloflight

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于UAP（不明航空现象）报告的可靠性及相关组织的权威性，以及是否存在隐秘的高科技或社会机制来掩盖这些现象。

不同观点：
• **质疑组织的权威性与真实性**：
   - **addaon** 认为该组织缺乏与国家机构的明确关联，因为其联系方式仅为个人电话和邮箱，且仅有简单的网页，怀疑其是否真的具备全国性的存在。同时，质疑其是否会根据报告的地理位置选择性处理信息（如忽略来自加拿大的报告）。
   
• **支持UAP现象存在的观点**：
   - **unidentifiedfly** 引用了NARCAP的报告，详细描述了一次UAP目击事件，包括其运动轨迹、颜色变化以及与商用飞机的互动。该评论者认为这些行为是典型的UFO现象，暗示这些现象可能具有真实性，并与已知物理规律不一致。
   
• **讨论情报机构和私人部门的关系**：
   - **twic** 提到评论中对情报机构（如MI6和MI5）的隐晦提及，指出评论中未明确解释的术语，如"Vauxhall"作为MI6的代称，以及"两岸"（Thames河的两边）指MI6和MI5。这暗示了情报机构与私人部门之间存在某种关系或合作，且可能涉及非公开的操作。
   
• **质疑政府对UAP报告的处理**：
   - **robertclaus** 提出一个简单的问题，质疑政府是否已经在处理这些UAP报告，暗示如果政府已经在处理，那么这些组织的报告是否多余或重复。

• **对UAP和隐秘科技的进一步推测**：
   - **motohagiography** 认为存在与当前物理学理解不一致的交通工具（指UAP），并通过类比加密学和安全领域的历史，指出过去也有类似情况，如ECHELON项目和BULLRUN后门。该评论者推测，UAP可能受到类似于加密领域的隐秘社会机制保护，且随着AI技术的发展，未来可能会有更多关于高级推进技术和能源技术的披露，以保持科技优势。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的NARCAP报告及其细节（如UAP的运动轨迹、颜色变化、雷达无法检测等）提供了支持UAP现象存在的具体例子。
• 关于情报机构的讨论揭示了私人部门与国家情报机构之间可能的复杂关系，以及信息不对称或隐晦表述的问题。
• **synack** 的简短评论（"NARC? Cute."）暗示了对NARCAP组织的不屑或怀疑态度，增加了对该组织权威性的争议性。

争议焦点：  
• UAP现象的真实性及其背后的物理规律是否与现有科学理解一致。
• 相关报告组织（如NARCAP）的权威性与可信度，特别是其是否与国家机构存在正式关联。
• 政府是否已经在处理UAP报告，以及这些非官方组织是否在进行重复或补充的工作。

   - **addaon** 认为该组织缺乏与国家机构的明确关联，因为其联系方式仅为个人电话和邮箱，且仅有简单的网页，怀疑其是否真的具备全国性的存在。同时，质疑其是否会根据报告的地理位置选择性处理信息（如忽略来自加拿大的报告）。
   
• **支持UAP现象存在的观点**：
   - **unidentifiedfly** 引用了NARCAP的报告，详细描述了一次UAP目击事件，包括其运动轨迹、颜色变化以及与商用飞机的互动。该评论者认为这些行为是典型的UFO现象，暗示这些现象可能具有真实性，并与已知物理规律不一致。
   
• **讨论情报机构和私人部门的关系**：
   - **twic** 提到评论中对情报机构（如MI6和MI5）的隐晦提及，指出评论中未明确解释的术语，如"Vauxhall"作为MI6的代称，以及"两岸"（Thames河的两边）指MI6和MI5。这暗示了情报机构与私人部门之间存在某种关系或合作，且可能涉及非公开的操作。
   
• **质疑政府对UAP报告的处理**：
   - **robertclaus** 提出一个简单的问题，质疑政府是否已经在处理这些UAP报告，暗示如果政府已经在处理，那么这些组织的报告是否多余或重复。

• **对UAP和隐秘科技的进一步推测**：
   - **motohagiography** 认为存在与当前物理学理解不一致的交通工具（指UAP），并通过类比加密学和安全领域的历史，指出过去也有类似情况，如ECHELON项目和BULLRUN后门。该评论者推测，UAP可能受到类似于加密领域的隐秘社会机制保护，且随着AI技术的发展，未来可能会有更多关于高级推进技术和能源技术的披露，以保持科技优势。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的NARCAP报告及其细节（如UAP的运动轨迹、颜色变化、雷达无法检测等）提供了支持UAP现象存在的具体例子。
• 关于情报机构的讨论揭示了私人部门与国家情报机构之间可能的复杂关系，以及信息不对称或隐晦表述的问题。

争议焦点：  
• UAP现象的真实性及其背后的物理规律是否与现有科学理解一致。

Maybe the worst state for a company to get in is what I call Mutually Assured Mediocrity.
This is where people are so holistically mid that they agree not to criticize each other for fear of their own mediocrity being found out.
And what’s worse is that leaders on top of MAM organizations are by default mediocre, and most of their signal on performance comes from peers complaining about each other (which doesn’t happen), so they think bad results are just acts of god instead of the obvious outcomes from mediocre teams.
Herein we’ll talk about how to encourage a healthy judgement of one’s coworkers and how to avoid Mutually Assured Mediocrity.
A Sad Story
In the early days of a startup, teams are in survival mode - if you’re not pulling your weight, we’re not sharing food with you. Startups that became successful rarely stifled peer feedback in the early days.
Then you hire more vocations. As you add PM and Design and Product Marketing, you eventually hit your first conflict between these groups. It’s usually an engineer alleging that another vocation is not doing their job because, amongst other reasons, engineers are usually hired first (more tenured).  And then the big lie begins - you don’t understand what we do, stay in your lane.
Your company dies a bit on that day.
Eventually someone again alleges someone is not doing their job, and the leader of the target employee agrees with the assessment, but they’re not gonna let someone who’s never been in their shoes tell them how to run their team. So they drag their feet and nobody does anything about it.
Your company dies a bit more on that day.
Meanwhile, the leaders you’ve hired are trying not to get into fights while ramping up, and your CEO is trying to avoid criticism that they don’t know how to hire executives or manage different kinds of employees. Everyone is trying to avoid being accused of being a fraud; they don’t cast judgement on others to avoid getting judged themselves.
Finally, you get to a place where there’s enough mediocrity that the few truth tellers left start to get punished because they’re the only ones who won’t pretend that standards have fallen.
As then your company is officially dead.
You’ll make it until the last of the good tenured leaders stick around to keep the boats afloat. Eventually the whole company will be mediocre and you achieve a full state of Mutually Assured Mediocrity.
A Different Way
It doesn’t have to be this way. In fact, with the right guidance you can encourage your team to judge their coworkers’ abilities, learn from it, and have it be part of a healthy ecosystem of accountability and growth.
Here’s how to do it.
Ground Rules
First, things fail when people start attacking others directly and publicly. People can disagree in meetings, but people should not be making judgements on their teammates in public. Performance is public, performance management is private. Make it clear to your team that any and all feedback shared on a coworker’s ability is shared either in a private conversation between a person and their own manager, or in the peer feedback section of a performance review.
Second, follow-ups are done privately. There is never the expectation that people are privy to the details of some else’s performance management. That said, if a peer’s performance is causing significant issues for an individual, team, or the business, it may be appropriate to talk about how to work around those issues while performance management is happening.
Finally, you must make clear that nobody is promised a perfect coworker. All teammates are imperfect, and the average action is not termination but coaching. One of the teachable moments in a discussion about peer performance is making clear that people are expected to succeed despite imperfect coworkers; imperfect coworker performance is a reality, not an excuse.
How To Do It
OK, here’s how to productively encourage your team to think about evaluating their coworkers’ performance.
First of all, you should set an expectation that your reports actually have an opinion on their peers’ performance. Sometime in the first few months you should say out loud something like:
We strongly value peer feedback and the ability to understand and evaluate peer performance. As we work together, I’ll periodically ask you how your peers are doing and I’d like you to be able to have thoughtful conversations about it.
Furthermore, if they’re in a leadership position, you might add something like:
It’s quite important that you have a mature opinion on how your cross-functional partners are doing. Please make sure that you’re thinking about the different roles and responsibilities you share, how they are performing, and where you see opportunities for improvement.
Next, you should periodically ask your report (e.g. once every 6-12 months) how they think their peers are doing. This is now when the productive conversation starts.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： co-fermented咖啡的实验及其风味体验

不同观点：
• fleebee认为生产者尝试co-fermented咖啡以寻找新的体验是酷的，但个人体验往往令人失望。他指出，这种咖啡在初次品尝时会让人感到新奇，但后续口感负担较大，风味过于强烈，缺乏清晰度和深度。他将其比作添加水果 adjuncts 的啤酒，认为原材料本身已经具备丰富的表现力，不需要额外发酵水果。

补充讨论：
• fleebee指出，co-fermented咖啡的风味虽然强烈，但在竞赛中可能更具优势，因为其独特性容易引人注意，但在家庭日常饮用中并不理想。他认为发酵过程 delicate，容易导致过度发酵，产生过熟的水果味，掩盖咖啡本身的微妙风味。

• fleebee用啤酒的例子进一步说明，像酵母和啤酒花等原料本身已经能够展现出丰富的香气和风味，如同Flanders red ale无需添加水果即可展现出酸樱桃的风味，这与co-fermented咖啡的情况类似。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于co-fermented咖啡是否真正提升了饮用体验。fleebee认为这种方法虽然创新但往往牺牲了咖啡的清晰度和深度，而其他人可能会觉得这种实验带来的新奇风味是一种值得探索的体验。

data.title: Why does a fire truck cost $2m
data.author: Guid_NewGuid
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了为何消防车价格飙升至200万美元以上。主要原因包括私募股权公司对消防车制造行业的整合，形成了垄断。例如，美国工业合伙公司（AIP）通过收购多家小型企业，创建了REV集团，成为美国三大消防车制造商之一。这导致了生产选择减少、交付时间延长（2至4.5年）以及价格大幅上涨。由于市场控制力增强，厂商可以在下单后更改价格，使得各地消防部门难以负担新车，只能继续使用老旧车辆。例如，芝加哥消防部门的老旧车辆频发故障，其他地区如洛杉矶和亚特兰大的消防部门也面临类似困境。文章指出，这种垄断不仅推高了价格，还加剧了公共安全的风险。

• **其他建议与批评**：

  - **fitsumbelay**：批评公共部门中的腐败和不当行为可能助长了消防车成本的不合理上涨。

- 讨论中多次提到垄断、通货膨胀和疫情对车辆价格和供应链的影响，这些因素共同导致了消防车成本的上升。
- 还提到了不同国家（如中国、德国）制造的消防车可能提供成本更低的选择，这引发了对美国市场现状的反思。
- 最后，讨论中涉及了志愿消防部门在资源有限情况下的艰难处境，强调了设备对社区安全的重要性。

Why does a fire truck cost $2 million?
Why does a fire truck cost $2 million?
Katherine Laidlaw
Katherine Laidlaw
Published:
July 18, 2025
These firefighters just wanted to save lives. Private equity had other ideas
This past Valentine’s Day, a firefighter behind the wheel of an enormous ladder truck felt his brakes give out.
He was driving in the heart of Chicago, on a busy city street, about to lose control of a truck that was supposed to help him save people’s lives. He looked around, panicked. The 25-year-old truck — and the nightmare — picked up speed.
He had three choices: drive into traffic, hit a local grammar school, or plow into the side of a church on the corner. He swerved, narrowly avoiding a pole, and picked the church.
“It was pretty tragic,” says
Pat Cleary
, president of the Chicago Fire Fighters Union Local 2. “We were just happy no one got injured.”
It wouldn’t be the last time something like this happened to one of the departments’ 96 rigs. Weeks later, another truck dropped a rear axle responding to a medical emergency. And in January, the department threw a mock 30th birthday for one of its trucks — it was older than many firefighters on the force.
A birthday cake celebrating D545’s 30th birthday. (Chicago Fire Department/Facebook)
For years, the Chicago fire department has struggled to repair and replace its aging fleet of trucks, the priciest of which now come at a cost of
$2m+
.
And it’s not just in Chicago: Across the fire truck industry, increased consolidation has led to spikes in demand, production delays and sky-high prices, leaving departments nationwide scrambling to provide life-saving services to their citizens.
“There’s a monopoly in the business. They’re taking over,” Cleary says. “Civilians are going to suffer.”
How did we get here?
Emergency vehicles didn’t start out as the custom builds driving down our streets today.
Back in the 1950s, they were largely just trucks outfitted with special add-ons — ladders, pumps — to differentiate them from the vehicle that might deliver your furniture. Family-owned businesses sprung up across the country to serve a region’s specific needs, and competition kept prices low.
Olivia Heller/The Hustle
Fast forward 60 years, and those businesses were contending with aging founders, depleted municipal budgets, and declining fire-truck orders. Sensing an opportunity, a private equity group called American Industrial Partners (AIP) began to roll up the industry.
Wait: what’s a roll up?
It’s when a company buys up a spate of smaller businesses and merges them together to create a conglomerate.
AIP took its bundle and called it the
REV Group

data.title: Blender: Beyond Mouse and Keyboard
data.author: dagmx
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了将Blender软件全面引入多点触控平板设备的计划，如Apple iPad Pro和Microsoft Surface等。目标是让Blender在保持完整功能的同时，适应这些设备的操作特性，提供更任务导向的用户界面，减少信息密度。初期将专注于基础对象操作和雕刻功能，后续加入Grease Pencil和分镜等更复杂的工具。

平板UX面临的挑战包括单窗口全屏工作流、较小的屏幕空间、无键盘鼠标操作、有限的处理能力和电池等。为解决这些问题，Blender将通过扩展输入方式、改进工作区和应用模板来优化用户体验。某些设计改进，如快速收藏编辑器和助手覆盖层，也将惠及桌面用户。开发团队计划先在iPad Pro上测试，之后扩展到Android和其他图形平板。

文章还展示了UI和交互的初步设计模型，强调在有限屏幕空间内提供高效工作环境。
data.comments_summary:
