data.article_summary: NASA面临大规模人才流失，近3,900名员工将通过自愿辞职计划离开，其中包括许多资深人员。在两轮计划中，约3,000人参与了第二轮，870人参与了第一轮。前宇航员John Grunsfeld称此为“人才外流”，离职者多为经验丰富、掌握关键知识的高级员工。NASA的员工总数将从近18,000人减至约14,000人，未来可能进一步削减至11,853人。部分离职人员将退休，其他人可能进入私营部门，尤其是国防承包商。有人担忧这将影响NASA的太空探索任务，如“金色穹顶”项目，一个旨在通过卫星防御导弹的系统。NASA表示将努力保持高效运作，专注于月球和火星探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NASA人才流失及其影响

不同观点：
• **人才流失到国外**：lawlessone和一些其他用户认为，NASA的人才流失将导致这些人最终在欧洲或中国工作，而政府对此会表现得十分震惊。这暗示了对人才外流到国际竞争对手的担忧。
  
• **人才流向私企**：t1234s提出，这些前NASA员工可能会流向像Lockheed、Raytheon这样的私企，继续为NASA的客户做类似的工作，暗示人才并没有真正流失出美国的航天产业。

• **人才流失与机构效率**：Molitor5901认为，NASA一直被期待变得更加精简和高效，而SpaceX等私营公司的快速发展可能对NASA构成了挑战，暗示人才流失或许是机构改革和竞争压力所致。

• **人才流失的影响和机会**：blindriver则从另一个角度提出，NASA的人员流失可能会为新毕业生和现有员工创造晋升机会，暗示人才流失不一定是坏事，可能为机构内部带来新的活力。

• **政治因素影响**：jmclnx指出，政治环境，尤其是特朗普和共和党的政策，使得NASA员工不愿意继续留在该机构工作，暗示政治因素是人才流失的重要原因之一。

补充讨论：
• **预算和资金问题**：ck2提到，五角大楼将大笔资金转移到其他项目上，可能导致包括NASA在内的多个领域的资金短缺，并进一步引发社会问题。这与人才流失问题共同构成了对美国科技和国防领域的广泛担忧。

• **对未来的调侃**：robotburrito以调侃的方式提到AGI（人工通用智能）的发展，暗示在AI快速发展的背景下，传统的人才流失问题可能并不是最紧迫的议题。

• **重复讨论**：BJones12和ChrisArchitect提到该话题在其他地方已有讨论，并提供了链接，表明此话题已在不同平台上被多次提及和讨论。

争议焦点：NASA人才流失的根本原因（政治因素、机构效率、私企竞争）以及其对美国航天事业的实际影响（短期挑战与长期机会）。

44712459.article_content:
Science
6
NASA faces brain drain as thousands exit under voluntary resignation scheme
6
Some heading into retirement, others to private sector
Richard Speed
Mon 28 Jul 2025
//
16:01 UTC
Almost 3,900 of NASA's workforce is set to leave the agency thanks to voluntary incentives, with senior staffers among those heading out the door.
The figures were issued by NASA HQ on Friday. About 3,000 employees opted to take part in a second round of the agency's Deferred Resignation Program. Some 870 participated in the first round, earlier this year.
The exodus has led observers to bemoan the loss of talent. Former Hubble astronaut Dr John Grunsfeld described the departures to
The Register
as "a real brain drain."
He told us that employees who accepted early exit offers tended "to be the most senior people with the most knowledge."
The number of NASA employees leaving is subject to change. Staff could decide to drop out of the buyout programs, or NASA might opt to reject their resignations. However, the headcount reduction has caused alarm.
A letter of dissent titled "The Voyager Declaration," with hundreds of signatures from current and former NASA employees,
said
: "Thousands of NASA civil servant employees have already been terminated, resigned, or retired early, taking with them highly specialized, irreplaceable knowledge crucial to carrying out NASA's mission."
Figures
on NASA's website put the workforce at just under 18,000. The number given in the
FY2026 budget request
is 17,391. A drop of almost 4,000 is therefore substantial. It also calls into question how NASA would manage to continue all its missions should the cuts in the White House's original budget proposal be unpicked by lawmakers.
A NASA spokesperson told us:
"NASA's Deferred Resignation Program, Voluntary Early Retirement Authority, and Voluntary Separation Incentive Program closed July 25. Safety remains a top priority for our agency as we balance the need to become a more streamlined and more efficient organization and work to ensure we remain fully capable of pursuing a Golden Era of exploration and innovation, including to the Moon and Mars.
Numbers are as follows:
Deferred Resignation Program #1: about 4.8% of the workforce (about 870 individuals)
Deferred Resignation Program #2 (including VERA and VSIP, in addition to DRP): about 16.4% of the workforce, approximately 3,000 employees<
NASA's expected remaining civil servant workforce following both DRP programs, as well as normal attrition (about 500) over the same time period: about 14,000
The final number could well fluctuate in the coming days, based on factors including a departure approved beyond January 9, 2026, as well as the employee withdrawing from the process or the resignation not being approved."
Further cuts will be necessary if the agency is to reduce its workforce to the 11,853 level outlined in the agency's FY2026 budget request.
The real reason why Trump is killing the Mauna Loa observatory in Hawai'i
NASA Goddard Center Director quits as agency staffers issue dissent letter
Thousands of NASA senior staffers expected to quit after budget slashed
Former reality TV star appointed NASA interim administrator
It is unclear where all those staff will go. Some will opt for retirement. Others, according to Grunsfeld, might head into the private sector. "Probably a lot of them will go to defense contractors and work on the 'Golden Dome'... Which is a doomed project."
The
Golden Dome
is a proposal to protect the US from foreign threats, including ballistic missiles, via a constellation of satellites. Its cost far exceeds NASA's proposed budget.
"I'm sure a lot of interesting technology will come out of it," said Grunsfeld, "but we've done this before with Star Wars."
"Star Wars" was a media-coined nickname for the US's Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI), announced in 1983 by President Ronald Reagan. While SDI did not deliver as initially envisioned, the dream of a space-based missile defense system has not gone away, and thanks to NASA's cuts, there could soon be a wave of scientists available to try to make the latest dream a reality.
"Can you imagine a constellation of weaponized satellites orbiting the Earth?" said Grunsfeld. "A constellation of sensor satellites orbiting the Earth that are looking for missile launches and trying to track missile launches?"
"In a world with aircraft and commercial rocket launches and everything else controlled by AI... What could go wrong?"
The Register
asked NASA to comment. ®

data.article_summary: 《Aeneas：改变历史学家连接过去方式的新模型》介绍了一种名为Aeneas的人工智能模型，旨在帮助历史学家更好地解释、归因和修复古罗马铭文。该模型通过在海量拉丁铭文间寻找文本和上下文相似性，加速了传统上复杂且耗时的对比工作，并能处理多模态输入，如文字和图像，以确定铭文的地理来源。Aeneas还能修复未知长度的文本空白，并在恢复和断代 damaged texts方面达到了先进水平。该模型基于一个包含超过17.6万条拉丁铭文的大型数据集进行训练，并与诺丁汉大学等多所高校合作开发。Aeneas不仅适用于铭文，还能扩展至其他古代语言和媒介，如纸草和钱币。研究团队将提供免费的互动版本和开源代码，以促进更多研究。

主要讨论点：对新技术在历史研究中应用的看法

不同观点：
• [bpodgursky] 认为这个发现带有一定的讽刺意味，因为罗马的埃涅阿斯故事本质上是一种政治宣传，用来创造民族创始叙事。这暗示了他对历史叙事真实性的质疑，以及对利用技术还原历史文本的复杂态度。

• [bawana] 对技术的实际应用表示怀疑，并通过反问语气表达了对该技术能否完整还原古希腊石刻文字及其年代的疑惑，显示出对技术能力边界的关心。

• [ViktorRay] 对这一新技术表示赞赏，认为它将为历史学家的研究工作带来便利，显示出对技术进步在历史研究中积极作用的认可。

补充讨论：
• bpodgursky 的评论引入了对历史叙事的批判性思考，特别是关于历史如何被政治化地构建，这为讨论增添了历史与政治宣传关系的维度。
• bawana 的质疑揭示了人们对新技术实际效果和可靠性的关注，尤其是在处理复杂和不完整的古代遗迹时。
• ViktorRay 的积极评价强调了技术进步在简化和加速历史研究方面的潜在好处，代表了技术乐观派的观点。

争议焦点：
• 该技术的实际应用效果和可靠性是讨论中的一个潜在争议点，特别是在面对历史文本的复杂性和历史叙事的政治背景时。

44672230.article_content:
Research
Aeneas transforms how historians connect the past
Published
23 July 2025
Authors
The Aeneas team
Share
Copy link
×
Introducing the first model for contextualizing ancient inscriptions, designed to help historians better interpret, attribute and restore fragmentary texts.
Writing was everywhere in the Roman world — etched onto everything from imperial monuments to everyday objects. From political graffiti, love poems and epitaphs to business transactions, birthday invitations and magical spells, inscriptions offer modern historians rich insights into the diversity of everyday life across the Roman world.
Often, these texts are fragmentary, weathered or deliberately defaced. Restoring, dating and placing them is nearly impossible without contextual information, especially when comparing similar inscriptions.
Today, we’re publishing a
paper
in Nature introducing
Aeneas
, the first artificial intelligence (AI) model for contextualizing ancient inscriptions.
When working with ancient inscriptions, historians traditionally rely on their expertise and specialized resources to identify “parallels” — which are texts that share similarities in wording, syntax, standardized formulas or provenance.
Aeneas greatly accelerates this complex and time-consuming work. It reasons across thousands of Latin inscriptions, retrieving textual and contextual parallels in seconds that allow historians to interpret and build upon the model’s findings.
Pause video
Play video
Our model can also be adapted to other ancient languages, scripts and media, from papyri to coinage, expanding its capabilities to help draw connections across a wider range of historical evidence.
We co-developed Aeneas with the University of Nottingham, and in partnership with researchers at the Universities of Warwick, Oxford and Athens University of Economics and Business (AUEB). This work was part of a wider effort to explore how generative AI can help historians better identify and interpret parallels at scale.
We want this research to benefit as many people as possible, so we’re making an interactive version of Aeneas freely-available to researchers, students, educators, museum professionals and more at
predictingthepast.com
. To support further research, we’re also open-sourcing
our code and dataset
.
Aeneas’ advanced capabilities
Named after the wandering hero of Graeco-Roman mythology, Aeneas builds upon
Ithaca
, our earlier work using AI to restore, date and place ancient Greek inscriptions.
Aeneas goes a step further, helping historians interpret and contextualize a text, give meaning to isolated fragments, draw richer conclusions and piece together a better understanding of ancient history.
Our model’s advanced capabilities include:
Parallels search:
It searches for parallels across a vast collection of Latin inscriptions. By turning each text into a kind of historical fingerprint, Aeneas identifies deep connections that can help historians situate inscriptions within their broader historical context.
Processing multimodal input:
Aeneas is the first model to determine a text's geographical provenance using multimodal inputs. It analyzes both text and visual information, like images of an inscription.
Restoring gaps of unknown length:
For the first time, Aeneas can restore gaps in texts where the missing length is unknown. This makes it a more versatile tool for historians dealing with heavily damaged material.
State-of-the-art performance:
Aeneas sets a new state-of-the-art benchmark in restoring damaged texts and predicting when and where they were written.
Animation of a restored bronze military diploma from Sardinia 113/14 C.E. (
CIL
XVI, 60).
How Aeneas works
Aeneas is a multimodal generative neural network that takes an inscription’s text and image as input. To train Aeneas, we curated a large and reliable dataset, drawing from decades of work by historians to create digital collections, especially the
Epigraphic Database Roma
(EDR),
Epigraphic Database Heidelberg
(EDH) and
Epigraphic Database Clauss Slaby
(EDCS-ELT).
We cleaned, harmonized and linked these records into a single machine-actionable dataset that we refer to as the
Latin Epigraphic Dataset
(LED), comprising over 176,000 Latin inscriptions from across the ancient Roman world.
Our model uses a transformer-based decoder to process the textual input of an inscription. Specialized networks handle character restoration and dating using text, while geographical attribution also uses images of the inscriptions as input. The decoder retrieves similar inscriptions from the LED, ranked by relevance.
For each inscription, Aeneas’ contextualization mechanism retrieves a list of parallels using a technique called “embeddings” — encoding the textual and contextual information of each inscription into a kind of historical fingerprint containing details of what the text says, its language, when and where it came from, and how it relates to other inscriptions.
Diagram of Aeneas’ architecture

data.title: Principles for production AI agents
data.author: carlotasoto
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了在agentic开发中积累的六条简单经验，旨在帮助新手快速上手。主要原则包括：

1. **投资系统提示**：提供清晰、详细的上下文，避免模糊和矛盾，无需复杂技巧。可以使用LLM生成初始草稿，再人工优化。
   
2. **分割上下文**：提供最小必要知识，通过工具获取更多上下文，避免模型产生幻觉或偏离主题。使用简单的上下文压缩工具帮助管理。

3. **精心设计工具**：工具应接口直观、功能集中、参数严格，避免过多选项导致上下文混乱。工具设计应考虑幂等性，类似于为分心的开发者设计API。

这些原则旨在优化LLM代理的性能和效率，使其更可靠地执行任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在评估和工具调用中的应用与有效性

不同观点：
• roadside_picnic 认为评估（evaluations）在改进AI工具和系统性能中至关重要。他质疑“LLM作为批评者”（LLM as critic）的方法，表示在其工作经验中，LLM在此角色上的表现并不理想，且缺乏有效的实证支持。他强调需要基本的评估作为比较基准。

• prats226 提出在工具调用中，通常只指定函数的输入，而不指定预期的输出类型。他建议，在DSL风格的代理中，如果提供有关调用函数所需的结构化输入信息以及预期的输出信息，可能会带来更好的规划效果。

• SrslyJosh 对上述讨论持简短的否定态度，仅回复“不要这样做。”（"Don't."），暗示对使用LLM作为批评者或进行特定调用的反对或 cautionary stance。

• carlotasoto 没有直接参与讨论，但其用户名下的评论可能暗示其关注从构建生产性代理系统中获取实际经验，这与讨论主题相关。

补充讨论：
• roadside_picnic 的评论中提到了实际工作中的实验结果，表明LLM在作为批评者时的表现并不理想，但没有详细描述具体实验细节。
• prats226 的观点引入了DSL风格代理的概念，强调了结构化输入输出信息对规划的重要性，可能为提高LLM在工具调用中的效果提供了一种思路。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM作为批评者的有效性，以及在工具调用中如何更好地利用结构化信息以提高模型表现。

总结：讨论围绕LLM在评估和工具调用中的应用展开，涉及对其有效性的质疑和改进建议，特别是在提供结构化信息以优化模型规划方面的潜在策略。

44712315.article_content:
Every now and then, people ask me:
“
I am new to agentic development, I’m building something, but I feel like I'm missing some tribal knowledge. Help me catch up!
”.
I’m tempted to suggest some serious stuff like multiweek courses (e.g. by
HuggingFace
or
Berkeley
), but not everyone is interested in that level of diving.
So I decided to gather six simple empirical learnings that helped me a lot during
app.build
development. This post is somewhat inspired by
Design Decisions Behind app.build
, but is generalized and aimed to be a quick guideline for newcomers in agentic engineering.
Principle 1: Invest in your system prompt
I’ve been skeptical about prompt engineering for a long time, it seemed more like shaman rituals rather than anything close to engineering. All those approaches “
I will tip you $100
” or “
My grandmother is dying and needs this
” or “
Be 100% accurate or else
” could be useful as local fluctuation leveraging local model inefficiency, but never worked in the longer run.
I changed my mind regarding prompt / context engineering when I realized a simple thing: modern LLMs just need direct detailed context, no tricks, but clarity and lack of contradictions. That’s it, no manipulation needed. Models are good at instruction following, and the problem is often just the ambiguous nature of the instructions.
All LLM providers have educational resources on best practices on how to prompt their models (e.g.,
one by Anthropic
and
one by Google
). Just follow them and ensure your instructions are direct and detailed, no smart-pants tricks required. For example, here is a
system prompt
we use to make Claude generate rules for
ast-grep
- nothing tricky, just details on how to use the tool that the agent barely knows.
One trick we like is to bootstrap the initial system prompt with the draft created by Deep Research-like variants of LLM. It typically needs human improvements, but is a solid baseline.
Keeping a shared part of the context is beneficial for the
prompt caching
mechanisms. Technically, one can cache user messages too, but structuring context so that the system part is large and static and user one is small and dynamic works great.
Principle 2: Split the context
Alright, a solid system prompt is here. But there is a reason why "context engineering" has been the latest trend over "prompt engineering".
Context management is a subject for a trade-off. Without proper context, models tend to hallucinate, get off track or just refuse to provide an answer with a too large context. They’re subject to attention attrition (where models struggle to focus on relevant parts of very long contexts, leading to degraded performance on key details buried in the middle), higher costs and latency.
A principle we found useful is to provide the bare minimum of knowledge in the first place, and the option to fetch more context if needed via tools. For example, in our case it may mean listing all the project files in the prompt and providing a tool to read the files that are relevant for the requested change; although if we’re certain some file content is crucial, we can include its content in the context in advance.
Logs and other artifacts from the feedback loop can bloat the context pretty quickly. Simple
context compaction
tools applied automatically can help a lot. Encapsulation was a hype word for object-oriented programming, but for context management it is even more important: separate the concerns, and provide every bit of your agentic solution only the context it absolutely needs.
Principle 3: Design tools carefully
The core feature of an AI agent is
tool calling
, the combination of an LLM + exposed tools + basic control flow operators makes an agent.
Designing a toolset for the agent is somewhat similar to designing an API… but actually more complex. Human API users are more capable of reading between the lines, can navigate complex docs and find workarounds. Tools created for agents are usually more limited (having too many of them is a way to pollute the context), should have direct straightforward interfaces and overall bring order to the stochastic LLM world. When building for a human user, it may be fine to design one main road and some tricks for corner cases; LLMs are very likely to misuse your loopholes, and that’s why you don’t want to have any loopholes.
Good tools typically operate on a similar level of granularity, and have a limited number of strictly typed parameters. They are focused and well-tested, like an API you’re ready to provide to a smart but distractible junior developer. Idempotency is highly recommended to avoid state management issues. Most software engineering agents have under 10 multifunctional tools (such as read_file, write_file, edit_file, execute…) with 1-3 parameters each (
appbuild example
,
opencode example
), and attaching additional tools based on context
may be suitable too
.

data.title: Real-Time Messaging: Speed and Context
data.author: ahstilde
data.article_summary: GrowthLoop推出了实时消息功能，旨在帮助营销团队在关键时刻通过各种渠道与客户互动。该功能允许在单一画布上结合实时触发和生命周期旅程，利用云数据进行个性化跟进，无需批量ETL。借助事件流（如Kafka），营销人员可以快速发送基于完整客户背景（如购买历史和忠诚度状态）的个性化消息，而无需数据仓库。该功能与现有工具和渠道无缝集成，支持电子邮件、短信、推送通知等多种方式，帮助营销团队提高效率和灵活性，同时保持数据治理。通过实时消息，企业可以在高意图时刻提供精准的客户体验，从而增加收入和忠诚度。

Introducing Real-time Messaging: Speed and context together in one canvas
Introducing Real-time Messaging: Speed and context together in one canvas
Orchestrate journeys that engage users at exactly the right moment, across every channel, powered by your own data.
written by
Swati Teerdhala
Blog
Product
Introducing Real-time Messaging: Speed and context together in one canvas
Key Takeaways:
Our new feature, Real-time Messaging, enables you to engage customers in their highest intent moments, without waiting on batch ETLs.Â
Marketers can combine real-time triggers with lifecycle journeys in one single journey canvas, and use cloud data for personalized follow-ups.
Real-time Messaging uses event streams like Kafka, no warehousing required.Â
By orchestrating on top of your data cloud, GrowthLoop gives marketing teams speed and flexibility, while data teams retain full governance.
Real-time Messaging works seamlessly with your existing tools and channels, making it easy to activate across email, SMS, push, and more.
Table of Contents
Example H2
Building meaningful customer connections is the core of great marketing. It starts with knowing your customers well and understanding their preferences enough to deliver relevant, personalized experiences across channels. But to really cap it off, you need one more thing. Perfect timing.Â
Thatâs why GrowthLoop is launching
Real-time Messaging
as a part of Universal Journeys.
â
Imagine being greeted with a discount for the shoes you were browsing online, the moment you step into that brandâs store. Thereâs no chance youâre forgetting that experience, or that brand.
Whether itâs knowing when theyâve purchased from your brand for the first time or that theyâve signed up for your newsletter, a well-timed message at the exact right moment, in real-time, can be the difference between a lifelong customer and one who moves on.Â
Real-time and composable data havenât been friends
Traditionally, marketing in real-time has faced one major challenge: context. Marketers face a frustrating tradeoff between two incomplete solutions.
Deliver fast, generic messages powered by incomplete and fragmented data?Â
Or send personalized offers that are slowed down by disconnected data across marketing tools?Â
Either way, marketers have been forced to choose between speed and context.
Marketing clouds can handle speed in the form of real-time marketing across channels. But they lack access to deeper data from your data cloud
that gives marketers the full picture of your customer
, like purchase history or loyalty status. As standalone SaaS platforms, theyâre built separately from your existing data infrastructure, which means that they canât query your warehouse directly, adding latency and data duplication.Â
Without contextual personalization from the data cloud, a VIP customer might get the same message as a first-time customer, creating a disconnected, negative experience that could lead to churn.Â
Reverse ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) tools have access to your enterprise cloud and allow your marketing team to access the most critical customer data, with information like transaction history, engagement, and demographic attributes. But these tools also rely on batch data processing to sync that cloud data into your marketing orchestration tools, and these ETLs are usually scheduled at night, once a day. This is great for data accuracy and reporting, but not as much for reacting to customer events in the moment.
By the time the data has synced to your marketing orchestration tool, itâs stale â and worse, the moment of high intent has passed. Your customer is gone, and your ability to deliver the perfect message is too late to matter, resulting in lost revenue.
Over time, continuously missing opportunities to deliver the personalized, customer-centric experiences that drive revenue and loyalty adds up.
We believe that thereâs a better way to leverage speed and data context, together.
Introducing Real-time MessagingÂ
Finally, you can send the right messages at the right moment, across channels â all powered by your first-party data and built on top of your existing data cloud.Â
Real-time Messaging combines instant triggers and lifecycle marketing in one unified journey canvas. Marketers finally have the flexibility to trigger messages in seconds, without complex workarounds or custom engineering,Â  while relying on their own data to add the
personalization
and relevancy that drives purchases, brand affinity, and loyalty.Â
All-in-one journey orchestration

data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在macOS上使用类似Linux `strace`的工具进行调试，主要涉及使用Apple的Endpoint Security框架。关键工具包括`eslogger`，它可以记录系统事件，并支持通过命令行监控特定事件（如文件操作和进程执行）。可以通过`eslogger`结合`jq`处理JSON格式输出，例如列出被执行的文件路径。此外，Homebrew提供了`FileMonitor`和`ProcessMonitor`等工具用于文件和进程监控。所有这些工具都基于同一框架，结果类似。文中还提到了一些开源应用如`Crescendo`和`Red Canary Mac Monitor`。

command line

sudo eslogger stat |

data.title: Measles isn't just dangerous, it may erase your immune system
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了麻疹的严重危害，尤其是它可能削弱甚至消除人体免疫记忆，导致感染过其他疾病后再次失去免疫力。麻疹不仅会导致失明、肺炎、严重腹泻，甚至死亡，还可能通过“麻疹健忘症”现象，减少免疫细胞的数量和多样性，使儿童更容易感染其他疾病。研究表明，麻疹疫苗不仅能预防麻疹，还能通过“非特异性效应”增强整体免疫力，防止其他传染病的发生。由于疫苗犹豫和免疫活动的缺失，全球麻疹病例正在上升。文章呼吁重视麻疹疫苗接种，以保护儿童免受多种疾病的威胁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：麻疹对患有自身免疫疾病人群的影响

不同观点：
• more_corn 表示担心麻疹对患有自身免疫疾病的人可能会有更严重的影响，但未给出具体例子或数据，只是表达了一种担忧。
• [潜在回应观点] 有人可能会认为麻疹是一种病毒，对所有免疫系统较弱的人都会造成更大威胁，不仅仅是自身免疫疾病患者，例如HIV患者或正在接受化疗的人也面临高风险。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于麻疹对不同免疫系统状况的人群影响程度是否有足够的医学证据支持。目前对麻疹的关注主要集中在其高传染性和对免疫系统较弱人群的潜在严重后果。
• more_corn 的评论引发了对特定人群在面对麻疹感染时的脆弱性的关注，但尚未提供具体论据或数据支持其观点。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点包括麻疹是否对免疫系统异常的人群有更长期的影响，如引发其他并发症或导致自身免疫疾病的恶化等。

44712725.article_content:
July 16, 2025
The GIST
Measles isn't just dangerous, it may erase your immune system
by Antony Black,
The Conversation
edited by
Gaby Clark
, 																								reviewed by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
trusted source
written by researcher(s)
proofread
Credit: Nataliya Vaitkevich from Pexels
Blindness, pneumonia, severe diarrhea and even death—measles virus infections, especially in children, can have devastating consequences. Fortunately, we have a safe and effective defense. Measles vaccines are estimated to have averted more than
60 million deaths
between 2000 and 2023.
Yet despite this success,
measles cases
are
rising sharply
in the UK and around the world. This global surge is the result of several factors, from
vaccine hesitancy to missed immunization campaigns
, leaving many children unprotected and vulnerable.
But there's more at stake than just measles itself. Emerging research suggests that the measles vaccination may offer surprising additional health benefits. Children who receive the vaccine have been shown to have a significantly
lower risk of infections
from diseases unrelated to measles.
One explanation for this broader benefit is the idea of "measles amnesia." This refers to the ability of the measles virus to erase parts of the body's
immune memory
.
Our immune system contains various cells that protect us from infections. Some produce antibodies that neutralize viruses, while others detect and destroy infected cells. Immune memory allows the body to "remember" past infections and mount faster responses in the future.
However,
measles infection may reduce
the number and diversity of these memory cells—leaving children vulnerable to a wide range of diseases they had previously developed immunity to. In other words, the virus doesn't just make children ill in the short term, it may also undo years of immune protection.
In one study, researchers found that between
11% and 73% of antibodies
targeting other diseases were lost after a measles
infection
in unvaccinated children. This immune depletion was not observed in children who had received the vaccine, suggesting that vaccination protects against this damaging effect.
This broad loss of immune protection may explain why measles outbreaks are often followed by spikes in other infectious diseases. Ongoing studies are exploring the impact of measles amnesia in regions such as
West Africa
, where measles and other infections remain widespread.
A vaccine that does more?
Another theory for the vaccine's broader benefit is known as the "non-specific effect." Unlike measles amnesia, which explains how the virus weakens immunity, the non-specific effect suggests that the measles vaccine actively strengthens the immune system against a wide range of pathogens.
Recent research has shown that measles vaccination may
enhance the function
of certain immune cells, making them more effective at fighting off other diseases. Some scientists believe this effect, rather than protection against amnesia alone, could be the primary reason why vaccinated children have better overall health outcomes.
The measles vaccine is a
live attenuated vaccine
, which means it uses a weakened version of the virus to stimulate a strong immune response. Live vaccines, including the BCG vaccine for tuberculosis, are known to provide
broad immune training effects
, which may explain this non-specific protection.
Forgotten the dangers
In the 1960s, before widespread vaccination, measles caused around
2.6 million deaths per year
. It's hard to imagine today, but that's partly the problem.
As measles became rare,
society began to forget
how serious it is. We forgot how contagious it is (one infected person can spread the virus to up to 90% of nearby unvaccinated people) and we forgot how effective vaccination is (
two doses
provide more than 90% long-term protection).
And in some circles, this fading memory has been replaced by something more dangerous: mistrust. Misinformation, vaccine myths, and anti-vaccine rhetoric are spreading, just like the
virus
itself.
So, whether the additional protection offered by the vaccine is due to prevention of immune amnesia, a non-specific immune boost, or both, the takeaway is the same: Vaccinate children against measles. Because when we protect them from
measles
, we may also be protecting them from so much more.

主要讨论点：图书馆是否应支付高额费用获取数字版权，还是可以通过自行数字化纸质书来实现更经济的操作

不同观点：
• **Lesuorac的观点**：认为图书馆花费50美元购买数字副本是不必要的支出。他建议图书馆可以购买纸质书并自行数字化，以降低成本和提高操作便利性。他提到AI公司有关格式转换的法律诉讼，暗示这种做法在法律上可能得到支持。

• **Bookofjoe的观点**（通过提供的链接暗示）：Bookofjoe提供了一个存档链接，可能是在支持或补充Lesuorac的观点，表明有资源可以辅助了解关于数字化和格式转换的法律问题。这暗示了对Lesuorac观点的法律可行性的认同或提供进一步的信息支持。

补充讨论：
• **法律问题**：Lesuorac提到了AI公司面临的法律诉讼，这些诉讼可能在确立格式转换的合法性。这表明Lesuorac认为图书馆自行数字化纸质书可能受到这些法律判例的保护，从而在法律上可行。

• **经济性与便利性**：Lesuorac强调了通过自行数字化纸质书可能带来的经济优势和操作便利性，这表明他关注的是图书馆预算的有效使用和为读者提供更便捷的服务。

争议焦点：
• 自行数字化的合法性：Lesuorac的观点基于格式转换的法律可行性，但这一点可能存在争议，因为不同国家和地区对版权和数字化的法律规定可能不同。

• 数字版权的价值：图书馆支付高额费用获取数字版权的原因可能包括对合法性和内容提供者权益的尊重，这与通过自行数字化实现经济性的观点形成对比。

总结：讨论的核心在于图书馆是否可以通过自行数字化纸质书来替代购买昂贵的数字版权，涉及到法律、经济和操作便利性等多个方面。Lesuorac主张自行数字化，并引用法律诉讼来支持其观点，而Bookofjoe提供的链接可能进一步探讨这一策略的可行性。

总结：讨论的核心在于图书馆是否可以通过自行数字化纸质书来替代购买昂贵的数字版权，涉及到法律、经济和操作便利性等多个方面。Lesuorac主张自行数字化，并引用法律诉讼来支持其观点，而Bookofjoe提供的链接可能进一步探讨这一策略的可行性。

data.title: Linux dev quits after "personal attacks" from user over antivirus tool
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Kapitano, a Linux GUI frontend for the ClamAV antivirus engine, has been discontinued due to personal attacks and harsh words directed at its developer, zynequ. The issue began when a user reported false positives allegedly caused by Kapitano, but the developer explained that the problem lay with ClamAV itself, not the frontend. The user escalated the situation, accusing zynequ of being a "malicious actor" and demanding the project be blocked. Despite zynequ's efforts to clarify, the conflict led to the developer abandoning the project. Kapitano's code has been released into the public domain, and the project will be delisted from Flathub. The incident highlights the challenges faced by open-source developers dealing with online harassment.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术论坛中的不良行为及其应对方式

• **gruez** 和 **riffic** 对“Linux开发者”（Linux dev）的定义提出异议，指出在讨论中应明确区分“为Linux开发软件的人”和“Linux内核贡献者”，以避免混淆。

44711788.article_content:
Kapitano was a tool with a simple job: to give the ClamAV scanning engine a modern face on Linux. It relied on the ClamAV database, a massive, constantly updated list used to sniff out all sorts of nasties like viruses, worms, and Trojan horses.
Since
ClamAV is primarily a command-line tool
, it depends on a GUI (frontend) for users who prefer not to live in the terminal. There are apps like ClamWin on Windows, ClamXav on Mac, and, until recently, Kapitano on Linux.
Screenshot of Kapitano
Now, the dev behind the Linux frontend, "zynequ," has marked the project as "Not Maintained" following what they described as personal attacks and harsh words.
It all started when a user created an issue on the project's Codeberg page with the title, "Kaptiano resulted in 24 positives- for win.exploits and Trojans." In the post, they claimed the antivirus frontend was generating false positives on their Linux Mint system.
The user noted that all the flagged files were related to the Kapitano Flatpak itself and ended with a rather aggressive warning. The whole thing seemed "strange," they said, concluding with, "program has ZERO reviews, and should remain that way until source code is verified by an independent source. DO NOT DOWNLOAD!"
Zynequ, the project's author, responded by
calmly referencing the wiki
and
explaining that the problem
was with ClamAV itself, not his application. Kapitano, built with GTK4 and
libadwaita
, is just a wrapper that sends commands to the
clamscan
utility but has no say in what gets flagged.
For reference, this is the code that is related to your concerns:
https://codeberg.org/zynequ/Kapitano/src/branch/stable/src/utils/clamav.py
On method
scan_for_malware
and
update_malware_definitions
, you can see that it just calls
clamscan
and
freshclam
.
The developer also called the user out for the "personal attacks" and addressed the zero reviews situation, pointing out that this was hardly a conspiracy since the project was very new, having launched back in June. They insisted that there is nothing "fishy" about their code and that it is fully open for review.
Things escalated from there. After Zynequ closed the issue, the user created a duplicate one, then proceeded to
resubmit the complaint under issue #13
, this time with a different title: Kapitano developer is a malicious actor. Get this malware distributor blocked.
After a heated back and forth with the dev, the user finally posted, "Your project is off of my laptop disk. Let it rest. Goodbye."
This exchange is what led to the zynequ
publishing their final note
. They explained that Kapitano was "a hobby project, created in my free time without any financial support," and that it's hard to stay motivated when "personal attacks" are directed towards you.
I'm sorry to say that this project is no longer being maintained.
Recently, I had an unpleasant experience [...], where I was accused of distributing malware. Although I explained that the issue wasn't caused by the app, the conversation escalated into personal attacks and harsh words directed at me.
This was always a hobby project, created in my free time without any financial support. Incidents like this make it hard to stay motivated. That said, I'm genuinely grateful to everyone who tried the app, and I appreciate the attention it received.
Zynequ noted that the project's code was now released into the public domain under The Unlicense, meaning anyone could fork it and do whatever they want with it. Kapitano will be delisted from Flathub, and the
Codeberg repo
will still be alive for a few months before they delete it and close their account for good.

data.title: FCC Paramount/Skydance Decision Redoes Broadcast Journalism by Bureaucratic Fiat
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: Paramount同意支付1600万美元以解决特朗普提起的指控其编辑采访视频的诉讼，与此同时，特朗普任命的联邦通信委员会（FCC）主席布兰登·卡尔（Brendan Carr）正审查Paramount与Skydance Media的合并案。尽管卡尔声称Paramount的和解与合并案无关，但FCC随后批准了这笔80亿美元的交易。拜登任命的委员安娜·戈麦斯（Anna Gomez） dissent指出，这起和解和合并批准时机可疑，并质疑FCC借此干涉新闻自由。法律专家批评FCC的行为违宪，认为政府不应控制媒体的编辑决策。卡尔则辩称，这些措施旨在提高新闻公正性和透明度，并表示FCC有权确保广播公司符合公共利益。批评者认为，卡尔的做法实质上是扩大政府对媒体的控制，违背言论自由原则。

44711607.article_content:
A few weeks ago, Paramount, which owns CBS, announced that it would pay $16 million to settle a
laughable lawsuit
in which President Donald Trump claimed the network had committed consumer fraud by editing a pre-election interview with former Vice President Kamala Harris to make her seem "less dumb." It was a striking surrender, especially since CBS had accurately
described
Trump's claims as "completely without merit." But Brendan Carr, the Trump-appointed chairman of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), insisted that the settlement had nothing to do with his agency's review of Paramount's pending merger with Skydance Media.
On Thursday, the FCC
announced
that it had approved that $8 billion business deal. By Carr's account, the timing of that decision was entirely coincidental. But FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez, a Joe Biden appointee, had a different take.
"I cannot support this order approving this transaction in light of the payout and other troubling concessions Paramount made to settle a baseless lawsuit," Gomez
said
in her dissent. "After months of cowardly capitulation to this Administration, Paramount finally got what it wanted. Unfortunately, it is the American public who will ultimately pay the price for its actions. In an unprecedented move, this once-independent FCC used its vast power to pressure Paramount to broker a private legal settlement and further erode press freedom."
In addition to its suspicious timing, the FCC's approval of the Paramount/Skydance deal was contingent on concessions regarding CBS news coverage. Those constitutionally questionable conditions confirm that Carr is
determined
to curb freedom of the press by asserting government control over the content of broadcast journalism.
"This has been an unconstitutional shakedown from start to finish,"
said
Will Creeley, legal director at the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression. "Per the First Amendment, federal law, and longstanding precedent, the FCC has no business dictating the editorial choices of media outlets or conditioning merger approval on the viewpoints a network chooses to air….No federal bureaucrat should ever be allowed to play-act as our nation's editor-in-chief."
Paramount needed the FCC's approval for the merger because it entailed the transfer of broadcast licenses held by CBS-owned stations. Under the
Communications Act of 1934
, the question was whether those transfers were "consistent with the public interest, convenience, and necessity." As Carr sees it, that standard requires assurances that licensees will cover the news in a way that he deems fair, accurate, and balanced.
"Americans no longer trust the legacy national news media to report fully, accurately, and fairly," Carr
said
in a press release. "It is time for a change. That is why I welcome Skydance's commitment to make significant changes at the once storied CBS broadcast network."
In particular, Carr said, "Skydance has made written commitments to ensure that the new company's programming embodies a diversity of viewpoints from across the political and ideological spectrum. Skydance will also adopt measures that can root out the bias that has undermined trust in the national news media. These commitments, if implemented, would enable CBS to operate in the public interest and focus on fair, unbiased, and fact-based coverage. Doing so would begin the process of earning back Americans' trust."
Skydance also
agreed
to "have in place an ombudsman who reports to the President of New Paramount, who will receive and evaluate any complaints of bias or other concerns involving CBS." It says "New Paramount's executive leadership will carefully consider any such complaints in overseeing CBS's news programming." Carr's press release also touted that concession, which he said will "promote transparency and increased accountability."
Carr, in other words, thinks it is entirely appropriate for federal regulators to demand "significant changes" in the way news organizations operate, including what they cover, how they cover it, the sources they interview, the people they invite to comment on current events, and the way they respond to complaints of bias. He is explicitly setting the FCC up as an arbiter of good journalism.
That power grab is consistent with Carr's
understanding
of the government's role in the marketplace of ideas, which he thinks should include
restricting
the editorial discretion of social media platforms in the name of "reining in Big Tech" and preventing "discrimination against core political viewpoints." Carr, an
avowed free speech champion
, presents his concerns about broadcast news bias in similar terms,
saying
"a handful of national programmers" should not "control and dictate to the American what the narrative is, what they can say, what they can think." As with his vendetta against "Big Tech," he perversely portrays government interference with private editorial decisions as a victory for freedom of speech.

data.title: Return of wolves to Yellowstone has led to a surge in aspen trees
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 1995年，狼被重新引入黄石公园，此前它们因栖息地丧失、人类猎杀和政府的消灭计划而在1930年从公园消失。狼的消失导致麋鹿数量失控增长，过度啃食植被，尤其是白杨树，使得新树苗无法生长。到1990年代，黄石北部的白杨树苗几乎绝迹。狼重返公园后，麋鹿数量下降，白杨树苗开始显著恢复。研究发现，许多区域出现了多年未见的大量健康白杨树苗。虽然白杨恢复显著，但随着麋鹿数量减少，野牛数量增加，可能成为新的限制因素。狼的重新引入不仅促进了树木的恢复，还提升了整个生态系统的生物多样性，包括浆果灌木、昆虫、鸟类和海狸等物种的栖息环境。这项研究展示了顶级捕食者对生态系统的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：狼的重引入对生态系统及社会的影响

不同观点：
• **支持狼重引入及其生态影响**：
  - mkw5053 指出狼的重引入对黄石公园的生态系统产生了积极影响，例如麋鹿不再长时间停留在溪流旁，柳树和棉白杨得以生长，河狸数量增加，进而提高了水位并重建了湿地。KurSix 强调了物种之间的相互关联性，指出狼的重引入展示了生态系统中营养级联效应的实际案例。
  - thangalin 分享了一个视频链接，展示了狼如何重塑了黄石公园的生态系统。
  - arnon 简单表示这是今天的good news。

• **对狼群管理的争议**：
  - pcmaffey 强烈反对蒙大拿州提出的增加狼猎杀配额的提案，认为这是政治和利润驱动，而非科学。提案允许猎杀多达500只狼，增加了50%的猎杀量，并且每人可猎杀30只狼。pcmaffey 提出狼对维持健康猎物群体、控制慢性消耗性疾病有帮助，并指出合法狩猎可能增加偷猎行为。
  - rr808 提到当地牧场主因牲畜损失而反对狼的重引入，提出了“整体利益是否比当地居民的利益更重要”的伦理问题。

• **替代管理方案**：
  - declan_roberts 建议通过增加麋鹿标签数量来控制麋鹿数量，而不是通过猎杀狼来实现。
  - atentaten 关注狼的重引入对其他物种（如山狮）的影响，担心这是否只是在转移问题。

补充讨论：
• **对生态恢复的反思**：
  - owenthejumper 反思了过去250年中人类对生态系统的破坏，以及现在为修复这种破坏所需的努力。
  
• **其他生态系统的适应能力**：
  - cadamsdotcom 提出问题，是否其他生态系统也能像黄石公园一样适应和响应物种变化，还是仅黄石公园有这种能力。

• **教育与传播**：
  - tomrod 提到通过歌曲教育孩子关于狼重引入的知识。

争议焦点：
• **狼群管理提案的科学性与伦理问题**：
  - 支持者认为狼的重引入对生态系统有益，反对者则担心对当地居民和经济的影响，以及提案的科学和伦理基础。

Wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone in 1995, over 60 years after their eradication from the national park.
(Image credit: Photo by William Campbell/Sygma via Getty Images)
Yellowstone's wolves are helping a new generation of young aspen trees to grow tall and join the forest canopy — the first new generation of such trees in Yellowstone's northern range in 80 years.
Gray wolves (
Canis lupus
)
had disappeared from Yellowstone
National Park by 1930 following extensive habitat loss, human hunting and government eradication programs. Without these top predators, populations of elk (
Cervus canadensis
) grew unfettered. At their peak population, an estimated 18,000 elk ranged across the park, chomping on grasses and shrubs as well as the leaves, twigs and bark of trees like
quaking aspen
(
Populus tremuloides
). This stopped saplings from establishing themselves, and surveys in the 1990s found no aspen saplings.
"You had older trees, and then nothing underneath,"
Luke Painter
, an ecologist at Oregon State University and lead author of the new study, told Live Science.

Wolves help restore trees in Yellowstone and the largest interstellar object ever seen
Colossal chief scientist clarifies de-extinction claim, while confirming its 'dire wolves' are 'grey wolves with 20 edits'
But when wolves were reintroduced in 1995, the picture began to change. As wolf numbers rose, the elk population in the park dropped sharply, and it is now down to about 2,000.
In the new study, published Tuesday (July 22) in the journal
Forest Ecology and Management
, Painter and his colleagues surveyed aspen stands — specific areas of the forest where these trees grow.
Related:
Reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone helped entire ecosystem thrive, 20-year study finds
The team returned to
three areas surveyed in 2012
to examine changes to aspen sapling numbers. Of the 87 aspen stands studied, a third had a large number of tall aspen saplings throughout, indicating the trees are healthy and growing. Another third of the stands had patches of tall saplings.

"We're seeing significant new growth of young aspen and this is the first time that we've found it in our plots," Painter said. These are young aspen with a trunk greater than 2 inches (5 centimetres) in diameter at chest height — which haven't been seen there since the 1940s, he added.
"It doesn't mean that they're not going to get killed or die from something, but it's a pretty good indication that we're getting some new trees," Painter noted. "As they get bigger, they get more resilient."
Such trees are old enough to spread themselves, either by sending up new shoots from their roots a fair distance from the main tree, or via seed production, he said.
The researchers found tall aspen saplings in many of the sites studied.
(Image credit: Photo provided by Luke Painter, OSU College of Agricultural Sciences.)
However, while Yellowstone's quaking aspen are recovering, they aren't out of the woods just yet. The elk population has declined, but bison (
Bison bison
) numbers have increased in some areas in recent years.
Bison are a lot harder for wolves to take down
, said Painter, so increasing numbers of bison may be emerging as a new constraint on aspen in some areas.
Painter said that the variation in aspen recovery shows the effects of reintroducing a big predator to the top of the food chain, rather than to changes in the overall climate, for example.
The re-emergence of aspen has widespread effects, he told Live Science. "Aspen are a key species for biodiversity. The canopy is more open than it is with conifers and you get filtering light that creates a habitat that supports a lot of diversity of plants."
This means a boost to berry-producing shrubs, insects and birds and also species like beavers, because
the trees are a preferred food and building material for the semi- aquatic rodents
, along with the willows and cottonwoods that grow near to water in the region.

There are also hints that the number of bears and cougars in the region have increased since wolves were introduced, Painter said, but it's not clear why.

44658323.article_summary: 1995年，狼被重新引入黄石公园，此前它们因栖息地丧失、人类猎杀和政府的消灭计划而在1930年从公园消失。狼的消失导致麋鹿数量失控增长，过度啃食植被，尤其是白杨树，使得新树苗无法生长。到1990年代，黄石北部的白杨树苗几乎绝迹。狼重返公园后，麋鹿数量下降，白杨树苗开始显著恢复。研究发现，许多区域出现了多年未见的大量健康白杨树苗。虽然白杨恢复显著，但随着麋鹿数量减少，野牛数量增加，可能成为新的限制因素。狼的重新引入不仅促进了树木的恢复，还提升了整个生态系统的生物多样性，包括浆果灌木、昆虫、鸟类和海狸等物种的栖息环境。这项研究展示了顶级捕食者对生态系统的重要性。

data.title: 4k NASA employees opt to leave agency through deferred resignation program
data.author: ProAm
data.article_summary: 近4,000名NASA员工选择通过延迟辞职计划离开该机构，约占NASA员工总数的20%，使员工人数从18,000减至14,000。这一计划是特朗普政府为缩减联邦政府 workforce 推出的，此外还提议将NASA的预算削减约24%。不过，近期通过的《One Big Beautiful Bill Act》为NASA在2032年前额外拨款近100亿美元，支持火星任务和重返月球计划。NASA的预算和裁员计划遭到科学家和太空组织的批评，300多名现任和前任NASA员工联名致信，反对这些削减计划。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NASA预算削减及其影响，尤其是科学任务和人员被裁减的问题，以及与SLS等项目的低效对比。

不同观点：
• **支持科学任务的观点**：[gammarator]、[ericvolp12]、[rockskon]认为，NASA削减了极具生产力的科学任务，导致大量专家流失，特别是在天体物理学和深空探测领域。这些领域的人才在私营部门没有对应的机会，因此他们的失业将对美国科学研究产生长期负面影响。

• **支持改革和精简的观点**：[eagerpace]、[bradley13]认为，NASA需要改革，尽管当前的改革方式可能导致人才流失和不确定性，但从长远来看，可能带来新的思维方式和改进。SLS项目被认为是低效的，应该被重新审视。

• **批评当前改革方式的观点**：[samrus]、[yalogin]认为，当前的削减是政治操作，旨在通过削弱联邦机构来推动私有化，最终会导致美国在科学领域的领导地位下降，并对公共卫生和国家安全等领域产生长期负面影响。

• **关注具体实施和影响的观点**：[cozzyd]、[mosesbp]关注削减预算对具体项目和人员的影响，特别是涉及到的承包商和科研人员的去向问题。他们担心关键项目的延误和科研人员的流失。

• **建议改革NASA运营模式的观点**：[BobbyJo]建议，NASA需要一个更明确、可衡量的使命，类似于联邦储备的简单明确目标，以便公众和代表能够对NASA进行有效监督，避免成为政治利益的牺牲品。

• **关注人员构成和再就业的观点**：[hk1337]、[_carbyau_]、[tonyhart7]关注NASA内部人员构成，特别是工程师与管理人员的比例，以及被裁人员再就业的可能性，希望私营航天公司能够吸纳这些专业人才。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于NASA当前的预算削减是否合理，特别是科学任务的取消和对SLS等项目的持续投资是否符合长远利益。
• 私营部门在科学研究中的角色也被提及，强调SpaceX等公司不进行基础科学研究，无法填补NASA科学任务被削减带来的空白。
• 讨论还涉及联邦机构的改革和私有化问题，部分评论认为当前的改革是短视的资本运作，将对国家长期发展不利。

44699052.article_content:
NPR
Nearly 4,000 NASA employees opt to leave agency through deferred resignation program
Chandelis Duster
Jul. 26, 2025
MORE
Workers on scaffolding repaint the NASA logo near the top of the Vehicle Assembly Building at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla., May 2020.
Photo by
John Raoux
-
AP
Nearly 4,000 NASA employees have opted to leave the space agency through the Trump administration's deferred resignation program, NASA said on Saturday.
The cuts amount to an estimated 20% of NASA's workforce, and will reduce the agency from 18,000 to 14,000 employees, NASA spokesperson Cheryl Warner said in a statement shared with NPR. The total number includes the agency's loss of 500 other workers due to normal attrition, she said.
During a second round of the program, which closed at midnight Friday, 3,000 employees applied to leave the agency, Warner said, following the 870 employees that applied to leave during the first round.
The resignations follow the Trump administration's plan to reduce the federal workforce and implement cuts recommended by the
Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
.
NPR has reached out to the White House for comment.
It's unclear when the full reduction of the workforce will take effect, Warner said. NASA did not respond to NPR's questions about how the workforce cuts will affect the agency.
The administration has also proposed
decreasing NASA's budget
. A fiscal year 2026
budget request
released in May would reduce funding for the agency by about 24% (from nearly $25 billion to nearly $19 billion.) But the
House
and
Senate
are discussing recommendations that would keep funding for the agency around the current budget.
Concerning funding beyond the next fiscal year, however, the agency recently got a boost — reversing earlier proposals to retire some NASA programs. Trump's
One Big Beautiful Bill Act
that he signed into law earlier this month, allocates nearly $10 billion in additional funding for NASA through 2032, including backing for Mars missions and plans to return to the moon.
The White House's proposed budget cuts and changes at the agency have faced criticism from scientists and space organizations, including The Planetary Society, a nonprofit led by Bill Nye, "The Science Guy."
"The Planetary Society believes that a great nation deserves a great space program, one that reflects our national ideals and serves the public interest," the organization said about the White House budget proposal in May. "This proposal doesn't merely fall short — it actively rejects that promise, undermining the rare opportunity NASA provides to build unity at home and collaboration abroad through American leadership."
On Monday, more than 300 current and former NASA employees signed and sent a
letter
known as the "Voyager Declaration" to interim NASA administrator Sean Duffy, criticizing "rapid and wasteful changes" at the agency that they say include cuts to programs and research. They also urged Duffy to not implement the proposed cuts and said "they are not in the best interest of NASA."

data.author: taubek

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：QR码和数据恢复中的错误纠正技术及其应用

不同观点：
• [eknkc] 分享了20年前从Usenet下载数据时使用par文件进行错误纠正的经历。他提到文件被分割成块，若某块丢失或损坏，par文件可以帮助恢复，且无需下载整个par文件，只需下载对应缺失部分即可。他还表示对错误纠正（如Reed-Solomon算法）的原理非常感兴趣，甚至自己尝试实现了一个简单的版本。

• [dunconian] 讲述了自己在工作中处理不可扫描的QR码的经历。他通过手动解码QR码，发现是错误纠正模式中的一个错误导致信息长度位被翻转，从而导致不同扫描器出现不同问题（如返回垃圾数据、崩溃或返回上次扫描的结果）。这个经历让他深入了解了Reed-Solomon错误纠正的实际应用。

• [Theodores] 对QR码的美学设计提出了问题，比如边框大小规则以及如何在QR码中添加Logo。他还讨论了在不同大小的QR码（如21x21模块）中如何选择优化方案，并询问是否"块状"设计最优。

补充讨论：
• [cinntaile] 提到该内容在三天前已经被重新提交，暗示可能存在重复讨论的问题，这与内容的时效性和社区的讨论管理有关。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户关注的角度不同：[eknkc] 和 [dunconian] 更关注错误纠正技术的实现和原理，而 [Theodores] 则关心QR码的设计和优化问题。这两方面在实际应用中可能需要权衡。

• 对于QR码设计和错误纠正的优先级存在潜在讨论空间：美观和功能性之间的平衡，以及不同场景下QR码的最优大小和设计选择。

data.author: duxup
data.article_summary: Meta面临新的诉讼，指控其通过BitTorrent网络盗版并分发成人视频以加速下载其他数据，用于训练其AI模型。原告Strike 3 Holdings称，Meta自2018年以来持续盗种至少2,396部成人影片，部分IP地址明确属于Meta，甚至包括其员工。原告认为，Meta利用这些高品质视频获取不正当优势，可能借此绕过BitTorrent协议，加速下载大量其他内容，并可能将这些视频用于训练AI模型，最终可能生成类似内容，损害原告的市场竞争。Strike 3 Holdings要求Meta赔偿损失、停止侵权行为，并删除从其AI模型中盗用的数据。这一证据可能帮助之前指控Meta盗版书籍数据的作者赢得诉讼。
data.comments_summary:
[MossyRope]: It’s hard to say what the exact probability is, but given Meta’s scale and the complexity of their content moderation systems, the chances aren’t zero. If it did happen, I’m sure there would be a massive public outcry, and lawmakers might push for more accountability. But let’s not jump to conclusions without evidence.

[TechSavvySasha]: I think the bigger issue here is the lack of transparency. Meta has been notoriously secretive about how their algorithms work, and that makes it difficult to know what’s really going on. If CSAM was distributed under this scheme, it’s likely because of systemic failures in their moderation systems, not intentional distribution.

[JustHereForTheTea]: To be fair, Meta has invested a lot in AI and human moderation to catch this kind of content before it spreads. The fact that we haven’t heard of any large-scale incidents involving CSAM on their platforms doesn’t mean it’s impossible, but it’s also not something that happens frequently, or else we’d have heard about it by now.

[ConcernedCitizen123]: The real problem here is accountability. Even if it was an accident, Meta should be held responsible for any CSAM that slips through their systems. They’re a multi-billion dollar company with resources to handle this. They should be proactive in fixing these issues and being transparent when something goes wrong.

[TimorousBestie]: But how do we ensure accountability? Meta has a history of downplaying its mistakes and shifting blame to third-party contractors or technical glitches. If CSAM was distributed, what guarantees do we have that they’ll be upfront about it and take meaningful action?

[TechSavvySasha]: That’s why there needs to be third-party oversight. Meta shouldn’t be the only ones investigating themselves. Independent audits and regulatory bodies should have the power to scrutinize their processes and ensure they’re doing everything they can to prevent the spread of CSAM.

[JustHereForTheTea]: I agree that transparency is important, but we also have to be realistic about what Meta can control. They’re dealing with billions of pieces of content daily. It’s not an excuse, but it’s a reality that makes complete prevention difficult. Maybe we should focus on improving detection technology instead of just blaming companies.

主要讨论点：Meta是否在内容分发中传播了儿童性虐待材料（CSAM），以及如果发生这种情况，责任应如何追究。

不同观点：
• TimorousBestie和ConcernedCitizen123认为Meta应该对任何CSAM的分发负责，并对Meta是否会透明处理此事表示怀疑，指出Meta以往有推卸责任的历史。
• MossyRope和JustHereForTheTea认为在没有证据的情况下不应妄下结论，且Meta已有大量资源和技术投入来防止CSAM传播，大规模事件应早已曝光。
• TechSavvySasha强调Meta的系统复杂性和缺乏透明度是主要问题，如果CSAM被传播，应归因于系统性失败而非故意行为，并提出需要第三方监督来确保Meta的自我监管。

补充讨论：
• 关于如何确保Meta的透明度和责任追究，TechSavvySasha建议第三方审计和监管机构应介入。
• JustHereForTheTea则认为应关注技术改进，而不是一味指责公司，理解Meta面临的海量内容管理的挑战。

Porn sites may have blown up Meta's key defense in a copyright fight with book authors who earlier this year
said that Meta torrented
"at least 81.7 terabytes of data across multiple shadow libraries" to train its AI models.
Meta has defeated most of the authors' claims and claimed there is no proof that Meta ever uploaded pirated data through seeding or leeching on the BitTorrent network used to download training data. But authors
still have a chance to prove that Meta may have profited
off its massive piracy, and a new
lawsuit
filed by adult sites last week appears to contain evidence that could help authors win their fight, TorrentFreak
reported
.
The new lawsuit was filed last Friday in a US district court in California by Strike 3 Holdings—which says it attracts "over 25 million monthly visitors" to sites that serve as "ethical sources" for adult videos that "are famous for redefining adult content with Hollywood style and quality."
After authors revealed Meta's torrenting, Strike 3 Holdings checked its proprietary BitTorrent-tracking tools designed to detect infringement of its videos and alleged that the company found evidence that Meta has been torrenting and seeding its copyrighted content for years—since at least 2018. Some of the IP addresses were clearly registered to Meta, while others appeared to be "hidden," and at least one was linked to a Meta employee, the filing said.
Meta’s AI training tactics may have harmed minors
According to Strike 3 Holdings, Meta "willfully and intentionally" infringed "at least 2,396 movies" as part of a strategy to download terabytes of data as fast as possible by seeding popular high-quality porn. Supposedly, Meta continued seeding the content "sometimes for days, weeks, or even months" after downloading them, and these movies may also have been secretly used to train Meta's AI models, Strike 3 Holdings alleged.
The porn site operator explained to the court that BitTorrent's protocol establishes a "tit-for-tat" mechanism that "rewards users who distribute the most desired content." It alleged that Meta took advantage of this system by "often" pirating adult videos that are "often within the most infringed files on BitTorrent websites" on "the very same day the motion pictures are released."
These tactics allegedly gave Meta several advantages, making it harder for Strike 3 Holdings' sites to compete, including potentially distributing the videos to minors for free without age checks in states that now require them.
"Meta specifically targeted Plaintiffs’ content for distribution in order to accelerate its downloads of vast amounts of other content," the lawsuit said. And while Meta claimed that it "wrote a script to intentionally limit distributing popular books on BitTorrent," Strike 3 Holdings believes "discovery will likely show" Meta "continuously" distributed its adult videos specifically as a strategy to get around the BitTorrent protocol.
So far, Strike 3 Holdings says it has documented at least five episodes in which Meta "hand-picked" adult videos from a specific site for "intense periods of distribution" to avoid seeding other content it was sourcing through BitTorrent.
"The only reason to incur the server and bandwidth expense of remaining in a swarm for these long durations is to leverage the extended distribution as tit-for-tat currency in order to efficiently download millions of other files from BitTorrent," Strike 3 Holdings alleged.
Strike 3 Holdings is seeking extensive damages and an injunction to permanently stop Meta from pirating its videos.
The company also wants Meta to delete any stolen videos from its AI training data and existing AI models. The company alleged that Meta could use its high-quality copyrighted works—which provide rare long cuts of "natural, human-centric imagery" showing "parts of the body not found in regular videos" and "unique" forms "of human interactions and facial expressions"—to create a rival adult video generator that could "eventually create identical content for little to no cost."
"Plaintiffs cannot compete against Meta when it ignores federal and state laws and offers Plaintiffs’ works for free," Strike 3 Holdings alleged. "This will effectively eliminate Plaintiffs’ future ability to compete in the marketplace" as well as its brands' "hard-earned reputations as respected and ethical sources for high-quality adult motion pictures by potentially allowing minors unfettered access to Plaintiffs’ content against Plaintiffs’ consent."
Ars could not immediately reach Meta, Strike 3 Holdings' in-house lawyer, or book authors' lawyers for comment.

data.author: mathattack
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：去中心化应用（dapps）的现状及未来趋势

不同观点：
• mathattack 认为目前去中心化应用（dapps）领域存在大量的低质量项目，许多项目只是简单复制已有功能，缺乏创新。这导致市场充斥着许多不可靠的项目，尤其是一些交易量超过百万美元的dapps，实际上并没有提供独特的价值。

• mouse_ 指出，随着市场流动性下降，dapps为了维持运营可能会增加杠杆和交易量，但这并不是一个好的趋势。同时，他也预期市场将会出现整合（consolidation），即许多功能相似的dapps会被淘汰或合并，最终留下更少但更具竞争力的项目。

补充讨论：
• mathattack 提到了“低门槛”的问题，认为这使得创建dapps变得过于容易，从而导致大量低质量的项目涌现。这可能是市场不成熟的一个表现。

• mouse_ 强调了流动性和杠杆的问题，认为流动性的下降可能会迫使dapps采取一些冒险的策略，如增加杠杆和交易量，这可能会进一步增加市场的风险。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于dapps市场的未来发展趋势。mathattack 对当前市场的低质量项目表示担忧，而 mouse_ 则更关注流动性下降带来的潜在风险和市场整合的可能性。两者都认为当前市场存在问题，但关注的方面有所不同。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于市场整合的预期。mouse_ 认为市场将会出现整合，而 mathattack 并没有直接提及这一点，但其对低质量项目的批评间接支持了这一预期。

总结：
当前dapps市场面临着项目质量参差不齐、流动性下降以及潜在的市场整合等问题。不同观点主要集中在问题的具体表现和未来趋势的预期上。

data.title: I Got Claude to Write Code I Could Ship
data.author: gen220
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何使用Anthropic的Claude Code工具来编写可交付的代码。尽管Claude Code能自动化处理许多任务，如修复bug和重构代码，但它生成的代码往往过于庞大且难以理解，导致审查困难。为解决这一问题，作者引入了"stacked PRs"（堆叠式拉取请求）的方法，将大块代码拆分为一系列小而可独立审查的PRs。通过在提示中加入规划和分步执行的指导，Claude Code学会了按计划生成堆叠的PRs，从而提高了代码的可审查性和质量。最终，Claude Code成为作者处理工程任务的得力工具，尤其在处理遗留代码和长期搁置的重构任务方面表现出色。作者还开发了GT MCP工具，以推广这种工作流并应用于其他AI代理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：代码提交的结构和流程优化

不同观点：
• frankfrank13指出，当前堆栈中最大的Pull Request（PR）包含268行代码，但大部分是HTML。这表明该PR的主要内容为HTML结构和样式，可能相对简单。该用户关注代码的组成以及每部分的贡献。

• frankfrank13建议在编写任何代码之前，应向用户展示计划提交的堆栈结构，并请求确认。这强调了在开发过程中透明度和用户确认的重要性，以确保开发方向符合预期。

• 该用户还强调了每个PR的代码必须是原子的（即单一职责，不包含不相关更改），并且必须通过持续集成（CI）。这指出了代码质量和开发流程中的关键要求，以确保每个PR的独立性和稳定性。

补充讨论：
• 强调了在PR提交之前，确认代码结构和通过CI的重要性，以避免不必要的错误和回滚。
• 提出了对代码提交流程的改进建议，特别是在多层审核和确认机制方面，以提高团队协作的效率和代码质量。

争议焦点：
• 当前堆栈中PR的大小和内容构成是否合理。有人可能认为268行的HTML代码是可以接受的，而其他人可能觉得应该进一步拆分以提高可读性和审核效率。
• 如何在代码提交前有效地进行结构展示和确认，以平衡开发速度和代码质量。这可能涉及工具支持和团队流程的调整。

44711199.article_content:
Engineering
Launches
Stacking
How I got Claude to write code I could actually ship
July 25, 2025
Last week, Anthropic released a statement showing that Claude Code
usage has increased by 300%
in the last 3 months. The appeal of Claude Code is obvious; every team has a laundry list of tasks that are nice-to-have but never make it over the cut line. You know the drill:
Refactor that brittle module I’ve been side-eyeing since early-2024.
Clean up some interfaces that scream “we rushed this out to hit the deadline, and have been scared to touch it ever since.”
Write tests.
Proponents claim that Claude Code can now automate all of this work. If this were true, it would change a lot of things. So, I figured we had to try it out for ourselves.
Testing Claude Code’s abilities
I started with something small: identifying the cause of a bug that was triggering off-by-one errors under very specific edge cases on the Graphite dashboard. After reticulating for a minute or so Claude, impressively, returned a concise summary of the problem, the offending change that regressed this behavior (spoiler: it was me) and staged a fix.
Emboldened by this success, I moved on to having Claude perform a refactor in some well tested code that I’d been putting off. It confidently responded with a few thousand lines of code—an unreadable mess that would take hours to carefully review. Worse, Claude had modified the test files, too. Though the PR was “green,” I was no longer sure it was safe to land.
It turns out this was a theme. Trying to vibe code even medium‑complexity features was proving difficult—not because writing the code was hard, but because it was too easy. It was too easy to create thousands of lines of code where even you as the author have no idea how it works. When that code makes it to review, your only option is to “LGTM” and pray, which isn't really an option in any serious engineering org. For many engineers on our team, this tradeoff meant that they were either using Claude Code for point fixes or not at all.
AI-generated code needs stacked PRs
Large PRs are not a novel problem.
Studies show
that only 24% of large PRs (>1000 lines) receive
any
review comments. AI only exacerbates this by producing far more code than humans do. And let’s face it, that code often fails to capture the intent of the person who prompted it.
The solution to this problem, for humans, is something we at Graphite know a thing or two about—
stacked diffs
. Instead of a single, large PR that implements an entire feature, engineers can put up a sequence of smaller PRs in a “stack” that keeps each change focused and easily reviewable.
This got me wondering, “Could we teach Claude to stack?”
Teaching Claude to stack
I started by adding instructions that explained stacking and how to use the
gt
CLI to our monorepo’s
CLAUDE.md
file:
With this new prompt, Claude started using
gt
to
create stacks of PRs
, but the boundaries between them were messy. Tests were added before their dependencies existed, and a refactor was split across multiple PRs, leaving none able to pass CI.
I realized that stacking is about more than just writing “small PRs.” It forces you to think critically about the work you intend to do, so you can build a clear plan and share it meaningfully with reviewers. The PRs were small, but they didn’t build and were hard to understand. Turns out, stacking like a senior engineer takes planning, which Claude wasn’t doing on its own, so we need to teach it that too.
Before I create a stack myself, I like to think about where the feature is going and the building blocks that will be needed to get there. For example: I might start by defining interfaces, then the server logic, and finally the frontend UX.
This maps cleanly to the concept of “Todos” in Claude Code, which is the mechanism that the agent uses internally to plan out complex tasks. I added this to Claude’s instructions:
With a few more tweaks to the instructions, Claude Code started organizing its “Todos” as a stack—one pull request for each task. Check out this example, where I asked Claude to build a
Wordle
app:
And voilà! Claude Code built Wordle, as a stack of pull requests:
#1 feat: add basic HTML structure and styling for Wordle game
+268/-0
#2 feat: implement core game logic and state management
+129/-2
#3 feat: add keyboard input handling
+29/-1
#4 feat: add animations and visual feedback
+33/-4
Each PR focuses on a different area of the project, and can be independently reviewed.
Building with Claude Code and GT MCP
Claude Code has become my go-to tool for getting real engineering work done—building features, cleaning up legacy code, and finally tackling the long list of refactors I’d been putting off. It works well because it plans the way engineers do: breaking things down into smaller, reviewable steps. We built the
GT MCP
to capture this workflow and make it so any agent can follow stacking best practices.

• 该用户还强调了每个PR的代码必须是原子的（即单一职责，不包含不相关更改），并且必须通过持续集成（CI）。这指出了代码质量和开发流程中的关键要求，以确保每个PR的独立性和稳定性。

补充讨论：
• 强调了在PR提交之前，确认代码结构和通过CI的重要性，以避免不必要的错误和回滚。
• 提出了对代码提交流程的改进建议，特别是在多层审核和确认机制方面，以提高团队协作的效率和代码质量。

争议焦点：
• 当前堆栈中PR的大小和内容构成是否合理。有人可能认为268行的HTML代码是可以接受的，而其他人可能觉得应该进一步拆分以提高可读性和审核效率。
• 如何在代码提交前有效地进行结构展示和确认，以平衡开发速度和代码质量。这可能涉及工具支持和团队流程的调整。

data.title: When photography was born, fascination, obsession, and danger followed
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：摄影技术的发展、其与艺术的关系以及与现代AI技术的类比

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun分享了个人作为“摄影系谱学家”的经历，讲述了家族照片收集和分析的过程。他强调了摄影技术从早期锡版照片到柯达布朗尼相机，再到彩色照片的发展历程，并对不同阶段的照片质量进行了评价。他认为彩色照片在某些阶段的质量不如黑白照片，并对技术革新带来的质量变化表示感慨。

• api将摄影技术的发展与当前AI和艺术的讨论进行了类比，指出两者在道德恐慌和公众讨论上的相似性。他提到历史上对摄影的道德批评，特别是其在色情内容制作中的应用，并认为这些讨论与当前AI生成内容的争议非常相似。

• chazeon通过参观宾夕法尼亚铁路博物馆的经历，将早期铁路技术与当前AI技术的发展进行了类比，指出人们对新技术的恐惧和抵制是一种常见现象。

• k__认为摄影写实主义只是表面上的真实，任何技术娴熟的摄影师都知道这并非事实。他将此与LLM生成的文本进行比较，指出两者都具有类似的表面真实性。

• echelon将早期摄影技术的批评与当前生成式AI的批评进行了对比，指出尽管摄影技术发展过程中存在诸多问题和争议，但最终其积极影响超过了负面影响。他引用了Susan Sontag等人的观点，强调了摄影技术对文化和社会的影响。

• 75345d4c持有激进观点，认为化学感光摄影技术永远不能算作真正的艺术，主张委托画家进行创作。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于摄影技术是否能被视为艺术，以及新技术（如AI生成内容）在艺术领域的地位和影响。
• JKCalhoun通过具体例子展示了摄影技术发展的不同阶段及其对照片质量的影响，提供了历史发展的实证支持。
• api和echelon都将历史上的摄影技术争议与当前AI技术的讨论进行了类比，强调了技术发展过程中相似的心理和社会反应。
• 75345d4c的观点较为极端，认为传统绘画才是真正的艺术，对摄影和AI技术持否定态度。

data.title: Claude Code is a slot machine
data.author: rgoldfinger
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了AI工具对软件工程师工作的影响。作者最初因为热爱编程过程——将想法变为现实的乐趣——而成为工程师。然而，AI工具的引入打破了这种“心流”体验，编程变得更多是间歇性的奖励和等待。作者引用了两种工作模式：“魔法师”模式，快速创造但不深入；以及“书记员”模式，深入理解每个细节。真正的技能在于知道何时使用哪种模式，并在两者间灵活切换。AI工具可以加速创建过程，但最终仍需深入细节才能确保其正常工作。文章还提到，AI工具的流行部分源于类似老虎机的间歇奖励效应，吸引人们不断尝试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码工具（如Claude Code）对软件工程的影响及使用体验

不同观点：
• Wowfunhappy：认为AI编码工具（如Claude Code）能帮助处理繁琐的细节工作，使得编码过程更加有趣和高效。尽管AI无法完全替代人工，但在解决技术问题和迭代测试方面表现突出。
• jonator：强调AI工具帮助加速了从构思到产品实现的过程，减少了繁琐的决策过程，同时提高了输出质量。尽管对AI的社会影响有疑虑，但认可其在软件开发中的巨大价值。
• tptacek：指出大部分编程工作是机械重复的，应该被自动化。AI工具的出现有助于解放程序员，让他们专注于更有趣和创新的工作。
• kregasaurusrex：分享了AI工具在处理复杂问题时的局限性，例如在处理特定语言或库的兼容性问题时可能效率不高，导致时间和成本的浪费。
• b_e_n_t_o_n：认为AI应被视为一种工具，而不是万能解决方案。AI在某些情况下非常有用，但滥用可能导致挫败感。
• eric-burel：批评了关于LLM开发的低质量讨论，认为专业领域应该有更高质量的讨论和资源。
• quatonion：作为有多年经验的程序员，享受AI工具带来的新鲜体验和高效生产力，尽管需要一些指导和帮助。
• ryanegt：承认AI工具在处理重复性工作中的价值，但强调AI只有在良好的代码基础上才能发挥最大作用，程序员需要适应和学习新工具。
• scoreandmore：指出AI工具使用过程中可能导致的“上瘾”现象，类似于赌博，需要自我控制。
• stillpointlab：描述了与AI工具合作的独特体验，尽管需要频繁修正和调整，但总体上提高了工作效率和代码质量。
• jgb1984：批评AI生成的代码质量低下，认为这会导致软件质量下降，行业面临风险。
• gonzalohm：分享了AI在处理复杂规则时的局限性，认为AI在某些情况下无法提供有效的帮助。
• ChuckMcM：将LLM的使用比喻为“老虎机”，有时能带来巨大收益，但也存在风险。
• dmh2000：作为年长程序员，认为AI工具延长了其职业生涯，帮助应对因年龄导致的专注力下降。

补充讨论：
• AI工具在软件开发中的潜力和局限性：一些用户认为AI能显著提高生产力和代码质量，而另一些用户则指出其在处理复杂问题和特定语言或库时的局限性。
• 对AI工具的依赖和“上瘾”现象：有用户担心过度依赖AI工具可能导致效率低下和挫败感，类似于赌博行为。
• 对软件行业和社会的影响：部分用户关注AI工具对软件行业质量的影响，以及其在社会层面的潜在影响。
• 适应和学习新工具的必要性：许多用户强调程序员需要适应和学习如何有效使用AI工具，以保持竞争力。

44702046.article_content:
...but the odds are better
Claude Code keeps me waiting. Here I am pressing return like a crack-addicted rodent in a lab. âYes, I want to make this edit.â I watch as it works, glassy-eyed and bored as the code scrolls by, and on the edge of my seat because my ideas are about to become reality.
I became a software engineer because I loved the process of it. I could sit for hours, figuring out how to wire something up
just so
and get an idea made into something real. And it didnât feel like work. It was just fun. Joyful. Satisfying.
AI disrupts the process. What was that high from flow state is now intermittent rewards and a lot of waiting. And maybe that's ok. Maybe that's the new skill. Iâm in meetings all day anyways.
Software engineering is all about managing complexity. Early on in my career, someone much wiser than me described two modes of operating: the Conjurer, and the Scribe. The Conjurer is a wizard, creating realities out of thin air, working in broad strokes and never going deep. The Scribe reads every line of the text, and every line it refers to, understanding everything to its deepest and fullest extent before acting. Some of us tend more towards one way of operating or the other. Both are critical.
But the real skill, the real thing that makes you effective, is knowing when to use one mode or the other, and being able to switch between them as needed. When does understanding matter? When should we skip it and move onto the next thing? In a field with endless and important detail at every level, we have to both âlet it go and move onâ and âslow downâ constantly.
AI coding tools supercharge this, allowing you to bring whole machineries to life by waving your hands around, offloading the understanding for much longer, but if you want it all to actually
work
, you'll need to dive into the details eventually.
I'm guessing that part of why AI coding tools are so popular is the slot machine effect. Intermittent rewards, lots of waiting that fractures your attention, and inherent laziness keeping you trying with yet another prompt in hopes that you donât have to actually turn on your brain after so many hours of being told not to.
The exhilarating power of creation. Just insert a few more cents, and youâll get another shot at making your dreams a reality.
July 26, 2025
Â·
Roger Goldfinger

data.title: Linux on Snapdragon X Elite: Linaro and Tuxedo Pave the Way for ARM64 Laptops
data.author: MarcusE1W
data.article_summary: 在2025年Linaro Connect大会上，Linaro和TUXEDO Computers展示了采用Snapdragon X Elite SoC的ARM64 Linux笔记本原型，标志着Linux对Snapdragon设备支持的显著进展。尽管这些设备主要支持Windows on Arm，但通过Qualcomm、Linaro及社区的合作，Linux内核已支持包括Lenovo、Dell、HP等多款Snapdragon笔记本。当前进展包括GPU加速、外接显示、音频、摄像头、Wi-Fi等功能的支持。尽管Linux在ARM64笔记本上的体验仍落后于Windows和x86笔记本，但Ubuntu和Fedora等发行版正积极增加支持。TUXEDO Computers承诺推出预装Linux的Qualcomm笔记本，进一步推动Linux在ARM架构设备上的应用，为用户提供更多选择和创新机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux在商用笔记本上的支持情况、Tuxedo笔记本的硬件与软件问题、移动设备上的Linux与虚拟化支持。

不同观点：
• **Tuxedo笔记本的批评**：[pentamassiv] 提到Tuxedo笔记本未能兑现对fwupd、上游驱动和coreboot的支持承诺，内核开发者甚至考虑将其列入黑名单。此外，Tuxedo的设备设置需要依赖其Electron应用，体验不佳，且设备不可自行修理。
• **对移动Linux设备现状的不满**：[fb03] 表达了对当前移动Linux设备（尤其是Ubuntu）在电池续航和性能上的失望，认为苹果设备尽管封闭但表现更好。同时批评了Snapdragon上的软件进展缓慢。
• **对Surface支持的质疑**：[shenki0] 指出微软Surface Laptop 7的触摸板和触摸屏不支持，质疑其是否真的“支持”Linux。
• **对低功耗Linux笔记本的需求**：[rr808] 表示希望摆脱Windows和苹果生态，但目前可选的Linux笔记本不多，对高续航低功耗的Linux笔记本有强烈需求。
• **对商用笔记本Linux支持的体验**：[teo_zero] 提到当前Linux内核已经支持许多商用笔记本型号，询问其他用户的使用体验。

补充讨论：
• **Linux在ARM设备上的潜力与挑战**：[diabllicseagull] 认为Linux在ARM设备上有很大潜力，但电源管理和固件支持仍是主要问题。
• **未来移动设备与虚拟化**：[arend321] 和 [jz00ellis] 讨论了通过Android虚拟化框架或AR眼镜加Raspberry Pi实现移动Linux设备的可能性，展示了创新的解决方案。
• **对厂商支持的失望**：[bilgi42] 表示对厂商对待Linux用户的态度不满，认为如果设备支持不到位就不应宣称支持。
• **其他选择**：[holri] 提到了MNT Reform这款ARM64笔记本，提供了另一种选择。
• **对x86兼容性的讨论**：[0x000xca0xfe] 和 [OptionX] 讨论了Snapdragon芯片是否支持类似Apple Rosetta 2的兼容层，以及是否有类似的x86兼容项目。

争议焦点：
• **Tuxedo笔记本的实际支持情况**：用户[pentamassiv]对Tuxedo的实际支持情况表示强烈不满，尤其是驱动和软件支持问题，而[TheJCDenton]提供了更多背景信息，指出Tuxedo与Qualcomm的合作未如预期。

At Linaro Connect 2025 Linaro, thanks to its work within the Qualcomm ecosystem, and TUXEDO Computers, showcased an off-the-shelf prototype ARM64 Linux laptop using the Snapdragon X Elite SoC, demonstrating progress in enabling Linux on Snapdragon devices to meet the increasing demand for ARM computing.
But wait! This is just the tip of the iceberg of a long journey!
Advancements in Linux Support for Snapdragon X Elite:
Over the past year, substantial progress has been made in integrating Linux support for Snapdragon X Elite laptops.
Qualcomm and many laptop vendors worked together to bring to market a new family of Snapdragon-powered personal computers. This new processor family ticks all the boxes for powerful and productive machines, and the collaboration with Microsoft brought the support for Windows on Arm on these devices as the main operating system (which Linaro has
contributed to as well
).
Unfortunately, like Apple computers, there is no native out-of-the-box Linux support.
The effort from Qualcomm and Linaro has been crucial to bring a functional Linux to the new family of ARM64-powered laptops.
The engineering experts from Qualcomm, Linaro and the kernel community have made a stable Linux experience possible across many Qualcomm processors, including the newer Snapdragon X Elite.
But we are still missing pre-installed Linux laptops. In the x86 processor-based laptop market, many vendors now offer Linux options.
State of the art:
Where are we now with the Linux support on these Snapdragon laptops?
A year after the processor announcement, the current Linux Kernel 6.15 already supports many commercial laptops:
Lenovo Yoga 7x
Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 6
Dell XPS 13
Asus Vivobook S15
HP Omnibook x14
Microsoft Surface 13/15
The enablement wouldn’t have been possible without the collaboration between Linaro, Qualcomm, the community, and the laptop vendors.
During the last few years, Linaro engineers have contributed to many improvements in terms of functionalities and use cases, including:
GPU and 2D/3D acceleration
External display output (USB-C DP altmode)
USB enablement
Audio support
Software camera support
Thermal management
Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/Modem
Suspend/resume
Contact Us
to know more.
Currently, the Linux experience on ARM64 laptops lags behind Windows on the same hardware and Linux on x86 laptops. Linaro’s goal is to enhance the out-of-the-box experience, reliability, and overall user experience on Qualcomm-powered laptops running popular Linux distributions, such as Debian and Fedora, by addressing fundamental issues.
Watch the Linux ARM64 Compute Laptops BoF discussion at Linaro Connect 2025
Thanks to the changes available in the kernel, Ubuntu community has released an installable Concept Distro for Ubuntu 24.10 and now Canonical is adding ARM64 Laptops
support for Ubuntu 25.04 distro
and also
Fedora is working on it
.
In other words, the development progress is going in the right direction, distro support is on its way and many people are starting to drive these devices with Linux daily.
TUXEDO Computers’ Commitment to Linux on ARM:
The integration of Linux on Qualcomm laptops signifies more than just a technical milestone. It has the potential to create a positive impact on the global technology ecosystem and the wider market.
This is what the folks at
TUXEDO Computers
are putting their bets on, a full-fledged laptop with one of the latest and innovative ARM64 processors with Linux. The promise and the commitment from TUXEDO to release a Qualcomm Laptop with pre-installed Linux is a living fact that this operating system is mature enough for desktop use on these devices.
Tuxedo directly contacted us for help for technical support to bring up the missing bits on the device, and they sent us two prototypes to develop on. Collaboration between experts from both companies successfully enabled Linux installation and the proper functioning of many features on this device.
The unique nature of this case study and its growing interest create new opportunities for developers, businesses, and consumers who require Linux in their Snapdragon X Series family products, paving the way for increased choice and innovation in the ARM64-based laptop space and beyond.

While we are still in the development phase, we can confidently say that users can look forward to long battery

data.title: I designed my own fast game streaming video codec – PyroWave
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了通过网络在两台机器间低延迟传输游戏画面的技术需求和挑战，强调每一毫秒的延迟都很关键。整个过程包括从机器A发送控制输入到机器B，B渲染帧、编码并传输，最后机器A解码并显示图像。为实现低延迟，通常使用GPU加速的视频压缩，如H.264、HEVC或AV1。为了进一步减少延迟，可以采取以下策略：

1. **仅使用帧内编码**：抛弃运动预测以提高错误恢复能力和简化编码过程，代价是比特率大幅增加。
2. **抛弃熵编码**：熵编码不利于并行化，去除它可以加速编码。
3. **离散小波变换**：尽管现代编码多用离散余弦变换（DCT），但小波变换在某些特定领域仍有应用价值。

这些方法可以实现超低延迟，但代价是更高的带宽消耗，适合本地局域网内使用，而不适合互联网传输。文章还提到了专业广播领域和特定硬件实现的例子。
