44714914.article_content:
Streaming gameplay from one machine to another over a network is a reasonably popular use case these days. These use cases demand very, very low latency. Every millisecond counts here. We need to:
Send controller input from machine A to B over network
B renders a frame on the GPU
B encodes the frame into a bitstream
B sends the result over a network to A
A decodes the bitstream
A displays image on screen
Dopamine is released in target brain
Every step in this chain adds latency and we want to minimize this as much as possible. The go-to solution here is GPU accelerated video compression using whatever codec you have available, usually H.264, HEVC or if you’re really fancy, AV1. Ideally, we want all of this to complete in roughly ~20 ms.
To make this use case work well, we have to strangle the codecs quite a bit. Modern video codecs love latency since it allows tricks like flexible rate control and B-frames. That is what allows these codecs to operate at ridiculous compression ratios, but we have to throw away most of these tricks now. Since the codec cannot add latency, and we’re working on a fixed bit-rate budget (the ethernet cable or WiFi antenna), we’re left with:
Hard-capped constant bit rate
There is no buffer that can soak up variable bit rate
Infinite GOP P-frames or intra-refresh
Either choice deals with packet loss differently
When game streaming, the expectation is that we have a lot of bandwidth available. Streaming locally on a LAN in particular, bandwidth is basically free. Gigabit ethernet is ancient technology and hundreds of megabits over WiFi is no problem either. This shifts priorities a little bit for me at least.
Back in my student days, I designed a very simple low-complexity video codec for my master thesis, and after fiddling with Vulkan video and PyroFling for a while, that old itch was scratched again.
I wanted to see what would happen if I designed a codec with laser focus on local streaming with the absolute lowest possible latency, what could go wrong?
Throwing out motion prediction – intra-only
This is the grug-brained approach to video, but it’s not as silly as it sounds. Bit-rates explode of course, but we gain:
Excellent error resilience
Even on local WiFi streaming to a handheld device, this does matter quite a lot, at least in my experience
Simplicity
Duh
Consistent quality
With CBR, video quality is heavily dependent on how good of a job motion estimation can do
Intra-only has use cases in digital cinema (motion JPEG2000) and more professionally oriented applications where these concerns are likely more important than squeezing bandwidth. We’re now working at 100+ Mbits/s instead of ~10-20 Mbit/s, so streaming over the internet is no longer feasible outside of peer-to-peer with fiber links. For reference, raw 1080p60 with 420 chroma subsampling is in the range of 1.5 Gbit/s, and it only gets worse from there.
Throwing out entropy coding
Entropy coding is an absolute nightmare for parallelization, which means encoding solely on the GPU with compute shaders becomes an extremely painful affair. Let’s just throw that out and see how far we get. Gotta go fast!
There are codecs in this domain too, but it’s getting very specialized at this point. In the professional broadcasting space, there are codecs designed to squeeze more video through existing infrastructure with “zero” lag and minimal hardware cost. My master thesis was about this, for example. A more consumer oriented example is VESA display stream compression (I’m not sure if it does entropy coding, but the compression ratios are small enough I doubt it). There isn’t much readily available software in this domain, it’s generally all implemented in tiny ASICs. If FFmpeg doesn’t support it, it doesn’t exist for mere mortals.
Discrete Wavelet Transforms
While modern codecs are all block-based Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) + a million hacks on top to make it good, there is an alternative that tried its best in the 90s to replace DCTs, but kinda failed in the end.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UGXeRx0Tic4
is a nice video explaining some of the lore. DWT-based compression has a niche today, but only in intra video compression. It’s a shame, because it’s quite elegant.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_wavelet_transform
A graphics programmer will be familiar with this structure immediately, because this is just good old mip-maps with spice. Effectively, we downsample images, and also compute the “error” between the high-res picture and low-res picture. With signal processing lenses on, we can say it’s a critically sampled filter-bank. After processing N pixels, we obtain N / 2 low-pass and N / 2 high-pass pixels. The filters designed to do this are very particular (I really don’t know or care how they were made), but it’s basically just a basic convolution kernel, nothing too wild. The number of levels can vary but I chose 5 levels of decomposition.

data.title: Different Clocks
data.author: pppone
data.article_summary:
Ianto Cannon创建的时钟图形使用JavaScript生成可缩放矢量图形（SVG），源代码可自由使用和修改。每个时钟显示当前的协调世界时（UTC），包括以下几种样式：

1. **Binary**：方块显示Unix时间，即自1970年以来的秒数，以32位整数表示。
2. **Polygons**：多边形显示时间，格式为yy:M:w:d:h:mm:ss，其中M是月份，w是当月第几周，d是星期几。
3. **Blobs**：左起第一个blob显示每千年波峰移动一次，后续blob分别显示每年的波峰、每天的波峰、每小时的波峰、每分钟的波峰和每秒的波峰，最后一个blob综合了所有六种波。
4. **Peaks**：最高峰每千年从右向左移动一次，依次递减至每分钟移动一次。
5. **Waves**：与Peaks类似，但使用贝塞尔曲线而非锐边。

© Ianto Cannon 2025年7月28日
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同类型的创意时钟设计及其吸引力

不同观点：
• rezmason 对组合式的 "blob clock" 表达了喜爱，并计划在 CodePen 上创建一个简化版，只显示小时、分钟和秒，以探索这种设计的实际效果。这表明他对这种创意时钟的实现和实验充满兴趣。

• DougBTX 被每千年一次的标志所吸引，认为它们似乎可以被理解，但又不完全如此。这暗示他对时间标记的独特性和神秘性感到着迷，尤其是那些跨越长时间尺度的标记。

• xnx 提到了AI编码工具在创建不同钟表概念中的趣味性，并分享了一个基于"Against the Run"艺术作品的一次性时钟概念链接。这显示了他对结合AI和艺术创作的兴趣，以及对创意时钟设计的探索。

• GuinansEyebrows 回忆了一个旧的iPhone时钟应用"hms"，该应用通过一个长方体显示时间，每个维度对应小时、分钟和秒，形状会随时间增长并重置。这表明他对过去创意时钟设计的怀念，以及对独特时间显示方式的欣赏。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多种创意时钟设计，包括组合式、时间标记、AI生成和三维显示等，展现了对时间视觉化表达的多样化兴趣。
• 不同用户对创意时钟的关注点各异，有的关注实现和技术实验，有的则偏重于怀旧和艺术价值。
• 争议焦点并不明显，但可以看出用户对不同设计背后的实现方式和技术支持有不同的侧重和兴趣。

Ianto Cannon
's clock graphics
These clocks are generated as scalable vector graphics using JavaScript. Feel free to use and modify the source code.
Each clock displays the current Coordinated Universal Time (UTC):
Loading…
Binary
These squares show the Unix time, which is a 32-bit signed integer representing the number of seconds since 1970.
Polygons
These polygons show the time in the format yy:M:w:d:h:mm:ss, where M is the month, w is the week in the month, and d is the day of the week.

Blobs
The leftmost blob has a travelling wave that passes the top once per millennium.
The following blobs have waves that pass once per year, day, hour, minute, and second, respectively.
The final blob has all six of the above waves on it.
Peaks
The highest peak moves from right to left once per millenium, the next highest once per year, once per day, once per hour, and once per minute.
Waves
Similar to the peaks, but using Bézier curves instead of sharp edges.

• rezmason 对组合式的 "blob clock" 表达了喜爱，并计划在 CodePen 上创建一个简化版，只显示小时、分钟和秒，以探索这种设计的实际效果。这表明他对这种创意时钟的实现和实验充满兴趣。

• DougBTX 被每千年一次的标志所吸引，认为它们似乎可以被理解，但又不完全如此。这暗示他对时间标记的独特性和神秘性感到着迷，尤其是那些跨越长时间尺度的标记。

• xnx 提到了AI编码工具在创建不同钟表概念中的趣味性，并分享了一个基于"Against the Run"艺术作品的一次性时钟概念链接。这显示了他对结合AI和艺术创作的兴趣，以及对创意时钟设计的探索。

• GuinansEyebrows 回忆了一个旧的iPhone时钟应用"hms"，该应用通过一个长方体显示时间，每个维度对应小时、分钟和秒，形状会随时间增长并重置。这表明他对过去创意时钟设计的怀念，以及对独特时间显示方式的欣赏。

data.title: Robot hand could harvest blackberries better than humans
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 美国阿肯色大学开发了一种用于采摘黑莓的机器人夹爪，旨在解决近年来农场劳动力短缺的问题。该设备由机械工程师Anthony Gunderman及其团队开发，采用软机器人技术，具有三个由柔软材料制成的“手指”，灵感来自郁金香的开放和闭合机制。夹爪的指尖装有力传感器，确保采摘黑莓时不损伤果实。研究团队通过测量专业采摘者的力量，确定了合适的采摘力度。尽管该机器人尚未部署到农场，但未来有望比人工采摘更高效、一致，并可能用于采摘其他柔软水果。此外，该技术还有潜力帮助行动受限的人。

不同观点：

• ortusdux：从实际采摘经验出发，指出采摘动作中对果实成熟度的检查是关键，认为力反馈传感器可以用于检测成熟度，而不仅限于训练用途。

44714954.article_content:
Robot Hand Could Harvest Blackberries Better Than Humans
July 21, 2025
Photo by Chieko Hara
Mechanical engineer Anthony Gunderman holds a prototype of the robotic gripper for picking blackberries.
Fresh, frozen and processed berries are a multi-billion-dollar business in America. In Arkansas alone, fresh-market blackberries contribute $24.3 million each year to the state’s economy. But these delicate blackberries sold in clamshells at supermarkets must be picked by hand, and farm labor has been limited in recent years. A new berry-picking robot gripper developed at the U of A could give growers a high-tech replacement for limited labor availability.
The U.S patent was issued in April to the U of A for the invention “Soft Robotic Gripper for Berry Harvesting.” Technology Ventures, part of the Division of Research and Innovation, secured the patent.
The device was developed by Anthony Gunderman, at the time a Ph.D. student and now an assistant professor in U of A’s Department of Mechanical Engineering, with Yue Chen, a former U of A professor now at Georgia Tech, and Jeremy Collins, then a U of A undergraduate engineering student.
Inspired by Nature
The robotic gripper has three “fingers,” each made of a soft, pliable material. When a “tendon” — in this case a guitar string — is pulled, the fingers retract.
Building robots from pliable materials is known as soft robotics, an approach first used in the 1960s. When designing soft robots, developers often look to nature for models, a process known as biomimicry. For the berry-picking hand, the researchers were inspired by the design of a tulip.
The robotic gripper can harvest delicate blackberries. (Illustration colorized by Ross Maute based on a photo by Anthony Gunderman)
“I was inspired by the way a tulip flower opens and closes when the sunlight hits it,” Gunderman said.
On the tip of each finger is a force sensor, which makes sure the gripper can pluck the berry without crushing it. Roughly handled blackberries can be damaged at harvest or turn red after harvest, a condition called red drupelet reversion
.
Both are undesirable attributes for consumers. The USDA will also reject fresh blackberries with too much damage or too many red drupelets.
To determine the force needed to pick blackberries without damage,
the engineers worked with Andrea Myers, then a graduate student, and Renee Threlfall
, an associate professor in food science with the Arkansas Agricultural Experiment Station, the research arm of the U of A System’s statewide Division of Agriculture.
The team attached sensors to the fingertips of experienced blackberry pickers and measured how much force they applied while harvesting a berry.
Before the robot can be deployed on farms, the computer vision and positioning technologies that would let it find and reach for berries on the plant still need to be developed.
Today, heartier fruits like blueberries and pears are commonly harvested by machines. And rougher automated harvesting machines are used for blackberries that will be frozen or processed.
Better than a human
The human hand can adapt to many tasks. But Gunderman thinks one day the robotic hand could be better at picking blackberries.
“When we’re talking about one specific task, it is certainly the case that you could design something that is better than the human hand for that one specific task,” he said.
The robotic gripper could also be more consistent than human workers.
“Depending on if you have a brand-new hand harvester or someone who’s been doing it for decades, you will get vastly different berry quality,” Gunderman said.
The gripper could also be used to pick other soft fruits, such as raspberries.
The robotic gripper was tested on a range of objects, from hard items like a jar of pears and a can of beans to soft, flexible objects like a bag of potato chips and a T-shirt. The soft gripper, Gunderman said, might also be a tool for people with limited mobility due to injury or age.
Researchers measured the force needed to pick blackberries without damage. (Photo by Anthony Gunderman, University of Arkansas and University of Arkansas System Division of Agriculture)
About the University of Arkansas:
As Arkansas' flagship institution, the U of A provides an internationally competitive education in more than 200 academic programs. Founded in 1871, the U of A contributes more than
$3 billion to Arkansas’ economy
through the teaching of new knowledge and skills, entrepreneurship and job development, discovery through research and creative activity while also providing training for professional disciplines. The Carnegie Foundation classifies the U of A among the few U.S. colleges and universities with the highest level of research activity.
U.S. News & World Report
ranks the U of A among the top public universities in the nation. See how the U of A works to build a better world at
Arkansas Research and Economic Development News.
Contacts
Anthony Gunderman, assistant professor, Mechanical E

data.title: Claude Code weekly rate limits
data.author: thebestmoshe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anthropic对Claude使用设置的周限制及其影响

不同观点：
• Wowfunhappy：对每周限制感到紧张，担心一旦达到限制，整个星期都无法使用已习惯的工具。他质疑Anthropic所说的5%用户受影响的声明，认为这个比例过高。
• Jimbo808：不喜欢使用有限资源的感觉，习惯于互联网和短信等不限量服务。认为当前的定价模式让人感觉不好。
• OtherShrezzing：认为Anthropic的邮件不够具体，无法判断自己是否在受限的5%用户中。对"5%"的定义表示怀疑，认为这可能涵盖了大多数活跃用户。
• Strictnein：对"Max 20x"和"Max 5x"计划的资源分配感到困惑，质疑为何"Max 20x"不是"Max 5x"的四倍，而仅是略多。
• Alwillis：引用Anthropic的Reddit账号，提到一个用户在$200的套餐中消耗了数万美元的模型使用量。认为新限制是为了确保公平和防止账户共享及转售。
• Serf：认为$200的月套餐不够，需要一个不受时间限制和强制休息的方案。对"35小时"的限制表示不满，认为这在实际使用中根本不够。
• Submeta：认为Anthropic的解释模糊，缺乏对使用量的透明度。质疑Anthropic是否真的在针对滥用用户，还是只是为了限制访问找借口。
• Rstupek：认为"24/7运行Claude"的用户导致了限制措施，对这种行为表示不满。
• Wg0：认为滥用问题确实存在，但AI公司更多是受贪婪驱动，等待高估值收购。
• Jjcm：认为应该采用计量收费方案，而不是固定费用计划。指出AI公司正在调整限制以应对极端用户，但这导致了用户对价格的更多关注。
• Data-ottawa：认为5%的限制比例过高，质疑这是基于用户数量的任意削减。对新功能（如子代理）是否增加使用量表示担忧。
• Steve_adams_86：自认为在95%不受限的用户中，对那些轻易达到限制的用户行为感到好奇，并认为一些时间远离工具反而有助于保持思路清晰。
• Neom：正在开发一个编码代理，征求其他开发者对定价和可预测性的意见，担心复杂的信用系统不被用户接受。
• Swalsh：要求明确显示使用限制和已用量，以便用户清楚自己的使用情况。
• Sauwan：希望看到自己之前月份的使用情况，以判断是否会受到限制，对自己是否在5%中缺乏认知。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Anthropic对用户使用Claude设置的每周限制是否合理及其透明度问题。
• 用户对定价模式、限制的具体影响以及如何避免滥用行为存在不同看法。
• 一些用户对Anthropic的解释和沟通方式表示不满，认为缺乏具体细节和透明度。
• 部分用户对如何有效管理使用量和定价方案提出了自己的建议和看法。

data.title: Sign in with Google in Chrome
data.author: frizlab
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了在使用不同浏览器访问如Yelp等网站时遇到的"使用Google登录"提示问题。在Safari和Firefox中，这些提示会频繁出现，但Google Chrome中不会显示。通过在Safari中模拟Chrome的User-Agent，可以避免看到这些提示。然而，Chrome自身会有一个独特的One Tap对话框提示，这是浏览器原生界面的一部分，无法通过扩展如StopTheMadness Pro隐藏。用户可以在Chrome设置中通过输入特定地址（chrome://settings/content/federatedIdentityApi）并选择“阻止身份服务登录提示”来禁用此对话框。文章最后指出，这是Google通过Chrome获得优势的又一个例子。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google登录弹窗及其相关问题（隐私、用户体验、数据追踪）

不同观点：
• cosmotic认为谷歌登录弹窗应被视为违法。理由是该弹窗容易导致用户误点击，从而在未经用户授权的情况下将个人身份信息（PII）发送给不信任的第三方。这种设计严重侵犯了用户的隐私权。

• hnuser123456对弹窗有部分理解，并提到自己曾遇到登录问题，包括重定向循环和密码重置邮件未收到的情况。该用户提到，尽管弹窗令人困扰，但在某些情况下（如Chrome自动登录）却解决了问题，表明弹窗在特定情境下有其实际用途。

• josteink指出用户其实可以手动禁用该弹窗，但前提是需要登录Google账户并设置偏好选项。然而，josteink认为这种做法实际上是让Google能够通过ID和会话cookie追踪用户的活动，认为这是一种变相的“敲诈”，因为用户为了避免弹窗必须牺牲部分隐私。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于谷歌登录弹窗对用户隐私的影响。cosmotic和josteink都认为这种设计侵犯了用户隐私，但cosmotic更关注误点击导致的未经授权的数据共享，而josteink则强调禁用弹窗的前提是让Google追踪用户，这是不合理的“交易”。
• 另一个讨论点是弹窗的用户体验问题。hnuser123456指出了网站在登录过程中的技术问题，如重定向循环和密码重置失败，表明弹窗虽然烦人，但在某些情况下提供了便利。
• 最后，josteink提到的“黑mail”观点引发了一个更广泛的讨论，即用户为了避免麻烦（如频繁的弹窗）可能不得不接受某些公司（如Google）的追踪和数据收集政策。

In Safari Advanced Settings, enable âShow features for web developers.â This setting adds a Develop menu to Safariâs main menu bar. The Develop menu includes a User Agent submenu with a list of several web browsers. When you select Google Chrome from the list and then load Yelp, the âSign in with Googleâ banners no longer appear in Safari.
Although Chrome avoids the âSign in with Googleâ banners, Googleâs browser still has its own custom annoyance. If youâre already signed in to your Google account when you visit a participating website such as Yelp, Chrome will display a One Tap dialog.
This dialog differs from the âSign in with Googleâ banners you see in Safari and Firefox in a couple of important ways. First, the Chrome dialog is
not
an element in the web page but rather a part of the Chrome native app user interface. Thus, StopTheMadness Pro cannot hide the dialog. Indeed, while Chrome is displaying the dialog, it blocks
all
Chrome extension popup windows from appearing. Selecting an extension in the Extensions toolbar widget does nothing. (In other words, itâs not a bug in StopTheMadness Pro.)
The second difference is that the Chrome dialog can be disabled in Chromeâs Settings. Enter
chrome://settings/content/federatedIdentityApi
in the address bar to access the setting directly.
Select âBlock sign-in prompts from identity servicesâ to stop the dialogs from appearing in Chrome.
If the courts and antitrust regulators are reading—they probably wonât read my blog, but one can dream—this is yet another example of Google advantaging its own browser Chrome over other web browsers.

data.title: SQLx – The Rust SQL Toolkit
data.author: stmw
data.article_summary: SQLx 是一个用于 Rust 的异步 SQL 工具包，支持 PostgreSQL、MySQL、MariaDB 和 SQLite，强调纯 Rust 实现和运行时无关性。它具有编译时检查查询功能，不使用 DSL。SQLx 提供连接池、行流式处理、自动语句准备和缓存，以及嵌套事务等特性。对于 TLS 支持，SQLx 可与多种运行时（如 tokio、async-std）和 TLS 后端（如 native-tls、rustls）集成。使用时需根据选择的运行时和 TLS 需求在 `Cargo.toml` 中添加相应特性。SQLx 并非 ORM，且自 0.7 版本起移除了 MSSQL 支持，计划在 SQLx Pro 项目中重写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SQLx 库的使用体验与适用场景

不同观点：
• **支持观点（bitbasher）**：
  - 使用 SQLx 结合 PostgreSQL 在生产环境中表现稳定，处理较高查询量时没有问题。
  - 与 Go 相比，使用 Rust 编写 SQL 代码行数减少约 40%，且内存使用更少，CPU 和内存使用随时间推移保持稳定。
  
• **反对观点（thesuperbigfrog）**：
  - 在使用 SQLx 与 SQLite 时遇到了连接池问题，导致数据库在负载下意外断开连接。
  - 问题与具体 GitHub 上的已知问题相关（链接提供），调整连接池参数未能解决问题。
  - 最终通过重构数据层，改用 NoSQL 解决方案绕过问题。
  - 尽管欣赏 SQLx 的设计理念，但对使用 SQLx 与 SQLite 持谨慎态度。

• **中立/比较观点（hyperbrainer）**：
  - 没有使用过 SQLx，但认为最好的 SQL 集成方式是 LINQ，并询问 SQLx 与 LINQ 的比较。

• **反对观点（tmpfs）**：
  - 使用过 SQLx 和其他低级数据库驱动，更偏好不在编译时检查 SQL 的驱动。
  - 初期使用 SQLx 时，难以抽象出底层数据库后端，尽管现在可能已解决。
  - 对于简单应用，开始使用 SQLite 然后切换到 PostgreSQL 是很好的选择。
  - 在尝试将 SQLx 应用与 Docker 集成时遇到麻烦，需要在编译时运行 PostgreSQL，整合 Docker Compose 也很麻烦。
  - 现在不再使用 SQLx，推荐其他库如 sqlite 或 postgres。

补充讨论：
- SQLx 的连接池问题在 SQLite 下表现明显，尤其是高负载多并发场景。
- 不同用户对 SQLx 的使用体验差异较大，主要取决于具体数据库（PostgreSQL vs SQLite）和应用场景。
- 对 SQLx 的编译时检查特性存在争议，部分开发者认为这是优点，而部分开发者认为这增加了复杂性和不便。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某个 puzzle 游戏的概念、难度和演示设计的反馈

不同观点：
• tlh：认为游戏的概念有潜力，但对 puzzle 的难度感到不满意。具体来说，tlh 觉得解谜过程过于直接，只需依次移除字母即可解决问题，缺乏足够的认知挑战。不过，tlh 对游戏的设计表示赞赏，并鼓励继续改进。

• pimlottc：关注游戏的演示动画，建议在“如何游玩”的演示中展示两个单词的动画，以更好地说明“隐藏短语”的功能。这里没有对游戏难度做出评价，而是集中在如何提升用户对游戏机制的理解。

• tgv：与 tlh 类似，tgv 也认为游戏过于简单，并指出自己只犯了一个错误，且得到了错误提示，使得游戏进展较为轻松。tgv 提到自己并非英语母语者，暗示即使对于非母语者来说，游戏难度也偏低。此外，tgv 认为复杂的 puzzle 通常需要更多的反复尝试和回溯，这与当前游戏体验不同。

补充讨论：
• 游戏的难度是争议的焦点，tlh 和 tgv 都认为当前 puzzle 过于简单，缺乏挑战性，但没有提出具体的改进方案。
• tlh 基于自身开发类似游戏（Stackdown）的经验，提供了鼓励性的反馈，并暗示开发者可以通过更多反馈来改进游戏。
• pimlottc 则聚焦于游戏的演示动画，提出了一个具体建议，旨在帮助玩家更好地理解游戏中的“隐藏短语”功能，从而提升用户体验。

总体而言，评论者们都对游戏的潜力持积极态度，但对目前的实现提出了一些改进建议，主要集中在难度调整和演示优化上。

主要讨论点：关于第三颗星际天体3I/ATLAS的发现、大小推断、观测技术及其潜在科学意义的多角度讨论。

不同观点：
• Fripplebubby：认为3I/ATLAS的大小推断是通过概率方法得出的，而不是直接观测。基于过去多年对彗星的观测数据，可以推断该彗星更可能是0.5公里大小，而非10公里，因为根据碰撞破碎的幂律分布规律，大彗星出现的概率极低。

• NitpickLawyer：关注Vera Rubin天文台在发现3I/ATLAS中的作用，指出该天文台设计上就是为了发现类似天体，并认为通过历史数据回溯分析有助于调整观测模型。同时，期待未来更多观测数据，包括来自火星轨道器和JUICE探测器的数据。

• drewg123：提到Rubin天文台的观测显示3I/ATLAS有尘埃尾，但奇怪的是尘埃尾指向太阳，而不是像通常那样远离太阳。并提出是否是减速燃烧的现象。

• supportengineer：表示3I/ATLAS的发现让他想到电影《不要抬头》，暗示天体观测和公众认知之间的关系。

• unsupp0rted：提出一种假设，即3I/ATLAS是否可能“感知”到被观测，尤其是被哈勃望远镜观测，并开玩笑地提到“居民正在扫描我们”。

• 科学幻想的延伸：unsupp0rted的评论虽然带有幽默和科幻色彩，但也引发了关于星际天体是否可能具有“自我意识”或被高级文明观测的有趣讨论。

总结：评论主要围绕3I/ATLAS的大小推断、观测技术和科学意义展开，包含了实际观测数据分析、技术应用以及一些幽默和科幻的联想。

data.title: Visa and Mastercard are getting overwhelmed by gamer fury over censorship
data.author: mrzool
data.article_summary: 游戏玩家不满Steam和itch.io下架成人游戏，将愤怒转向支付处理公司Visa和Mastercard，发起大规模邮件和电话抗议活动。玩家认为这些支付公司是下架的幕后推手，尽管其规则模糊。玩家在社交媒体上组织动员，通过打电话和发邮件施压，意图通过制造沟通障碍，迫使支付公司关注问题。尽管客服代表表示无权改变政策，玩家仍坚持通过占用线路和回拨占用其他客户的服务资源。玩家还向高管发送邮件，并保持礼貌态度以增加影响力。同时，有组织提供资源和脚本帮助玩家参与抗议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：支付处理公司作为 gatekeeper 对内容进行审查的争议

不同观点：
• Kapura：认为少数人基于个人喜恶推动审查是荒谬的，特别是当这些内容并没有强迫任何人消费时。主张应继续对支付处理公司施压，同时也需抵制那些试图决定其他成年人如何支配时间的人。
• numpad0：指出最初被下架的是色情内容，但现在审查范围已扩展到恐怖游戏，如《Mouthwashing(2024)》。担忧审查范围会继续扩大。
• duxup：批评支付处理系统的不透明性，举例一家制作剑的公司无故被禁止使用信用卡支付，且无法得知具体原因或申诉。
• benoau：引用Collective Shout的博客，指出当Steam未回应时，他们转向支付处理公司施压，认为这是有效的策略。
• ThrowawayR2：认为消费者和企业对Visa、Mastercard没有其他选择，主张应向政治人物施压，特别是民主党立法者，以获得支持和选票。
• dehugger：建议Steam改变政策，让成人游戏只能用商店信用购买，以解决支付处理问题。
• tflinton：提醒大家即使某些内容不违法，也可能带来民事问题和风险，支付处理公司可能不得不采取审查措施以规避风险。
• motbus3：感叹当今社会人人想当审查者或统治者，表达对此趋势的不满。
• SilverElfin：认为某些内容应受到严格监管，但私人支付应由政府作为公共服务提供，以避免审查。
• vunderba：提供一个相关的在线请愿链接，呼吁对支付处理公司施压。
• bsenftner：质疑相关文章的真实性，认为其迎合游戏观众，没有实质内容。
• nemomarx：提供信息称Collective Shout通过大量电话成功引起支付公司注意，建议继续保持这种压力。
• 3acctforcom：认为普通人的电话无法影响大公司高层的决策，强调权力运作的现实。
• scirob：询问是否有任何行动可以减少这些公司的权力。
• CivBase：对“玩家愤怒”能否带来实质性改变持怀疑态度，但承认当前的Stop Killing Games活动可能具有一定影响力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于支付处理公司作为gatekeeper审查内容的合理性和合法性，以及应如何有效抵制这种趋势。
• 讨论中涉及的具体案例（如《Mouthwashing(2024)》游戏和制作剑的公司）突显了审查对不同类型内容的影响。
• 建议的应对策略包括向支付处理公司施压、通过政治途径寻求改变、以及利用集体行动引起注意。
• 对当前审查系统的透明度和申诉机制缺失的问题也有较多批评。

44713414.article_content:
News
Visa and Mastercard are getting overwhelmed by gamer fury over censorship
Gamers are sending mass emails and phone calls to major payment processors in protest over Steam and itch.io
by
Patricia Hernandez
Jul 28, 2025, 4:06 PM UTC
Facebook
Link
Image: OppaiMan
In the wake of storefronts
like Steam and itch.io curbing the sale of adult games
, irate fans have started an organized campaign against the payment processors that they believe are responsible for the crackdown. While the movement is still in its early stages, people are mobilizing with an eye toward overwhelming communication lines at companies like Visa and Mastercard in a way that will make the concern impossible to ignore.
On social media sites like Reddit and Bluesky, people are urging one another to get into contact with Visa and Mastercard through emails and phone calls. Visa and Mastercard have become the targets of interest because
the affected storefronts
both say that their decisions around adult games were motivated by the danger of losing the ability to use major payment processors while selling games. These payment processors have their own rules regarding usage, but they are vaguely defined. But losing infrastructure like this could impact audiences well beyond those who care about sex games, spokespeople for Valve and itch.io said.
In a now-deleted post on the Steam subreddit with over 17,000 upvotes
, commenters say that customer service representatives for both payment processors seem to already be aware of the problem. Sometimes, the representatives will say that they’ve gotten multiple calls on the subject of adult game censorship, but that they can’t really do anything about it.
The folks applying pressure know that someone at a call center has limited power in a scenario like this one; typically, agents are equipped to handle standard customer issues like payment fraud or credit card loss. But the point isn’t to enact change through a specific phone call: It’s to cause enough disruption that the ruckus theoretically starts costing payment processors money.
“Emails can be ignored, but a very very long queue making it near impossible for other clients to get in will help a lot as well,” reads the top comment on the Reddit thread. In that same thread, people say that they’re hanging onto the call even if the operator says that they’ll experience multi-hour wait times presumably caused by similar calls gunking up the lines. Beyond the stubbornness factor, the tactic is motivated by the knowledge that most customer service systems will put people who opt for call-backs in a lower priority queue, as anyone who opts in likely doesn’t have an emergency going on.
Image: OppaiMan
“Do both,” one commenter suggests. “Get the call back, to gum up the call back queue. Then call in again and wait to gum up the live queue.”
People are also using email to voice their concerns directly to the executives at both Visa and Mastercard, payment processors that activist group Collective Shout called out by name in their open letter requesting that adult games get pulled. Emails are also getting sent to customer service. In light of the coordinated effort, many people are getting a pre-written response that reads:
Thank you for reaching out and sharing your perspective. As a global company, we follow the laws and regulations everywhere we do business. While we explicitly prohibit illegal activity on our network, we are equally committed to protecting legal commerce. If a transaction is legal, our policy is to process the transaction. We do not make moral judgments on legal purchases made by consumers. Visa does not moderate content sold by merchants, nor do we have visibility into the specific goods or services sold when we process a transaction. When a legally operating merchant faces an elevated risk of illegal activity, we require enhanced safeguards for the banks supporting those merchants. For more information on Visa’s policies, please visit our network integrity page on Visa.com. Thank you for writing.
On platforms like Bluesky, resources are being shared to help people know who to contact and how, including possible scripts for talking to representatives or sending emails. A website has been set up with the explicit purpose of arming concerned onlookers with the tools and knowledge necessary to do their part in the campaign.
Through it all, gamers are telling one another to remain cordial during any interactions with payment processors, especially when dealing with low-level workers who are just trying to do their job. For executives, the purpose of maintaining a considerate tone is to help the people in power take the issue seriously.
The strategy is impressive in its depth and breadth of execution. While some charge in with an activist bent, others say that
they’re pretending to be confused customers
who want to know why they can’t use Visa or Mastercard to buy their favorite games.

data.title: ‘I witnessed war crimes’ in Gaza – former worker at GHF aid site [video]
data.author: nathanyz
data.article_summary: 一名退休的美国特种部队军官安东尼·阿吉拉尔向BBC透露，他因目睹以色列国防军在加沙人道主义基金会（GHF）援助点对巴勒斯坦平民进行 brutality and use of indiscriminate and unnecessary force而辞职。他称，这是他职业生涯中见过对无武装、饥饿平民最残酷的行动。与此同时，BBC还报道了以色列与伊朗之间的持续冲突，包括导弹袭击和双方的报复行动，造成了严重破坏和伤亡。美国也加入了打击伊朗的行动，使得局势更加复杂。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕以色列行为及其引发的社会和技术领域的讨论

不同观点：
• **calmbonsai的观点**：认为以色列国防军（IDF）在2024年4月对世界中央厨房（World Central Kitchen）工作人员开火并不令人惊讶，同时指出越来越多视频揭示了这些暴行。该评论暗示了对以色列军事行动的批评，并强调媒体揭露的重要性。

• **pavlov的观点**：认为许多科技公司和初创企业位于以色列，因此这个话题与技术社区相关。该评论从技术产业角度出发，试图将以色列问题与技术讨论联系起来，认为其具有相关性。

• **fuck_AI的观点**：支持通过抵制、撤资和制裁（BDS）运动来对抗以色列的政策，认为BDS运动的禁止恰恰说明了其有效性。该评论明确表达了对BDS策略的支持，并暗示以色列对该运动的反对是因为其威胁到了以色列。

• **crystal_revenge的观点**：通过个人经历反思教育中对大屠杀及其他种族灭绝的学习，对比如今对种族灭绝话题的禁忌性，尤其提到在公开场合批评以色列国家政策可能会带来风险。该评论还提到社交媒体上信息操纵的问题，认为存在不自然的负面投票和评论标记现象。

• **oulipo的观点**：强烈主张以色列应因其不可原谅的罪行而受到惩罚，语气坚决，表明了对以色列行为的严厉谴责。

补充讨论：
- **信息操纵与言论自由**：crystal_revenge提到社交媒体上存在信息操纵现象，并指出评论中的一些负面反应并非自然产生，暗示可能有组织的舆论控制。
- **言论风险**：crystal_revenge还提到在公开场合表达对以色列的批评存在风险，甚至需要使用匿名账户以避免风险，这引发了对言论自由和言论环境安全的关注。
- **教育与现实对比**：crystal_revenge通过对比90年代的教育内容和当前对种族灭绝话题的态度变化，提出了对社会价值观演变的反思。

争议焦点：
- **以色列行为的正当性**：不同评论者对以色列军事和政治行为的正当性持不同看法，部分人强烈谴责（calmbonsai、oulipo），而pavlov则试图从技术产业角度淡化讨论的敏感性。
- **BDS运动的有效性与合法性**：fuck_AI认为BDS是有效的，而其他人没有直接回应这一观点，但整体讨论显示出对以色列政策的不同态度，表明BDS是一个有争议的话题。

He added that in his entire career he has never witnessed such a level of "brutality and use of indiscriminate and unnecessary force against a civilian population, an unarmed, starving population".

data.author: samuli

44713945.article_content:
Is SoftBank Still Backing OpenAI?
Edward Zitron
Jul 24, 2025
37 min read
Earlier in the week,
the Wall Street Journal reported
that SoftBank and OpenAI's "$500 billion" "AI Project" was now setting a "more modest goal of building a small data center by year-end."
To quote:
A $500 billion effort unveiled
at the White House
to supercharge the U.S.’s artificial-intelligence ambitions has struggled to get off the ground and has sharply scaled back its near-term plans.
Six months after Japanese billionaire Masayoshi Son stood shoulder to shoulder with Sam Altman and President
Trump
to announce the Stargate project, the newly formed company charged with making it happen has yet to complete a single deal for a data center.
One might be forgiven for being a little confused here, as there is, apparently, a Stargate Data Center being built in Abilene Texas. Yet the Journal added another detail:
Altman has used the Stargate name, shared with a 1994 Kurt Russell film about aliens who teleport to ancient Egypt, on projects that aren’t being financed by the partnership between OpenAI and SoftBank. The trademark to Stargate is held by SoftBank, according to public filings.
For instance, OpenAI refers to a data center in Abilene, Texas, and another it agreed in March to use in Denton, Texas, as part of Stargate even though they are being done without SoftBank, some of the people familiar with the matter said.
Confusing, right? One might also be confused by the Bloomberg story called "
Inside The First Stargate AI Data Center
," which had the subheadline "OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank hope that the site in Texas is the first of many across the US." More-confusingly, the piece talked about Stargate LLC, which OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank were (allegedly) shareholders of.
Yet I have confirmed that SoftBank never, ever had any involvement with the site in Abilene Texas. It didn't fund it, it didn't build it, it didn't choose the site and, in fact, does not appear to have anything to do with
any
data center that OpenAI uses. The data center many, many reporters have referred to as "Stargate" has nothing to do with the "Stargate data center project."  Any reports suggesting otherwise are wrong, and I believe that this is a conscious attempt at misleading the public by OpenAI and SoftBank.
I confirmed the following with a PR representative from Crusoe, one of the developers of the site in Abilene Texas:
Funding for construction of [the] Abilene data center is a JV between Crusoe, Blue Owl and Primary Digital Infrastructure. Confirming that Softbank is not and has not been involved in the funding for its construction.
And, as a reminder,
Stargate as an entity was never formed
—
my source being the CEO of Oracle Safra Catz on Oracle’s earnings call
.
This is an astonishing — and egregious — act of misinformation on the part of Sam Altman and OpenAI. By my count,
at
least
15
different
stories attribute the Abilene Texas data center to the Stargate project, despite the fact that SoftBank was never and has never been involved. One would forgive anyone who got this wrong, because
OpenAI itself engaged in the deliberate deception in its own announcement of the Stargate Project
[emphasis mine]:
The initial equity funders in Stargate are SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX. SoftBank and OpenAI are the lead partners for Stargate, with SoftBank having financial responsibility and OpenAI having operational responsibility. Masayoshi Son will be the chairman.
Arm, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, and OpenAI are the key initial technology partners. The buildout is currently underway,
starting in Texas
, and we are evaluating potential sites across the country for more campuses as we finalize definitive agreements.
You can weasel-word all you want about how nobody has directly reported that SoftBank was or was not part of Abilene. This is a deliberate, intentional deception, perpetrated by OpenAI and SoftBank, who deliberately misled both the public and the press as a means of keeping up the appearance that SoftBank was deeply involved in (and financially obligated to) the Abilene site.
Based on reporting that existed at the time but was never drawn together, it appears that Abilene was earmarked
by Microsoft
for OpenAI's use as early as July 2024, and never involved SoftBank in any way, shape or form. The "Stargate" Project, as reported,
was over six months old when it was announced in January 2025, and there have been no additional sites added other than Abilene.
In simpler terms,
Stargate does not exist other than as a name that Sam Altman gives things to make them feel more special than they are, and SoftBank was never involved.
Stargate does not exist as reported.
The use of the term "Stargate" is an intentional act of deceit, but beneath the surface lies, in my mind, a much bigger story. Furthermore, I believe this deceit means that we should review any and all promises made by OpenAI and SoftBank, and reconsider any and all statements they've made,

44711940.article_content:
#
Requesting funding for 90s.dev
Hi everyone. A couple months ago I posted 90s.dev under the wrong title.
I called it a video game maker, because that’s the
vision
I had for it.
But I posted it prematurely, and it wasn’t yet a video game maker.
It was
an retro os web environment
, which I planned to make a game maker
in
.
So a lot of you showed interest, but I asked you to come back later.
Well, the problem was that I need to be monetized for my efforts on it.
I have practically no spare time due to my state and duties in life.
I
want
to work on it, but I had to focus on making money.
I was able to work on it for 3 months because I burned through
all my savings
.
Plus it’s entirely front-end code, which is inherently hard to monetize.
This is the age old problem of how to fund open source.
So I had an idea that I thought might be a good solution.
I would use GitHub Sponsors, but as a way to pay me hourly.
Instead of tiers, you would just specify an amount,
and for each $25 that I receive, I would work one hour on 90s.dev.
Since this would essentially be employment, I should share my resume.
90s.dev
App source:
https://github.com/sdegutis/os.90s.dev
Docs source:
https://github.com/sdegutis/90s.dev
I spent about 3 months on it, working ~14 hours a day, 6-7 days a week
[1]
.
It was my first time learning about and using most web worker features.
I had to learn about threads, broadcast channels, message ports, etc.
(At one point it used a shared worker for the file system but I took it out.)
hram.dev
– my day job
Old portfolio
To help fund this open source project,
go to
https://github.com/sponsors/sdegutis
.
Thanks for reading this, and I hope you have a lovely day.
See
https://github.com/sdegutis/os.90s.dev/graphs/code-frequency
and
https://github.com/sdegutis/90s.dev/graphs/code-frequency
↩︎

data.title: Num2words PyPI Package Compromised
data.author: varunsharma07
data.article_summary: 2025年7月28日，Python社区发现num2words库的0.5.15版本在PyPI上发布，但其GitHub官方库中没有对应标签，可能遭到 compromise。安全研究员@johnk3r指出，该事件疑似与曾发动供应链攻击的“Scavenger”黑客组织有关。该恶意版本发布后不久，自动化工具已开始尝试将其集成到项目中。尽管PyPI迅速下架了该版本，但此事件暴露了Python生态系统的供应链安全风险。建议开发者检查并降级至安全版本，并加强安全措施。企业用户可使用StepSecurity等工具增强CI/CD管道的安全性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python库num2words v0.5.15在没有代码库标签的情况下发布，并且与已知的威胁行为者相关联，引发了安全性和可信度问题。

不同观点：
• 观点一：这个事件暴露了开源项目在安全方面的脆弱性。varunsharma07认为，这种未标记版本发布以及与威胁行为者相关联的情况，反映了开源社区在安全审查和版本控制上的不足，可能会让使用者暴露于潜在的安全威胁中。

• 观点二：部分用户认为这可能是一个无意的错误或疏忽。一些评论者指出，版本标签缺失和与威胁行为者关联不一定是恶意的，可能只是维护者的操作失误，或者由于账户被盗用所致。他们强调在进一步调查之前不应过早下结论。

Supply Chain Security Alert: num2words PyPI Package Shows Signs of Compromise
Popular Python Package num2words v0.5.15 Published Without Repository Tag, Linked to Known Threat Actor
Ashish Kurmi
View LinkedIn
July 28, 2025
Share on X

Follow our RSS feed

Loading nav...
Key Takeaways
The Python package num2words version 0.5.15 was published to PyPI without a corresponding tag in the official GitHub repository
Security researcher
@johnk3r
identified potential links to the "Scavenger" threat actor, known for previous supply chain attacks
PyPI has removed the compromised package, preventing further installations
This incident highlights the ongoing risks in the Python ecosystem's supply chain security
The Incident
On July 28, 2025, the Python community was alerted to a potential supply chain attack involving the popular num2words package. Version 0.5.15 of this widely-used library for converting numbers to words was published to PyPI approximately 2 hours before being flagged as potentially compromised.
â
PyPI release history showing the suspicious v0.5.15 release published "about 2 hours ago"
Red Flags and Initial Detection
The compromise was first identified through several concerning indicators:
Missing Repository Tag
: Unlike previous releases, version 0.5.15 was published to PyPI without a corresponding tag in the official GitHub repository at
https://github.com/savoirfairelinux/num2words/tags
Timing Discrepancy
: The package appeared on PyPI without any associated commits or release activities in the source repository
Community Alert
: Security researcher @johnk3r quickly raised the alarm on social media, warning the community about potential compromise
GitHub repository tags showing the absence of v0.5.15, while previous versions (v0.5.14, v0.5.13, etc.) all have corresponding tags
The Scavenger Connection
According to @johnk3r's analysis, early indicators suggest this incident may be linked to "Scavenger," a threat actor previously associated with software supply chain intrusions. While full attribution requires deeper investigation, the modus operandi matches previous attacks:
Publishing malicious versions of legitimate packages
Exploiting the trust users place in established package names
Targeting popular packages to maximize potential impact
https://x.com/johnk3r/status/1949862337340461528
Credit:
https://x.com/johnk3r/status/1949862337340461528/photo/1
Automated Tools Already Upgrading to Malicious Version
Despite the quick response, automated dependency management tools had already begun creating pull requests to upgrade projects to the compromised version. A GitHub search reveals numerous automated PRs attempting to update num2words to version 0.5.15, demonstrating how quickly malicious packages can propagate through the ecosystem. Here is a sample pull request:
https://github.com/tarcisio-sousa/agiliza/pull/1075
Impact and Response
The num2words package is a widely-used Python library that provides functionality to convert numbers into their word representations across multiple languages. With thousands of downloads daily, any compromise could have had significant reach across the Python ecosystem.
Fortunately, the rapid response from the community and PyPI administrators helped contain the potential damage:
Quick Detection
: The suspicious release was identified within hours of publication
Swift Action
: PyPI removed the compromised package, preventing new installations
Community Warning
: Security alerts spread quickly through social media and developer channels
What You Should Do
If you use num2words in your projects:
Check Your Environment
â
Run
pip list | grep num2words
to verify which version you have installed
â
Downgrade if Necessary
f you have v0.5.15 installed, immediately downgrade to v0.5.14 using
pip install num2words==0.5.14
â
Audit Your Systems
Review logs and systems that may have installed the compromised version
â
Update Security Practices
Consider implementing additional supply chain security measures

data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了希特勒上台初期试图控制德国央行（Reichsbank）的努力，以及时任央行行长汉斯·路德（Hans Luther）如何抵制这些压力。1933年1月30日，希特勒就任总理数小时后，纳粹冲锋队强行进入央行并升起纳粹旗帜，路德立即向希特勒抗议，强调央行是独立机构，最终纳粹旗帜被撤下。希特勒试图逼迫路德辞职，但由于央行受1924年法律保护，其行长由包括国际银行家在内的14人董事会任命，希特勒无法直接将其撤职。路德凭借其丰富的政治和经济经验，以及在金融危机中的出色表现，成功保住了职位。文章还提到希特勒通过大规模清洗魏玛共和国公务员以巩固权力，但在此过程中无法撼动路德在央行的地位。

Adolf Hitler’s first week
s as chancellor were filled with so many excesses and outrages—crushing states’ rights, curtailing civil liberties, intimidating opponents, rewriting election laws, raising tariffs—that it was easy to overlook one of his prime targets: the German central bank.
The Reichsbank president was a man named Hans Luther, a fiscal conservative who subscribed to the “golden rule” of banking, which stipulated that a country’s indebtedness should never exceed its obligations. In his adherence to protocol and policy, Luther could be “holier than the Pope,” according to Lutz Schwerin von Krosigk, who served as the German finance minister from 1932 to 1945.
On the afternoon of Monday, January 30, 1933, just hours after Hitler’s appointment as chancellor, Luther stood in Hitler’s office with a complaint. Nazi storm troopers, known as the SA, had forced their way into the Reichsbank building in central Berlin, despite what Luther described as “emphatic protests” by bank personnel, and hoisted a swastika flag over the bank.
“I pointed out to Hitler that the SA actions were against the law,” Luther recalled, “to which Hitler immediately answered that this was a revolution.” Luther informed Hitler in no uncertain terms that the Reichsbank was not part of his revolution. It was an independent fiscal entity with an international board of directors. If any flag were to be flying over the bank, it would be the national colors, not the banner of his political party. The next morning, the swastika flag was gone.
On Hitler’s first full day in office, rumors circulated that he wanted Luther gone. Alfred Kliefoth, the chargé d’affaires at the United States embassy in Berlin, dispatched a memorandum to the State Department: “I have been informed, in confidence, by Dr. Ritter, the Chief Economist in the Foreign Office, that the new Government intends to exert pressure on Dr. Luther to resign.” The Social Democratic daily,
Vorwärts
, declared in a banner headline that the Hitler government was "demanding Luther's head."
H
itler’s rumored plans
to oust the Reichsbank chief came amid a massive purge of the Weimar Republic’s civil service. Senior officials who had served for decades were fired. Hitler assigned his chief lieutenant, Hermann Göring, to clean house in Prussia, the largest of Germany’s 17 federated states. When Göring entered the Prussian government offices in central Berlin, he told Rudolf Diels, the head of the Prussian political police, “I want nothing to do with the scoundrels sitting here in this building.” When Diels tried to defend one senior colleague, Göring responded by firing the colleague on the spot.
Timothy W. Ryback: How Hitler dismantled a democracy in 53 days
A memorandum was circulated to all state civil servants demanding blind loyalty to the Hitler government. Anyone who did not feel they could support Hitler and his policies, Göring added, should do the “honorable” thing and resign. The
Berliner Morgenpost
observed that Hitler was clearly working to “transform the state bureaucracy from the most senior positions down to the administrative levels to align with his political positions.” In a speech on March 11, Göring compared the Nazi’s draconian measures to cutting wood: “When you chop, chips fly.”
Despite Hitler’s heavy-handed assault on the government bureaucracy,  he could not touch Hans Luther. According to a 1924 law, the Reichsbank was independent of the elected government; the Reichsbank president served at the discretion of a 14-member board, which included seven international bankers and economists. Even Reich President Paul von Hindenburg, the ultimate constitutional authority, possessed the power only to confirm the appointment of the Reichsbank president, not to dismiss him. The Reich president headed the state and commanded the military, and the Reich chancellor ran the government, but the Reichsbank controlled the currency and the economy.
Luther brandished his independence and power with confidence and control. He had already served as finance minister and had also done a stint as chancellor. He understood both politics and economics. In 1923, Luther had designed the rescue plan that saved Germany from the inflation crisis that saw Germans pushing wheelbarrows full of cash through the streets to buy a loaf of bread. After the global market crash of 1929, he had guided Germany back to employment stability and production growth by the spring of 1932. Great Britain emerged from the crisis with twice the national debt of Germany. France’s was fourfold.
The New York Times
reported that Luther had “stood like a rock” amid the global financial turmoil. The newspaper
Vossische Zeitung
described Luther as “equal to any storm.”

44714648.article_content:
Thank-you! You've been successfully added to the Marginal Revolution email subscription list.
Sorry people, but you can fill in the links with Perplexity and Grok, both great for this purpose.
Olivier Blanchard is upset that Europe got such a raw deal, various people in the FT agree.  I would say that is itself data about broader European economic and security policies, and needs to be taken very seriously.  The Europeans are not stupid negotiators by any means, rather they are in a weak negotiating position for reasons that are largely their own fault and reflect underlying weaknesses of their basic economic and political model.
You can hate what Trump did, but for a “stupid” administration they, by their own standards at least, did a remarkably good job of it.
Justin Wolfers seems upset that Trump is raising taxes on Americans.  (I am too!)  But that feels kind of weird to me.  And it is nice to see that Europeans get somewhat lower taxes, though many European leaders are upset about that.  They should in fact buy more from the United States, and their non-tariff barriers are significant.
Conor Sen notes that the USA has come up with a multi-trillion revenue source that does not seem to diminish corporate profitability, https://x.com/conorsen/status/1949785522567549283?s=61, and he is wondering how exactly people will react to that.
We can all agree that negative externalities are what should be taxed!
But those policies typically are unpopular, so in some instances you will understand public affairs more clearly by switching to the “what will be done?” perspective, rather than the “what should be done?” stance.
My best guess is that these tariffs will stick for the most part, and that you are seeing some early major steps for how the U.S. will resolve its fiscal position.  Higher inflation will come too, and fiscally we will muddle through, albeit with notably lower real wages.
(To be clear, for a long time I have stated that I prefer to cut back on government-subsidized health care, rather than to lower real wages through these other means.  You can always use the extra money and try to buy back some health!  But I also never have thought I was going to get my way.  When Matt Yglesias tells you that “health care polls well,” you should take that seriously and Matt also should realize a bit that puts him in more of the pro-Trump, pro-tariff camp than he might like to think.)
I think a Democratic administration, whenever we get one next, would rather spend the revenue from the tariffs than repeal them.  By then the tariffs also will be what I call “emotionally internalized.”  And the Democrats have not loved free trade for a long time anyway, despite their current rhetorical moves toward criticizing the Trumpers.
So most of all we need to revise our estimates of what the political equilibrium looks like here.  We are receiving major pieces of information, and we must update our vision of the world to come.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章分析了字节跳动旗下的Trae IDE（基于Visual Studio Code的 fork）的性能和隐私问题。研究发现，Trae IDE存在资源消耗过多（33个进程，5.7 GB内存，远超VSCode的9个进程和0.9 GB内存）以及持续发送遥测数据的问题，即便用户已关闭遥测功能。测试还显示，Trae与字节跳动基础设施保持定期连接，传输大量数据，且包含用户ID等信息。虽然版本2.0.2解决了部分进程过多的问题，但遥测数据传输问题仍未得到有效解决。文章揭示了Trae IDE在性能和隐私管理上的不足及其对社区反馈的处理方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对不同IDE和编辑器中遥测（telemetry）功能的分析和争议

不同观点：
• **对测试方法的质疑**：
  - [kiitos] 认为在屏幕分享中，用户更改了遥测选项但没有重启编辑器，这样的测试无法得出有效结论。重启编辑器可能是必要的步骤。
  
• **推荐替代IDE**：
  - [barkingcat] 推荐了TheiaIDE，这是一个类似VSCode的编辑器，曾经比较粗糙，但现在有了显著改进，并被一些大公司使用。该用户认为TheiaIDE是一个值得考虑的替代方案。

• **对CapCut桌面版遥测的关注**：
  - [fjghajkhdfgjlk] 对ByteDance的CapCut视频编辑器感兴趣，认为其用户界面优秀，但担心其中可能包含遥测或间谍软件，希望看到相关分析。

• **对其他IDE（如Kiro）的分析请求**：
  - [spyridonas] 请求对AWS的Kiro（VSCode的AWS分支）进行遥测实践分析，表现出对不同平台数据收集实践的关注。

• **对遥测数据类型的接受度**：
  - [cchance] 认为所收集的系统信息、使用模式和性能指标等数据并不是特别敏感或冒犯，表示可以接受。

• **对遥测禁用问题的质疑**：
  - [drewbitt] 质疑为什么即使少数用户关闭了遥测功能，某些公司仍然不愿意完全禁用它。

• **对具体IDE身份的困惑**：
  - [theusus] 指出讨论中没有明确提到所讨论的IDE是哪一个，并提供了可能的链接，提醒不要误伤。

• **使用工具屏蔽遥测的建议**：
  - [efitz] 建议使用pi-hole屏蔽遥测端点，并通过观察功能是否正常来判断遥测的必要性。同时批评了某些公司无视用户偏好的行为。

• **对遥测数据安全的担忧**：
  - [leetbulb] 担心遥测事件可能被用来泄露任意数据（如源代码），指出通过特定方式编码数据的可能性。

• **对开源项目遥测的观察**：
  - [drewbitt] 指出Bytedance的trae-agent项目似乎没有包含遥测。

• **对使用专有软件的批评**：
  - [isatty] 质疑人们为什么会使用明显的“间谍软件”而不选择自由软件。

• **对不同公司遥测的比较**：
  - [nottorp] 比较了Bytedance和Microsoft的遥测，认为除了数据被发送到不同服务器外，没有太大区别。

补充讨论：
• **对透明度和用户控制的呼吁**：
  - [stan_kirdey] 赞扬了OP的详细分析，并呼吁IDE开发商通过默认选择加入遥测和提供真正的关闭选项来获得用户信任。

总体来看，讨论围绕遥测的功能、数据收集的合理性、对专有软件和自由软件的选择以及如何有效屏蔽或减少遥测展开。争议的焦点在于用户是否能有效关闭遥测功能以及遥测数据的安全性和透明度。

Performance and Telemetry Analysis of Trae IDE: A Deep Dive into ByteDance's VSCode Fork
Executive Summary
This analysis examines concerning performance and privacy issues discovered in Trae IDE, ByteDance's fork of Visual Studio Code. Key findings include excessive resource consumption (33 processes vs 9 in VSCode), persistent telemetry transmission despite user settings, and concerning community management practices.
1. Background and Methodology
During evaluation of development environments for a personal project, I conducted a comparative analysis of three popular IDEs: Visual Studio Code, Cursor, and Trae (ByteDance's VSCode fork). This analysis revealed significant discrepancies in resource usage and network behavior that warranted deeper investigation.
Testing Environment:
OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro
CPU: Intel Core™ i7-14700KF
RAM: 64GB
Test Project: Identical codebase loaded in each IDE
Monitoring Tools: System Informer, Fiddler Everywhere
2. Resource Consumption Analysis
Process Count and Memory Usage

After reporting this issue on Trae's Discord server (

3. Network Traffic and Telemetry Investigation
Now this is where the fun begins, network monitoring revealed persistent outbound connections to ByteDance infrastructure:

request frequency to the batch collection endpoint
With telemetry disabled, these calls can still quickly accumulate—during testing, a single batch reached up to 53,606 bytes. While actively using the editor, I observed around 500 calls within ~7 minutes, totaling up to 26 MB of data transferred in that short timeframe.

data.title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (July 2025)
data.author: david927
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各位用户在Hacker News上分享他们正在进行的项目，涵盖了从技术工具、教育平台到娱乐和实用工具等多个领域的开发和优化。

不同观点：
• [alextousss] 认为他们的蚊子 killing 无人机(Tornyol)可以有效对抗疟疾，相比传统方法如蚊帐(ITNs)更具优势。无人机的超声波探测和导弹控制理论的撞击机制能够快速覆盖大面积区域。
• [m-a-t-t-i] 正在开发一种无需工具或机器的手工服装构建块，类似于服装版的乐高，旨在让用户能够自由构建服装和配件。
• [marginalia_nu] 正在优化搜索索引代码，虽然新代码在基准测试中速度更快，但在实际运行中却因内存分页问题导致更慢。他们计划通过自定义缓冲池来解决该问题。
• [possiblelion] 正在开发一个模拟器，旨在让用户通过操作防御系统来学习空中防御知识，尤其适用于教学和演练，如乌克兰和中东的场景。

补充讨论：
• [azath92] 正在开发一个重新排序Hacker News首页内容的工具，根据用户的兴趣定制推荐内容，并让用户能够控制推荐的透明度和编辑性，以应对黑箱推荐算法的问题。
• [kaspermarstal] 开发了Excel扩展Cellm，允许用户通过单元格公式调用大语言模型(LLM)来处理重复性任务，如文本分类，旨在让非技术人员也能利用AI自动化工作。
• [bennyg] 创建了Stoodious学习平台，旨在为考试备考提供简洁有效的学习材料和练习题，解决了市场上的价格高和用户体验差的问题。
• [rorylaitila] 正在数字化编录美国 vintage 印刷广告，利用OpenAI视觉技术提取图像中的实体数据，并计划通过出售原画或复制品来支持项目。
• [mkw5053] 开发了一个开源的LLM代理，旨在简化在应用中添加LLM功能的过程，避免将API密钥暴露在客户端代码中，类似于Stripe、Auth0等服务的模式。
• [muragekibicho] 正在制作一个介绍椭圆曲线算术的视频，视频中将用C语言编写一个比特币钱包暴力破解器，以激发程序员的兴趣。
• [samwillis] 正在开发Tanstack DB，一个新的客户端存储解决方案，支持事务、乐观状态和跨集合的实时查询，旨在与任何同步引擎配合使用。
• [matty22] 正在记录和绘制全球可公开访问的彩色玻璃窗，目标是让旅行者能够方便地找到这些艺术品的位置。
• [piker] 正在改进Tritium，一个法律IDE，增加对密码保护文档的解锁支持和OCR功能，并提升文字处理器的性能和跨平台拼写检查功能。
• [rcy] 正在开发一个专为儿童设计的社交和学习平台，家长可以监控聊天，儿童可以参与编程工作坊和各种创意活动，旨在创造一个安全和积极的在线环境。
• [tombert] 分享了自己在失业期间通过攻读硕士学位打发时间，并成功获得计算机科学硕士学位(MS)的经历。

争议焦点：
• 各个项目的实用性和创新性受到不同程度的讨论，如Tornyol无人机与传统方法的对比，以及LLM工具在非技术人员中的应用潜力。
• [marginalia_nu] 提到了代码优化中的性能问题，指出实际应用中出现的意外挑战，这可能引发关于基准测试与实际性能差异的进一步讨论。

整体来看，这些讨论展示了不同开发者在各自项目中面临的挑战和解决方案，并涵盖了从技术细节到市场需求的广泛主题。

• [piker] 正在改进Tritium，一个法律IDE，增加对密码保护文档的解锁支持和OCR功能，并提升文字处理器的性能和跨平台拼写检查功能。
• [rcy] 正在开发一个专为儿童设计的社交和学习平台，家长可以监控聊天，儿童可以参与编程工作坊和各种创意活动，旨在创造一个安全和积极的在线环境。
• [tombert] 分享了自己在失业期间通过攻读硕士学位打发时间，并成功获得计算机科学硕士学位(MS)的经历。

争议焦点：
• 各个项目的实用性和创新性受到不同程度的讨论，如Tornyol无人机与传统方法的对比，以及LLM工具在非技术人员中的应用潜力。
• [marginalia_nu] 提到了代码优化中的性能问题，指出实际应用中出现的意外挑战，这可能引发关于基准测试与实际性能差异的进一步讨论。

整体来看，这些讨论展示了不同开发者在各自项目中面临的挑战和解决方案，并涵盖了从技术细节到市场需求的广泛主题。

data.title: Dumb Pipe
data.author: udev4096
data.article_summary: "Dumb pipe" 是一种简化设备间直接连接的工具，能够在2023年复杂的网络环境中穿透NAT，保持设备连接稳定。用户只需在两台计算机上运行一个命令即可建立连接并传输数据，无需账户或配置。该工具基于Iroh Rust库，使用QUIC协议，支持多路复用和加密。对于无法直接连接的情况，它通过中继节点传输数据。用户还可以利用Iroh的附加功能如pubsub和数据同步，但这些会使管道不再“简单”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过不同工具和方法实现计算机之间的通信和文件传输

不同观点：
• **使用SSH和socat进行加密传输**：[remram]提出可以通过SSH和socat或mkfifo工具实现加密的数据流传输，并提供了具体的命令示例。该方案可以通过中继服务器进行传输，适用于防火墙或NAT后的目标。
• **对“智能”产品的批评**：[44za12]认为，许多被称为“ dumb ”（简单）的产品实际上非常智能，因为它们只专注于基本功能而不进行额外的数据收集或广告推送。他希望通信工具能像管道一样简单直接。
• **文件传输工具的分享**：[smusamashah]分享了一个包含浏览器和CLI工具的列表，用于在不同设备之间传输文件，并希望获取更多类似工具。
• **USB直接通信的疑问**：[Aardwolf]质疑为什么不能通过USB电缆直接在两台电脑之间进行通信和文件传输，特别是对于USB-C接口，同时提到Android设备与PC之间的通信相对容易。
• **对Iroh系统中节点发现和解析的批评**：[kiitos]认为Iroh系统在节点发现和解析方面没有详细说明，虽然概念类似于DNS，但实际操作中存在困难，且作者没有给出明确的解决方案。
• **秘密短语共享的复杂性**：[Alifatisk]提到通过Iroh分享长秘密短语的过程繁琐，质疑是否有更简单的方法在设备之间共享此类信息。

补充讨论：
• **隧道解决方案的缺陷和需求**：[zackmorris]认为大多数隧道解决方案存在缺陷，并提出了一个检查清单来评估这些缺陷。他呼吁提供一个更全面的解决方案。
• **与Tailscale的比较**：[Liftyee]提到Iroh和Tailscale有相似的需求，质疑两者之间是否有重复的实现，并希望有现成的低级库来处理NAT等问题。
• **Iroh技术的赞赏与推荐**：[ilovefood]高度赞赏Iroh技术，并提到在Web3峰会上的相关工作坊，提供了代码和 slides 的链接。
• **隧道工具的资源分享**：[behrlich]提供了一个关于隧道工具的资源列表链接，供有兴趣的人参考。
• **SSH管道的实现**：[qudat]提到在pico.sh使用SSH构建了类似的管道传输工具，并提供了链接。
• **游戏实时网络的适用性**：[darzu]质疑Iroh技术是否适用于游戏中的实时网络，特别是对于需要低延迟和高带宽的UDP通信。
• **PWNAT工具的推荐**：[bob1029]推荐了pwnat工具，认为它避免了中间服务器的需求，尽管不完全覆盖所有使用场景。
• **基于Iroh的隧道管理工具**：[CGamesPlay]提到自己开发了一个基于Iroh的隧道管理CLI工具，支持TCP、UDP和UNIX socket的端口转发，并提供了链接。

争议焦点：
• **Iroh系统中节点发现和解析的实现细节不足**：[kiitos]认为Iroh在节点发现和解析方面缺乏详细的解决方案，而这正是P2P网络中的关键问题。
• **不同隧道解决方案的缺陷和需求**：[zackmorris]和其他用户讨论了各种隧道解决方案的不足之处，并希望找到一个能够解决所有问题的“终极”解决方案。

44701555.article_content:
Connect A to B. Send Data.
In 2023 it's hard to connect two devices directly. Dumb pipe punches through NATs, using on-the-fly node identifiers. It even keeps your machines connected as network conditions change.
What you actually
do
with that connection is up to you.
A unix pipe between computers
$ curl -sL https://www.dumbpipe.dev/install.sh | sh
get
dumbpipe
with a single command on two computers, connect them & pipe data from one machine to the other. No accounts. No configuration.
Receiver
$ ./dumbpipe listen
using secret key 23ryys7pgvjrr57pcrvyivdrhvqyykg2tv3leou5grm66xfd7zzq
Listening. To connect, use:
./dumbpipe connect nodeecsxraxjtqtneathgplh6d5nb2rsnxpfulmkec2rvhwv3hh6m4rdgaibamaeqwjaegplgayaycueiom6wmbqcjqaibavg5hiaaaaaaaaaaabaau7wmbq
Sender
echo
"hello"
| ./dumbpipe connect nodeecsxraxjtqtneathgplh6d5nb2rsnxpfulmkec2rvhwv3hh6m4rdgaibamaeqwjaegplgayaycueiom6wmbqcjqaibavg5hiaaaaaaaaaaabaau7wmbq
This will work, regardless of where the two machines are. Dumb pipe finds a way.
Put a dumb pipe in your app
Dumb pipes are Iroh Connections. The
dumbpipe
tool is a
200-line wrapper
around the
iroh
rust crate. You can use the iroh Endpoint to create a connection to use as a dumb pipe in your own app.
Iroh Endpoint Docs
QUIC & Dumb
These dumb pipes use QUIC over a magic socket. It may be dumb, but it still has all the features of a full QUIC connection: UDP-based, stream-multiplexing and encrypted. Besides using the multiplexed streams you can also use multiple connections each with their own ALPN.
Sometimes you gotta relay
For somewhere around 10-20% of connections, it's simply not possible to connect two devices directly. For those cases, we use a meshed network of relay nodes to pack up UDP traffic & send it over HTTP. Sounds silly, but it works. And the magic socket handles all this under the hood.
relay docs
Your own Network
The team behind number0 runs the default relay network, which has a capped bandwidth. High-throughput, authenticated relays are now available through
n0des
!
Need more?
Need pubsub? Data transfer? Sync? All of these are opt-in addons from
iroh
. But if you add these things, the pipe is no longer dumb. You decide how to feel about that.

data.title: Beyond Mouse and Keyboard
data.author: tambourine_man
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了将Blender的全功能引入平板设备的计划，以使其3D技术更易访问。目标设备包括Apple iPad、Microsoft Surface等。项目将通过适应平台特定范式，并提供任务导向的用户界面，以降低信息密度。初期将专注于Apple iPad Pro和Apple Pencil，之后扩展到Android及其他图形平板。目标用户包括需要笔设备进行绘画、雕刻、2D动画的艺术家，以及主要使用平板设备的用户。

平板UX的挑战包括单窗口工作流、较小的屏幕空间、无键盘鼠标、多输入接口、有限的处理能力和电池，以及孤立的文件系统。输入方法上，支持键盘和触控板配件，也适用于图形平板。

目前的模型展示了Blender在iPad上的界面和交互设计，包括对象操作和雕刻功能。开发目标是为平板设备设计自定义应用模板，同时改进桌面版的可用性，如快速收藏编辑器、快捷键辅助覆盖等。某些功能将专为平板和其他触控设备设计，如多点触控事件和手势处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于新闻文章中提到的某个话题（链接内容），参与者们进行了深入讨论，主要围绕技术变革对劳动力市场的影响、自动化与就业的关系以及对未来的预期。

不同观点：
• 观点一：技术变革和自动化将导致大规模失业。一些参与者认为，随着人工智能和自动化技术的进步，很多工作将被机器取代，尤其是重复性劳动和低技能工作，这将导致大量失业和社会不平等的加剧。他们引用了历史上的工业革命和近年来的自动化趋势作为例子，强调技术进步常常带来短期和长期的就业冲击。

• 观点二：技术变革会创造新的就业机会。另一部分人认为，虽然自动化会取代某些岗位，但它也会创造新的工作机会，特别是在技术开发、维护和新的服务行业。他们指出，历史上每次技术变革最终都带来了更多的就业机会，并提高了整体生活水平，因此对未来持乐观态度。有参与者举例，互联网和IT行业的兴起就是技术进步创造新就业的典型案例。

• 观点三：关注劳动力再培训和教育。一些讨论者提出，应对技术变革的关键在于教育和再培训，让劳动力能够适应新的工作环境和技能需求。他们建议政府和企业应加大对职业教育和终身学习的投资，以减少技术进步带来的负面影响。有人提到，北欧一些国家在这方面的成功经验值得借鉴。

• 观点四：对社会不平等的影响。一部分人关注技术变革可能加剧社会不平等，认为自动化可能使得资本所有者和高技能劳动者受益，而低技能劳动者则可能面临失业和收入下降的风险。他们呼吁政策制定者关注这一问题，并通过税收政策和社会保障措施来缓解不平等。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于技术进步是否必然导致大规模失业。一部分人认为历史会重演，技术最终会带来更多就业，而另一部分人则担心这次的技术变革（如AI）可能不同于以往，会导致更严重的失业问题。

• 有参与者提到，自动化和人工智能的发展还面临伦理和法律问题，如隐私、安全和责任归属等，这些问题也需要在讨论技术对就业影响时一并考虑。

• 还有人指出，全球化和经济结构变化也是影响就业的重要因素，不能单纯将就业市场的变化归因于技术进步，需要综合考虑多种因素的共同作用。

总体来看，讨论的核心在于技术进步对就业市场的双重影响，以及如何通过社会和政策手段来应对这一趋势。

44683131.article_content:
Beyond Mouse & Keyboard
July 24th, 2025
Branches
,
General Development
Dalai Felinto
Hjalti playing with the sculpting mockup.
Multi-touch interfaces like tablets have been common for years, but only recently thanks to increased processing power, have they started to serve as primary computing devices. To support Blender’s mission of making 3D technology accessible to everyone, it’s important to fully embrace these platforms.
Some of these devices include Apple iPad, Microsoft Surface, Huawei MatePad, and the Wacom MovinkPad, among others.
The idea is to bring the full power of Blender to these devices. This requires adapting to platform-specific paradigms, but also to offer more task-oriented user interfaces with reduced information density. This will be achieved by extending existing input methods, and improving workspaces and application templates, running on top of a regular Blender build.
The initial platform where this idea will be tested is the Apple iPad Pro with Apple Pencil, followed by Android and other graphic tablets in the future.
While standalone tablets are the primary target, the core design principles apply across all platforms. This means that any UI/UX improvements will immediately benefit regular tablet users, even as Blender is being ported to run natively on the targeted devices.
Design Overview
This is a breakdown of product design considerations taken into account when thinking about “what is Blender on a tablet”.
Audience – Who is it for?
The audience is “Blender users”. There is no distinction between desktop or tablet users, the same way mouse/keyboard and graphic tablet users are treated equally. Therefore, there is no specific intention of simplifying or tailoring Blender to appeal to an audience that might not be familiar with Blender or 3D.
The intention is to make Blender fully accessible for users working with those devices, for example:
Artists that need a pen-device for specialized tasks (painting, sculpting, 2D animation).
Artists that have tablets as their main device.
Artists that need Blender on-the-go.
While the ultimate goal is a complete Blender experience, the initial focus will be on basic object manipulation and sculpting. These will be followed by Grease Pencil and
storyboarding
, which are slightly more advanced as they require animation tools.
Tablet UX Challenges
Working on a standalone tablet comes with its own set of software and hardware limitations, such as:
Single, full-screen window workflow.
Relatively small screen real estate.
No keyboard/mouse (out of the box, use should be optional).
Multi-input interface (touch + pen).
Limited processing power and battery.
Siloed file system.
Input Methods
Some tablets can be paired with a keyboard and trackpad accessory, in which case they should provide the same experience as working on a desktop.
Similarly, the reverse also applies: working on a desktop paired with a graphics tablet (e.g., Wacom Cintiq) should offer the same benefits as working on a standalone tablet.
Mockups
Here are a few exploratory mockups showing how the UI and the interaction could look like on iPad.
They will change in the future
, but are presented as a snapshot of the initial direction the team is taking.
The current mockups try to convey how Blender could adapt to run in a “single area”, with temporary context made available through floating regions.
While this partially contrasts with the
non-overlapping
design paradigm, this is a good compromise between providing sufficient workspace and quick access to essential editors.
Object Manipulation
This mockup illustrates kit-bashing making use of an asset library.
While not a typical day-to-day scenario, this demonstrates the power of being able to view files prepared on the desktop while on the go.
This demo shows:
Custom application template.
Wheel menu window overlay (Ctrl/Cmd, Shift, Alt, Quick Favorites).
Sidebar tabs use icons.
Quick access to the Outliner and Properties Editor in the 3D Viewport.
Sculpting
This mockup explores the concept of single-window mesh sculpting.
Interactive mockup
.
In this demo, you can additionally see:
Menus collapsed by default.
Helper overlay with curated shortcuts.
Tool panel, moved from the sidebar tab into a floating pop-up.
Tool Settings header has been removed:
Tool-specific settings are shown in the floating Tool panel.
Mode settings/options moved to the sidebar.
Additional design explorations are available at
projects.blender.org
.
Development
The goal is to implement new core features in Blender while designing a custom
application template
tailored for devices like the iPad.
Many of the usability improvements will also benefit the desktop version of Blender. For example:
Quick Favorites editor.
Helper overlay with curated shortcuts.
Icon support for sidebar tabs.
Togglable sidebar tabs (already in Blender 5.0 alpha).
Some features will be specific to tablets and other touch devices:
Multi-touch events and gestures.
Handling multiple active ed

不同观点：
• 观点一：技术变革和自动化将导致大规模失业。一些参与者认为，随着人工智能和自动化技术的进步，很多工作将被机器取代，尤其是重复性劳动和低技能工作，这将导致大量失业和社会不平等的加剧。他们引用了历史上的工业革命和近年来的自动化趋势作为例子，强调技术进步常常带来短期和长期的就业冲击。

• 观点二：技术变革会创造新的就业机会。另一部分人认为，虽然自动化会取代某些岗位，但它也会创造新的工作机会，特别是在技术开发、维护和新的服务行业。他们指出，历史上每次技术变革最终都带来了更多的就业机会，并提高了整体生活水平，因此对未来持乐观态度。有参与者举例，互联网和IT行业的兴起就是技术进步创造新就业的典型案例。

• 观点三：关注劳动力再培训和教育。一些讨论者提出，应对技术变革的关键在于教育和再培训，让劳动力能够适应新的工作环境和技能需求。他们建议政府和企业应加大对职业教育和终身学习的投资，以减少技术进步带来的负面影响。有人提到，北欧一些国家在这方面的成功经验值得借鉴。

• 观点四：对社会不平等的影响。一部分人关注技术变革可能加剧社会不平等，认为自动化可能使得资本所有者和高技能劳动者受益，而低技能劳动者则可能面临失业和收入下降的风险。他们呼吁政策制定者关注这一问题，并通过税收政策和社会保障措施来缓解不平等。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于技术进步是否必然导致大规模失业。一部分人认为历史会重演，技术最终会带来更多就业，而另一部分人则担心这次的技术变革（如AI）可能不同于以往，会导致更严重的失业问题。

• 还有人指出，全球化和经济结构变化也是影响就业的重要因素，不能单纯将就业市场的变化归因于技术进步，需要综合考虑多种因素的共同作用。

不同观点：
• [jakedata] 提供汤姆·莱勒本人的声明，明确表示他已永久放弃对其所有作品的版权，并允许公众自由使用其歌词和音乐，无需支付或担心法律诉讼。他还特别提到翻译权和改编权也包括在内。

• [philodeon] 提到莱勒的讣告过时，指出莱勒曾为国家安全局工作的事实未在最新报道中更新，并讽刺了媒体在发布过时信息方面的失误。

• [dekhn] 分享了个人经历，讲述了莱勒的音乐和数学课程对其成长的影响，表达了对莱勒幽默感和教学能力的赞赏。

• [walterbell] 提供了一系列关于莱勒的新闻讨论链接，显示了莱勒相关话题在不同时间点的讨论热度。

• [lb1lf] 表达了对莱勒作品的持久影响力的赞赏，并提到莱勒的逝世对其个人情感的冲击，同时提及其他同期逝世的文化人物。

• [sitkack] 引用了莱勒在1981年的采访，反映了他对生活的幽默态度和对加州的调侃。

• [dosinga] 引用了莱勒歌词中的一句话，认为其依然具有现实意义，并结合现代技术（如矩阵乘法）进行对比。

• [jgrahamc] 分享了莱勒在演出中讲述的一个小故事，并将其与产品决策过程中的“富人病”隐喻联系起来。

• [HarHarVeryFunny] 表达了对莱勒逝世的哀悼，并提到通过DECtalk听到莱勒的歌曲，分享了类似的黑暗幽默作品。

• [ohjeez] 提到莱勒对国家安全局的恶作剧故事，并提供了一个链接供读者了解更多细节。

• [nmca] 认为人工智能安全社区未充分关注莱勒关于该主题的杰作，并提供了一个视频链接。

• [dlcarrier] 表达了对莱勒长寿的惊讶，提到直到阅读相关文章前，从未见过彩色照片的莱勒。

• [mark_l_watson] 分享了个人及家庭对莱勒音乐的喜爱，特别是某些歌词对他们的特殊意义。

• [ComplexSystems] 提到了莱勒的歌曲《Werner Von Braun》，并提供了一个视频链接以供欣赏。

• 莱勒的幽默和讽刺作品在其逝世后仍然具有广泛的影响力和讨论价值。
• 莱勒不仅作为音乐人和讽刺作家受到赞誉，他的数学课程也受到了学生的喜爱和怀念。
• 莱勒放弃版权、将作品释放至公共领域的决定引发了关于版权和艺术作品自由使用的讨论。
• 莱勒的个人背景，包括他在国家安全局的工作经历，成为讨论的另一焦点，显示了公众对他多重身份的兴趣。

[Outliers] Katharine Graham: The Washington Post
When Katharine Graham took over the Washington Post in 1963, she was a shy socialite who’d never run anything. By retirement, she’d taken down a president, ended the most violent strike in a generation, and built one of the best-performing companies in American history.
Graham had no training, no experience, not even confidence. Just a newspaper bleeding money and a government that expected her to fall in line.
Public Release: July 29.
Members have
access now
.
Join us
.
Coming Soon:
Apple Podcasts | Spotify |
Transcript
When her editors brought her stolen classified documents, her lawyers begged her not to publish. They said it would destroy the company. She published them anyway. Nixon came after her, attacking her with the full force of the executive. Then Watergate. For nearly a year she was ridiculed and isolated while pursuing the story that would eventually bring down the president.
Graham proved that you can grow into a job that initially seems impossible and no amount of training can substitute for having the right values and the courage to act on them.
This episode is for informational purposes only
and is full of practical lessons I learned reading her memoir,
Personal History
and watching
Becoming Katharine Graham.
10
Lessons
from Katharine Graham
1. The Velvet Hammer:
Katharine never raised her voice. She never pounded tables. Never tried to out-masculine the men. She stayed soft-spoken while becoming as hard as steel. Nixon’s administration learned too late: the quiet ones hit hardest. Competence whispers, it doesn’t shout.
2. Values Beat Analysis:
The Pentagon Papers decision arrived during Katharine’s Georgetown dinner party. The Washington Post had just gone public two days earlier. Everything was at stake. Publishing classified documents meant likely criminal charges, losing television licenses, and destroying the IPO. Her lawyers said it was financial suicide. Her editors said not publishing was journalistic suicide. She remembered her father’s principle: newspapers exist to tell the truth. “
Let’s publish,
” she said, then hung up.
3. Don’t Care What They Think:
Nine months into Watergate, the Post was still the only major paper digging. Everyone thought they were wrong. The Chicago Tribune and other major media outlets openly mocked them. The administration went after the Post, causing the stock to crash 45%. The President of the United States targeted their TV licenses. The Post’s lawyers begged them to stop. Katharine kept going. The rest is history.
4. Bounce, Don’t Break:
The pressmen destroyed equipment, beat a foreman unconscious, and walked out. They expected Katharine to fold. After all, what choice did she have if she wanted to print papers? But Katharine had been preparing for months, training replacements and arranging backup presses. When picketers blocked trucks, she hired helicopters. While they marched outside, she worked the mailroom floor. It lasted 139 days before she won.
5. Find a Teacher:
Warren Buffett bought 5% of her company without asking. The board panicked. Katharine ignored them. She met Buffett herself, saw his genius, and made him her professor. He’d bring 20 annual reports to board meetings, teaching her line by line. She was humble enough to know she didn’t have all the answers and smart enough to know who to listen to.
6. Freedom With Transparency:
Ben Bradlee got total editorial freedom. The only rule? No surprises. He could fight presidents, spend millions, and pursue any story in the public interest. She never questioned his judgment. He never blindsided her. Result: Pentagon Papers, Watergate, 18 Pulitzers. Maximum freedom requires maximum transparency.
7. Step Off the Edge:
“What I essentially did was to put one foot in front of the other, shut my eyes and step off the edge.”
That’s how Katharine described taking over the Post. There was no grand strategy, no master plan. Just the next step. Eight years later, she was staring down presidents. You’ll never feel qualified for what matters. Step anyway.
8. Decades Over Quarters:
Wall Street wanted quarterly earnings and exciting acquisitions. Katharine wanted to create a company that would last. She went against their wishes, buying back stock when it was cheap (and it was very uncommon to do so), and acquiring a “boring” education company, Kaplan, which would eventually generate more revenue than the newspaper. She was a public company but operated it like a private one.
9. Keep the Main Thing the Main Thing:
Katharine faced constant pressure to choose: profits or principles, safety or stories, shareholders or journalism. The Pentagon Papers could have killed the IPO. Watergate bled millions in legal fees and threatened their television licenses. The pressmen’s strike threatened operations. Every crisis offered an excuse to compromise but she never took it. data.title: High-performance RISC-V processors: UltraRISC UR-DP1000, Zhihe A210, SpacemIT K3
data.author: fork-bomber
data.article_summary:
2025年将推出几款高性能RISC-V处理器，包括UltraRISC UR-DP1000、Zhihe A210和SpacemIT K3。UR-DP1000是一款八核64位RISC-V SoC，具备8个64位UR-CP100核心，主频达2.0 GHz，支持硬件虚拟化和RISC-V RV64 ISA H扩展，内存支持UDIMM DDR4-3200 ECC，最高64GB。网络和I/O接口丰富，包括PCIe 4.0和千兆网卡。Titan mini-ITX主板支持多种操作系统，计划于2026年Q4获得Linux主线支持，目前可预订，售价279美元。

Zhihe A210采用8核64位RISC-V CPU，支持统一计算架构（UCA），兼容RVA23规范，具备12 TOPS AI推理能力，适用于边缘服务器、视频编解码和加密等应用。目前已完成制造和内部测试，开发者可申请测试。

SpacemIT K3基于X100核心，支持RVA23 64位RISC-V，具备2.5 TOPS AI计算能力，主频达2.5GHz，支持RISC-V向量和加密扩展，适用于服务器级别应用，具备虚拟化和RAS功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RISC-V设备的性能、可用性及其与现有技术的比较

不同观点：
• fidotron认为，目前讨论的性能不如即将推出的真实RVA23设备的可用性重要。他质疑在设备正式推出前对半导体性能的乐观预期，并指出如果RVA23设备推出，将为性能设立基准，减少频繁重建的需求。

• geerlingguy指出，RISC-V在高性能方面有所进步，但在效率（每瓦性能）上仍需追赶Intel/AMD和Arm。他认为，目前RISC-V的性能接近于Raspberry Pi的水平。

• bjoli对厂商强调“专有扩展”表示不满，认为虽然厂商有权这样做，但这让他失去兴趣。

• deivid表达了对更快RISC-V单板计算机（SBC）的期待，并提到目前在VisionFive 2上进行Rust编译的速度让他感到困扰。

Some high-performance RISC-V processors are in the pipeline for the rest of the year 2025, namely UltraRISC UR-DP1000, Zhihe A210, and SpacemIT K3. We currently have limited information about each of those processors, but let’s see what information we can gather from the web, mostly as a result of the recent RISC-V Summit in China.
UltraRISC UR-DP1000  – Octa-core 64-bit RISC-V SoC
UR-DP1000 Block Diagram
The first SoC is the UR-DP1000 octa-core from
UltraRISC
(the website loads slowly, and I could not find anything about the UR-DP1000 there). It will be used in
Shenzhen Milk-V Technology’s Titan mini-ITX motherboard
, and Sipeed also posted
the slide above on X
.
Preliminary UR-RP1000 specifications:
CPU
8x 64-bit RISC-V UR-CP100 “
RV64GCBHX
” cores up to 2.0 GHz
Two 4x core cluster design with 4MB L3 cache each, and a total of 16MB cache.
SPECCPU2006 single-core INT @ 10.4/GHz; single-core FP @ 12/GHz
Fully RVA22 compliant, and “Compliant with RVA23 excluding V extension.”
Supports Hardware Virtualization, RISC-V RV64 ISA H(v1.0) Extension
Memory – UDIMM DDR4-3200 ECC memory support, up to 64GB
Networking – GMAC
High-speed expansion interfaces
1x PCIe 4.0 x16
2x PCIe 4.0 x4
Other I/Os – 1x QSPI, 2x SPI, 4x I2C, 4x UART, 40x GPIO, eSPI/LPC
Titan motherboard renderings
Many features will have to rely on the PCIe interfaces, and for instance, the Titan motherboard also offers four USB 3.0 ports, which must have been implemented through a PCIe to USB 3.0 bridge.  It will have UEFI firmware with support for ACPI, CPPC, SMBIOS, and the ability to boot RISC-V ISO images from Debian, Ubuntu, openEuler, Centos, Deepin, Feroda Remix, and other operating systems. The plan is also to have mainline Linux support by Q4 2026.
The Titan mini-ITX motherboard is still under development, but
can be booked now for $5
, and purchased for $279 once it becomes available in about three months. It’s not sure whether that price includes
the $50 discount promised or not
.
Zhihe A210
We have even less information about the Zhihe Computing A210, with all details below coming from a
post in Chinese on Zhihu social network
.
The A210 will also have a big brother called the A600…
Zhihe A210 key features:
CPU
8-core 64-bit RISC-V CPU
Unified Computing Architecture (UCA) with unified memory and unified operators for enhanced computational efficiency.
Fully compatible with the RVA23 Profile
Up to 12 TOPS (INT8) AI inference capability (they don’t seem to use a separate NPU)
Memory – DDR memory optimized with large-capacity storage to support Mixture of Experts (MoE) model architectures (e.g., DeepSeek).
Target applications include edge server scenarios for video encoding/decoding, encryption/decryption, AI large model inference, and data storage. They want to offer a cost-effective solution that competes against traditional GPU/GPGPU solutions using HBM.
The post on Zhihu appears to focus a lot on RVA23 Profile compliance with support for all 81 mandatory and optional extensions, including Hypervisor, Vector, BF16, CFI, and Sv57. The processor also supports 123 official RISC-V extensions, covering AME, AIA, CoVE, Smmtt, QoS, IOMMU, and RERI. They also highlight the advantages of the RISC-V Vector (RVV) Extension, either matching (or close to it) or outperforming Intel and Arm instructions for tasks like video encoding/decoding, OpenSSL, LLMs, and CRC computation.
I could not find any of the I/Os used by the processor, but it’s probably safe to assume it has a few PCIe Gen4 lanes like the UR-DP1000 above. Zhihe says they’ve completed the fabrication and internal testing, and sample testing applications are open to developers, partners, and customers. The company does not appear to have a website as of July 22, 2025.
SpacemIT K3
SpacemIT
is already a known entity in the RISC-V space thanks to
K1 and M1 octa-core processors
found in products like the
Orange Pi R2S
board,
Banana Pi BPI-CM6 system-on-module
,
Muse Pi Pro SBC
, and others. They must have mentioned the K3 at the RISC-V Summit, but I can’t find any posts about it, and all we know is that the K3 is
based on X100 cores
, for which we
have more details
, and are also found in the
Vital Stone V100 server SoC
.
X100 core specifications:
RVA23 64-bit RISC-V processor
2.5 TOPS @ INT8 AI computing power compliant with RISC-V IME extension
RISC-V Vector 1.0 standard, providing 256-bit vector computing bandwidth
Supports RISC-V Vector Crypto extension
Performance
2.5GHz @ 12nm
9.0 SPECint2006/GHz with SpacemIT LLVM Compiler
7.7 CoreMarks/MHz with SpacemIT LLVM Compiler
Microarchitecture
12-stage four-issue out-of-order execution
Multi-core, multi-cluster processor, up to 64 cores
Support intra-cluster and inter-cluster consistency
Supports virtualization
Supports RISC-V Hypervisor extension
Supports AIA specification
Supports forming a complete virtualization system in combination with IOMMU
Other Server-level Features
Support RAS features and RISC-V standard RERI information reporting
